world: A cool, dry world smaller than most, locked to its star. The twilight band is khaki steppe, levelled in places into parade grounds and barrack grids laid out by Continuity to the metre; the scorched brown day side is a live-fire range, and the white night side holds the munitions stores, dug into the ice. There are a few shallow lakes in the twilight and no forest.
from_space: A khaki twilight ring with grey barrack grids, between a scorched brown face and a white night side. The barracks show as hard white rectangles in perfect rows, and the day side flickers now and then with range fire.
moons: Two moons: a large grey rock cratered all over as a gunnery range, and a smaller cratered rock carrying the range's tracking station.
people: 300 million hands, most in uniform: Pacifier regiments in barracks, with their training staff and depot crews.
story: The Pacifiers who keep order on the sector's city-worlds are barracked here in the twilight, out of sight, and rotated so the cities never see the same faces twice. They drill on the scorched day side and store munitions in the frozen night. Off duty they may not visit the cities.

world: A warm ocean world of ordinary size, with long chains of green volcanic islands, white beaches and coral shallows, and almost no ice. The island towns are old and grown, built round their harbours.
from_space: Deep blue sea with green island chains and pale beaches, under scattered white cloud. By night the harbour towns are bright beads along the chains.
moons: One small moon, a pale cratered rock.
people: About 40 million islanders in harbour towns; once a year a few thousand of them meet on the council raft.
story: A warm sea scattered with islands whose councils meet once a year on a raft lashed together from every island's boats. Alma has twice offered to buy the coastline for an executive resort; both times the raft voted no, and the second vote was close.

world: A warm dry world of sand seas and bare rock, with breathable air and a few low ranges. Water comes up only in the oasis basins where the three families' wells are, and the towns are old walled oases grown round them, with palm groves and date gardens inside the walls.
from_space: Sand-gold seas of dunes with dark green oasis spots in the basins, under a clear sky. At night a few small lights at the oases.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock.
people: 600,000 settlers in the oasis towns, most of them working for one of the three water families.
story: Three old families own every water well and sell it by the litre to anyone landing. They have refused the Hand, the Collective and each other for ninety years.

world: A temperate world of ordinary size, a little under half ocean, with broad plains and old forest between low, worn mountains and small ice caps. The reading halls stand in planned towns on the plains, long white blocks in rows round the relay domes, and a relay dome stands on every hilltop so that each one can see the next. Cloud is light and clears over the plains.
from_space: By day, green forest and grey-brown plain beside a blue sea, studded with white relay domes that catch the sun along the ridges. By night the reading halls light up in even grids and the hills carry chains of small white dome lights. Its one moon glints with antenna fields.
moons: One moon, a small rock plated over with antenna fields and dish arrays that relay the sector's traffic; Praevisio's technicians live in sealed huts among the masts. No rings.
people: 2.5 billion hands, Staff grade: about two billion readers in the reading halls, the rest relay technicians, canteen and clinic staff. Almost all live in Praevisio's planned hall towns on the plains.
story: Praevisio's listening world: every signal sent in the sector passes through its relays, and two billion hands work as readers, checking what the machine flags. They are told the job is temporary.
history: Akousma was settled as a farm world during the Settlement, and its plains still grow most of what its readers eat. The Republic put a postal relay on its highest ridge. At the Receivership the Tabularium took the relay over to carry its census traffic, and through the Hand's first century it built domes on hilltop after hilltop until every signal in the sector passed through them. When the Tabularium became Praevisio in R.132, the relays began to feed the machine, and the machine began to flag. A flag checked by a person was worth more to the Board than one that was not, so Praevisio hired readers by the hundred million and built the long white halls to seat them. Every reader signs on for a temporary post. Mantis Doran, born here in R.168, started reading at fourteen and matched the machine on every check for eleven years; in R.193 Pythia Kallos took him out of the halls and into the Auditors. Since then the halls have been emptying, a row at a time, as the machine's own checks improve, and the readers who are wrong go first. In R.212 two billion are still at their desks.

world: A barren world, 5,000 km in radius, with almost no air and no water. Its plains are bone-white gypsum, low and worn, cut by quarry benches that step down hundreds of metres; the old craters are half filled with white dust. The quarry towns are sealed domes laid out in rows along the quarry edges.
from_space: Bone white with long grey quarry scars and pale craters, under the faintest whitish haze of blown dust. At night rows of small dome lights along the quarry edges.
moons: None.
people: 80 million hands, Indentured quarry crews, in sealed dome towns along the quarry edges.
story: A barren world of gypsum quarries worked from sealed domes. Its dust coats everything white and gets through every seal, and the hands call their lungs the company's eighth quarry.

world: A warm ocean world a little smaller than most, nine-tenths sea, broken by thousands of sheer-sided stone mesas that rise flat-topped from shallow water. The rock grows nothing. The towns are packed onto the mesa tops, old and unplanned, and cable ferries swing between them on lines strung from cliff to cliff.
from_space: Turquoise shallows and deeper blue sea dotted with tan stone islands, each flat-topped and sharp-edged, under light cloud. By night the mesa towns are tight bright dots, with faint lines of ferry lights between the nearest.
moons: None.
people: 17 million mesa-dwellers in old towns on the mesa tops; the ferry guilds' families hold the cable stations and eat best.
resources: fish, cable-ferry trade; imports food and medicine
story: Towns sit on the tops of flat stone mesas rising from a warm sea, linked by cable ferries. The rock grows nothing, so every meal and every medicine is shipped in, and whoever controls the ferries controls the price of bread.

world: An old foundry world, 6,200 km in radius, with no open water left: dry brown basins where its seas were, worn mountains, slag hills and quarry scars. Heavy smog hangs over the foundry cities, which grew in the basins round the old shorelines without much plan.
from_space: Brown-grey under yellow smog, with dark slag scars; at night the foundry cities glow orange round the dry basins. Beside it the factory moon is dark, with a few old lamps still burning.
moons: One moon, an industrial moon covered by the arms factory abandoned when the Republic went bankrupt; its plating is dark and most of its windows are unlit. No rings.
people: 600 million free foundry workers and their families, in the basin cities.
story: An old foundry world with no open water left, whose moon holds an arms factory abandoned when the Republic went bankrupt. It still holds stock, and every year three buyers bid for it and the foundry councils sell a little more.

world: A warm airless world a little smaller than most, with no water and no weather. Its lowlands are brick-red bauxite plains opened into hundreds of stepped pits, with pale tan highlands and old craters between them. The towns are planned domes clustered on the pit rims and joined by sealed roads, and red mud from the washing plants is banked against their walls.
from_space: Brick red and pale tan, pocked with craters and scarred by huge stepped pits. By night the domed pit towns ring the pits with clusters of light, joined by thin lines of road.
moons: None.
people: 700 million hands, Indentured, in domed pit towns on the rims; most work the pits and the washing plants, the rest the smelters that turn the ore into aluminium.
story: Lode's alum and bauxite pits on an airless rock. The red mud from the mines piles against the town domes and gets into the air locks and the lungs, and the hands joke they were born rust-coloured.

world: A dry world, 6,200 km in radius, with no seas: tan grassland and ochre desert on the uplands, and forest only along the green river valleys that wind down to salt flats. The towns crowd the valleys, each grown by a different people, and the speech changes from one valley to the next.
from_space: Tan and ochre with winding green river valleys. At night strings of town lights follow the rivers.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 90 million free settlers of a dozen peoples, crowded along the river valleys.
story: A dry world settled by a dozen peoples who never agreed on one language, crowded along its green rivers. Its parliament still translates every speech six times, which slows everything down and keeps the peace.

world: A hot, dry world of blinding white salt flats cut by red canyons, with a few shallow brine pans where the old seas were. The towns are in the canyons, out of the glare. The Margrave's town is the oldest and the only one with a plan, built round the square where the refusals are read.
from_space: Blinding white pans veined with rust-red canyons under a hard sun. At night a few small lights show deep in the canyons.
moons: Three moons: a cratered grey rock, a small captured lump and a moon of cream frozen plains. None is worked.
people: 200,000 settlers in canyon towns, under the Margrave and the town assembly.
story: A white salt-pan world under one hard sun, held by the Margrave family under a deed older than the Receivership. Lode has offered to buy it seven times; each refusal is read aloud in the square on its anniversary.

world: A warm ocean world, 6,000 km in radius, nine-tenths sea. Its islands were low bare reef rock until Alma greened them; now they are flat and bright green, ringed by white beaches and turquoise lagoons, with no mountains at all. The studio towns are planned compounds behind the beaches, out of camera shot.
from_space: Turquoise sea dotted with bright green islands and white beach rims, under light fair-weather cloud. At night small neat grids of studio lights.
moons: None.
people: 8 million hands, mostly Staff grade media crews, plus each season's cast of lottery winners from the inner worlds.
story: Alma greened these islands from bare reef rock to film its broadcasts: smiling hands on white beaches, sold to the galaxy as ordinary life. The actors are hands from the inner worlds who won a lottery. Few ask what happens to them when the season ends.

world: A large temperate gas giant with soft bands and a deep rain layer, where water cloud forms every afternoon and pours down into the haze. One town hangs in that layer under a clear balloon several kilometres across, its terraces of fruit trees and herb beds watered by the daily rain through vents in the envelope. Nothing else is built on the planet.
from_space: Sky-blue and white bands with soft, smeared edges and pale rain cloud along them, and no great storms. At night one faint point of light shows in the southern temperate band: the town.
moons: None.
people: 1 million settlers in the balloon town, the children and grandchildren of the Alma clinic staff who founded it.
resources: fruit, herbs and medicine grown under the balloon, fuel gas
story: Founded a century ago by Alma clinic staff who walked out together and built a town under a clear balloon in the rain layer of a giant, where it rains every afternoon. Their grandchildren still smile too much, and nobody here will talk about why their grandparents left.

world: A cold tundra world, 5,600 km in radius, mostly dry frozen ground with a few ice-locked seas, low worn hills and little snowfall. Deep natural cave systems run under the tundra, widened by Praevisio into vaults, and every settlement is underground; the surface holds only cave mouths, vent stacks and landing pads.
from_space: White and grey-blue tundra pocked with dark cave mouths, with a few frozen grey seas. At night almost dark, with small cold lights at the cave mouths.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock, and a smaller cream frozen-plains moon. No rings.
people: 300,000 hands, mostly vault technicians and their supervisors, living in the caves beside the archives.
story: Praevisio keeps every forecast it has ever made in vaults under the tundra, the wrong ones included, and its technicians live down there with them. Nobody has ever been allowed to read the wrong ones. The Unruled have tried to burn it four times. The caves are too cold to burn.

world: A gas giant about 70,000 km in radius, banded cream and slate blue, with one vast white storm that has sat at the same latitude for four centuries. Its eye is calm and wide, and the university's halls float there in a great cluster, open to anyone who can fly in.
from_space: Cream and slate-blue bands round one vast white storm. At night the eye of the storm glows with the lights of the halls.
moons: None.
people: 3.5 billion free people in the storm-eye halls, a third of them students.
story: A free university older than the Hand, its halls afloat in the calm eye of a storm that has not moved in four centuries, open to anyone who can reach it. Praevisio has offered three times to buy its library, and the faculty has voted no by a narrower margin each time.

world: A cold, mid-sized world of frozen hills and small grey seas, with snow on everything above the valley floors. In the lowlands the families have run buried heat lines under the fields, so the pastures there are green-grey and stone-walled, a little more of them every few years. The farms and villages are small and scattered, grown over centuries with no plan.
from_space: White uplands round green-grey lowland pastures, under long bands of cloud. At night a thin scatter of farm lights shows in the valleys.
moons: None.
people: 5 million settlers on family farms in the warmed valleys.
story: A cold world of shepherds and stone farms, far from the lane, where each family runs buried heat lines under its fields and thaws one more pasture every few years. Praevisio flags it every year as 'low data', which means nobody has told it anything worth knowing.

world: A barren world, 6,000 km in radius, locked to its star, with almost no water. The day face is white-hot desert and mountain, covered by Praevisio's solar fields; the night face is dark cold rock where broken Proxies wait in scrap yards. The repair halls run along the pale sand twilight band in tight planned grids.
from_space: A pale sand twilight band laid out in white factory grids, between a white-hot day face glinting with solar fields and a dark night face. The grids are lit day and night.
moons: Two moons: an industrial moon of plated sheds and open pits, and a cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 300 million hands, mostly repair technicians, with the Tranche crews who ship the Proxies in and out.
story: Praevisio's repair works: broken Proxies come back from every front to be rebuilt in the twilight halls and sent out again. Solar fields cover the day side; scrap waits in the night side's cold yards. The Tranches who ship them have painted a word on the factory wall so often that Continuity no longer bothers to clean it off.

world: A scorched world of mountains and burned plains where the forests once stood. The peat under the ash still smoulders in long seams that glow dull red, and the smoke hangs in a grey-brown haze. There is no open water left. The scavengers live in the sealed ruins of the old towns, half buried in ash.
from_space: Black and grey scorched land under brown smoke, with dull red seams that glow on the night side and a few faint lights in the ruins.
moons: None.
people: 500,000 scavengers in sealed ruins, masked whenever they go outside.
story: A crop blight nobody could stop burned its forests two centuries before the Receivership, and the peat beneath still smoulders. Scavengers live in sealed ruins and wear masks outdoors; Alma's broadcasts show those ruins as proof of what happens to a world nobody manages.

world: A hot, dry world somewhat smaller than most, with no open water at all. Tan sand deserts cover both hemispheres, and a broad belt of black lava fields crosses the middle, broken by open pits where molten rock lies at the surface. The smelter crews work the pit edges and sleep in shielded towns strung along the line where the black gives way to sand; the towns grew wherever a crew found a ridge to shelter behind, and none of them has a straight street.
from_space: By day a tan desert with a black belt of lava across its waist, the pits in it glowing red under a thin yellow-brown dust haze. By night the pits burn like coals in a dark grate, and the towns are a faint, broken string of lights along the desert edge.
moons: None.
people: About 2 million smelters and their families, in shielded towns along the edge of the lava fields. The crews are free and work for themselves; Dust hauler crews bring raw ore down to the pits, and Lode's buyers wait in orbit for the ingots.
story: Free smelter crews work ore in the natural heat of open lava pits, cheap and lethal, and sleep in shielded towns at the desert's edge. The Dust call it the Kitchen. Lode buys the metal and asks no questions about the crews.

world: A volcanic world of ordinary size, with no sea and breathable air: black lava fields cover half of it, and between them grey-green ash forests grow on soil made of old ash. Grey plumes rise from the active vents, and the cracks in the newest fields still glow. The herb clans live in grown stilt towns above the ash flows and move them when a flow comes too close.
from_space: Black and grey-green, with glowing cracks under grey ash plumes. By night the cracks show orange and the stilt towns small warm clusters in the forests.
moons: None.
people: 5 million in herb-gathering clans, in stilt towns over the ash forests.
story: The bark of a tree that grows only in the ash between the lava fields goes into Alma's healing gel. Herb-gathering clans live in stilt towns above the ash flows and sell it, and the Growers keep asking them, politely, to stop.

world: A cool, dry world with no seas, of tan plains and low hills where grey forests are spreading. The trees grow back after fire faster than anywhere known, so each summer the settlers burn a district on purpose and the forest takes a little more of the plain. The towns are timber-built and grown, spaced along the firebreaks. Smoke drifts over the plains all summer.
from_space: Grey-green forest spreading over tan plains, smudged with brown smoke where the summer burns are lit. At night the burns glow red along their edges, and the towns are small scattered lights.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock.
people: 80 million settlers in timber towns along the firebreaks, led by burn-wardens chosen by lot.
story: The grey forests here grow back after fire faster than anywhere known, and each summer the settlers burn a district on purpose so the forest spreads a little further into the dry plains. Lode once tried to mine the ash for fertiliser; the settlers burned the survey camp too.

world: A grey-green gas giant, smaller than the great ones, with calm, even bands and little turbulence in its temperate layer. The workshop towns ride on hollow float-hulls in that layer, chained together by cable bridges, so a whole string of towns drifts as one along the wind. Each string runs a few hundred kilometres and carries forty or fifty towns.
from_space: Grey, olive and pale sage bands with one small pale storm in the southern belts. On the night side the town strings show as dotted lines of warm light lying along the bands.
moons: One small moon, a grey cratered rock, where the guild keeps a warehouse of finished boot kits for the broker.
people: 60 million workshop families in the floating towns, chained into strings across the temperate cloud layer; only the warehouse crews live on the moon.
resources: boot kits, synthetic leather, cheap goods
story: Workshop towns ride on hollow float-hulls, chained together by cable bridges so a whole string drifts as one. They make cheap boots in flat-pack kits; a broker sells them to Continuity's quartermasters, so half the Tranches march in boots made by people who hate them.

world: A bright azure gas giant about 52,000 km in radius, banded in light and deep blue, with a few small white storms. The guild cities float on vacuum cells in the calm upper cloud, each a dome on a broad deck, moored to its neighbours by cables so that the whole guild country forms one drifting lattice.
from_space: Bright blue bands with small white storms, crossed by a set of thin dark rings. At night the moored domes glow white in a long net of lights.
moons: No moons. A set of thin, sharp-edged dark rings, soot grey.
people: 850 million free citizens of the guild houses, all in the floating cities.
resources: luxury goods, fabric, jewellery, fuel gas
story: Its guild houses make jewellery and fine clothes for Hand executives in domed cities moored together above the blue, and are proud of never selling to anyone else. The Collective calls them the Board's tailors and has their order books.

world: A small, dull brown gas giant with few bands and almost no weather, which is the point. Its one town floats on its own fuel tanks just above the cloud tops, more tanks than houses, and when a strange ship arrives it floods the tanks and sinks out of sight until the ship leaves.
from_space: Dusty brown bands with a few grey patches, and nothing else: no rings, no moons, no lights to speak of. On a good night the town shows one dim light, and on a bad night none.
moons: None.
people: 20,000 Runners and families in one floating town.
story: A dull world on purpose: a Runner haven that looks like nothing from orbit. Its one town floats on its own fuel tanks, more tanks than houses, and when a strange ship arrives it floods them and sinks below the cloud tops until the ship leaves.

world: A small barren world, 3,000 km in radius, with almost no air: flat dull brown plains, low worn ridges and many old craters. The claimants' pressure camps are scattered at random across it, each fenced and armed at the edge of its own deed.
from_space: Dull brown and cratered by day. At night a few dozen tiny pinpricks of light, far apart.
moons: None.
people: 20,000 claimants and their guards, in pressure camps scattered across the surface.
story: A barren rock the Board once sold, twenty times over, to twenty buyers. Claimants' pressure camps still dot the surface, each with its own deed and its own guns.

world: A temperate world that has turned to desert: low hills and broad plains where the rainforest stood, now bare tan subsoil and grey stands of dead trunks. Rain still falls in season but runs straight off the hard ground in gullies, and there are no seas, only a few muddy lakes. The towns are old timber towns grown along the dry river beds, many of their houses built from the dead forest.
from_space: Pale tan plains with grey ghost-forests in wide patches, cut by the straight brown tracks of the old logging roads. At night scattered town lights follow the dry rivers.
moons: Three moons: a cratered grey rock, a dark ice-rock and a small captured lump. None is worked.
people: 10 million settlers in timber towns, every one of whom can tell you how long the lawsuit has run.
story: Lode strip-logged the rainforest for pit props and left, and the rains washed the soil away within a single lifetime. The settlers sued in the Republic's last court and are still waiting for a ruling.

world: A hot, arid world a little smaller than most: low desert hills, wide red mud plains that crack in the dry season and turn to slurry when the rare rains come, and limestone caves where the salts are dug. There are no seas and almost no ice. The broker families' compounds stand on the hills above the plains, with the holding yards and landing fields beside them.
from_space: Rust-red flats streaked with pale dry riverbeds, the hills a darker brick, under a dusty orange haze. By night a dozen bright compounds and the lit landing fields where the Hand's labour ships come down.
moons: None.
people: About 5 million, ruled by a dozen broker families; most live in mud-brick towns on the plains and owe one of those families something.
resources: people sold as contract labour, clay, cave salts
story: The mud-plain families sell their own debtors to Hand labour brokers, a head at a time, and call it settling accounts. It is a free world that trades in the one thing the Hand would otherwise have to breed.

world: A cold city-world larger than most, mostly land: the city fills the lowlands and valleys in silver grids, while dark conifer forest and snowy mountains survive on the high ground between them. Summers are short, winters long and the ice caps big. The city is planned round its cold stores, rows of windowless vaults the size of districts, dug into the mountain flanks where the cold is free.
from_space: A silver city grid with dark forests and snowy peaks under grey cloud. By night bright grids in the valleys, and long dark rectangles on the mountain flanks where the vaults show no light at all.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock.
people: 30 billion people, most of them working in the cold stores, the freight yards that feed them and the cartels' offices.
story: Thirty billion people behind walls of cold storage. Its freezing cartels will store anything for anyone, and Repossessors bring them debtors in sealed crates to keep until the price is right.
history: Bastide was settled during the Settlement for its forests and its cold. Under the Republic its families dug the first vaults into the mountains to keep fish and grain, and during the Last Famine they stored the relief grain Parliament bought on credit. They were paid late, and only in part, and they learned from it: store anything for anyone, and take payment first. By the Receivership the vault families had become freezing cartels, and the Hand found them more useful free than acquired. It pays them to keep its reserves and whatever else it would rather not hold itself. The cartels ask nothing about what goes in. Repossessors bring them debtors in sealed crates to keep cold until the price of the debt is right, and the cartels bill by the day. On the stacked decks of Dongyu, Praevisio tells children that Runners sell children to the freezing cartels here, and the boy called Nine believes it. Nobody on Bastide has ever said what the deepest vaults hold. The city has grown to thirty billion people round them, and still answers to the cartels.

world: A hot, wet world a little larger than most, with warm shallow seas over about half of it and low worn hills on the land. Jungle grows from coast to coast, broken by square red clearings where Lode has burned it off and planted the crop. Rain falls every afternoon, and the cloud rarely clears over the interior. The plantation towns are planned rows of barracks and drying sheds at the edge of each clearing, and they move inland as the clearings do.
from_space: By day, dark green jungle cut by a spreading patchwork of rust-red clearings, under heavy white afternoon cloud and blue-green shallows. At night the lights run in straight rows along the clearing edges and the freight strips, with black jungle all round them.
moons: One moon, a small grey cratered rock with no use; the field crews time the end of each shift by its rising.
people: 50 million hands, nearly all Indentured field and clearing crews, in planned barrack towns along the edges of the plantations; a few thousand Staff overseers live in the port town by the main freight strip.
story: Lode's plantation holding: red soil, hot jungle, and one crop every hundred days, shipped ahead of schedule. Workers who miss quota are reassigned to clearing new jungle, which is why the plantation keeps growing.

world: A cold world, 5,900 km in radius, of white uplands and long river valleys, with cold seas covering under a third of it. Pine forest fills the valleys, and the rivers run for thousands of kilometres and freeze at their heads every winter. In the settled valleys the councils have spread black dust on the fields and drilled greenhouse vents, so the valley floors are a little warmer every decade. The river towns are old and grown along the banks.
from_space: White uplands and dark green valleys threaded with silver rivers, under broken cloud, with dark patches of dust field on the valley floors. At night strings of town lights along the rivers.
moons: None.
people: 40 million free settlers, fishing and timber families in river towns, each valley run by its elected council.
story: A cold river world settled by refugees from the Republic's last famine, who have spent a century warming its valleys with black-dust fields and greenhouse vents. Its fishermen still set an empty place at every feast for those who never arrived.
history: Bela Voda was founded during the Last Famine, about pre-R 60 to pre-R 40, by refugees from the crowded worlds where the harvests had failed. Not every ship reached it; several that set out were never heard of again, and the fishermen still set an empty place at every feast for those who never arrived. The settlers found a cold world with fish in every river and pine in every valley, and for a century and a half they lived as the cold allowed. They were already a free world of river councils when the Receivership came in R.0, and the receivers never found a reason to want them. About a century ago, with the warm valleys full, the councils began to warm the rest: black-dust fields to drink the sun, greenhouse vents drilled into the valley floors, a little more each year and paid for by nobody but themselves. The valleys are greener now than any settler's grandparent remembers. The rivers carry the timber and the fish downstream to the ports, and the councils still meet on the river banks.

world: A calm gas giant of soft blue and cream bands, seven broad ones and one small tan storm, with gentle winds at the breathable layer. The banking houses' garden cities float there on vacuum cells, terraced like hillsides, with vineyards on the upper decks and the counting houses below.
from_space: Soft blue and cream bands, almost still, dotted with white terraced cities and their green vineyard decks. By night the cities glow warm gold on the dark cloud. Two bright ice moons.
moons: Two moons, both smooth bright ice, cracked and almost craterless: the larger close in, the smaller further out. No rings.
people: 6 billion free citizens in the floating garden cities: bankers, clerks, vintners and the households that serve them.
story: A rich free world whose banking houses sit in terraced garden cities held up by vacuum cells, with vineyards on the upper decks. The banks hold a great deal of Hand debt, which makes it the one free world the Board cannot afford to foreclose, and the bankers know it to the decimal.

world: A lilac gas giant, calm and banded, that nobody lives on. Its one moon is a warm living world of long slow rivers, vineyard slopes and small seas, with a boatyard town at every river bend, all of them old and grown.
from_space: Lilac and cream bands with a soft violet storm. Beside the giant, a green moon threaded with silver rivers.
moons: One living moon of long rivers, vineyard slopes and small seas, home to all the settlers.
people: About 30 million settlers on the moon, in river villages and boatyard towns; half the villages hide someone the Hand is looking for.
resources: wine, small boats, river trade, all from the moon
story: A river moon of vineyards and boatyards under a lilac giant. Its people take in whoever arrives, and half its villages now hide someone the Hand is looking for.

world: A rocky world of dark basalt plains and low mountains under a thick, pale yellow ammonia air that nobody can breathe. Its people live under great glass domes, hundreds of them, each the size of a city and each built by its own council on the flattest rock it could find. The glass is made locally and replaced pane by pane, so every dome is a patchwork of old clear glass and new.
from_space: Dark rock under a pale yellow haze, with the domes glittering in the sun like scattered glass beads. At night each dome glows as its own round pool of light.
moons: None.
people: 600 million dome dwellers. Each dome is a self-governing town that votes every year on how many children it can afford air for, and posts the result on the dome wall.
story: Nobody can breathe its ammonia air, so its people live under great glass domes. Each dome votes every year on how many children it can afford air for, and the result is posted on the dome wall.

world: A cold upland world smaller than most, mostly ice and snowfield, with a widening belt of pale green pasture spreading out of the ice from the equator where the shepherds' moots have warmed it field by field. The highlands are high and bare, and small seas lie in the warmed lowlands. The villages are stone-built and unplanned, scattered along the edge of the green and moving uphill as it spreads.
from_space: White ice with a widening band of pale green round the middle, drifting cloud and a few dark blue lakes and seas. By night only faint village lights along the green belt.
moons: None.
people: 3 million shepherds and their families in stone villages along the green belt; the weather service keeps a station and a flock at every moot.
story: The shepherds' moots are warming this ice world a field at a time, and the upland pastures green a little further every decade. Its weather service predicts the lane storms better than Praevisio does, using sheep, barometers and old songs. Praevisio has offered to buy the method three times and been sold a ram.

world: A hot tropical world of ordinary size, almost all sea: jungle islands, white beaches and broad reefs in a shallow turquoise sea, with no ice. Afternoon thunderstorms build over the islands. The hotel towns are old and grown along the beaches, each family's resort a tangle of terraces and piers added over generations.
from_space: Bright turquoise shallows and emerald islands on deep blue, with tall white storm cloud. By night every beach is a ribbon of warm light.
moons: Three moons: a smooth white ice moon the hotels sell as the view, a cratered grey rock, and a small captured lump.
people: 1 billion people, mostly hotel staff and their families in the beach towns; on any night a few million guests, from Executives on leave to Runner captains.
story: Reef resorts run by old hotel families who serve anyone who pays, including Executives on leave and Runner captains. Alma has offered to buy every hotel; the families raise their prices each time.
history: Belmare's hotels are older than the Receivership. Under the Republic, members of Parliament spent their recesses here, a short jump from the capital, and the first hotel families grew rich on their bills, paid, like everything Parliament paid, on credit. When the Republic defaulted in pre-R 1 the families were left holding years of unpaid bills, and they made the rule they have kept ever since: everyone pays at the door, and anyone who pays is a guest. Under the Hand the guests changed and the rule did not. Executives on leave came, then Board children and Lode captains, and from the R.170s Runner captains, who pay in cash and tip better. Belmare keeps no register and asks nobody for a name or a number; the Board's own Executives, who want their leave unrecorded, are why the Hand allows it. Alma has offered to buy every hotel on the world at least once a decade since its pill went on sale in R.88, because a holiday is what Alma sells and Belmare sells one without the pill: real sun, real sea, and guests who go home sorry it ended. The families raise their prices each time Alma offers. Since R.201 both sides have used the beaches to meet. Collective cell leaders and Hand officers have sat at neighbouring tables, and the staff serve both and remember nothing. In R.212 that is worth more to the Runners than the reefs.

world: A warm living world of plains, forest and coast, landscaped by Alma over sixty years. The jungle has been clipped into tidy gardens round the resorts, and long white beaches run along the coasts. The resorts and staff towns are strictly planned, set in neat rows along the shore and in garden rings inland.
from_space: Green and gold land, blue seas and white resort coasts under light cloud, with three pale moons beside it. At night neat strings of light trace the coasts.
moons: Three pale moons: two smooth ice moons, then a frozen-plains moon, cream and pale.
people: 80 million hands, mostly service staff in the resorts and staff towns, with a few hundred thousand Mordant and Continuity executives as guests.
story: Alma landscaped this jungle into tidy gardens over sixty years, as a rest world for Mordant and Continuity executives under three pale moons. Guests may buy a server's Birth Debt over dinner as a tip, so the staff compete for tables.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, about seventy percent land, its forests circling a chain of bright, shallow inland seas over white sand and gem gravel. The outer ocean is small. The divers' camps are planned dredge stations on the inland shores, with the spoil heaped in pale banks along them.
from_space: Green forest round bright turquoise inland seas, pale spoil banks along their shores, light cloud. At night a few lit dredge stations ring the seas.
moons: None.
people: 8 million hands, Contract divers and dredge crews, in planned camps along the inland seas; Lode's sorting houses, where every stone is weighed, stand at the largest.
story: Gem dredgers work the inland seas for the stones Executives wear. A diver who finds a stone above a set size gets one day off; most never see it.

world: A frigid world a little smaller than most, mostly frozen sea with low tundra islands and very little relief. For most of the year the sea ice joins the islands; in the short summer it opens into dark water. The island villages are small and unplanned, and the ice road between them is the only real street.
from_space: White and pale blue, almost featureless, the islands only a little greyer than the ice round them. By night the villages are faint scattered sparks, and in market season a thin line of lights runs across the ice between them.
moons: Two moons: a small moon of smooth white ice and a cratered grey rock.
people: About 450,000 settlers in island villages; in market season nearly all of them are out on the ice.
story: When the sea freezes, the ice road joins the islands and the year's only market opens on it for ninety days. Anything still on the ice when it melts belongs to the sea, by custom, so the market's last day is a frantic auction.

world: The larger half of the double planet, temperate and green: about sixty percent land, rolling forest country set with thousands of lakes, and low old mountains. The golden-barked trees Lode logs grow on the uplands. The foresters live in small planned camps along the logging roads and at the river landings where the timber is rafted down.
from_space: Green and gold forest freckled with lakes under light cloud, with the brown-green marsh of Bina Minor hanging close beside it. At night almost nothing: a few camp lights on the rivers.
moons: A twin planet, Bina Minor, a warm marsh world smaller than itself, hanging close. No other moons and no rings.
people: 2.4 million hands, Contract foresters and raft crews, in planned logging camps; the sawmills and the timber port stand on the largest lake.
story: The larger half of a double planet. Its golden timber panels every Board office in the Hand, and its foresters cannot afford a chair made of it.

world: The smaller half of the double planet, warm and flat: mud flats, reed marsh and slow brown rivers wandering across low plains to shallow seas, with hardly a hill on it. The farms are mud-flat paddies and fish ponds along the rivers, worked from Lode's planned farm villages on the few dry banks.
from_space: Brown and olive green under warm haze, laced with slow brown rivers, with the green-gold face of Bina Major looming huge beside it.
moons: A twin planet, Bina Major, a forest and lake world bigger than itself, hanging close enough to fill a wide patch of the sky; then three small moons: two captured lumps of dark rock close in, and a small grey cratered rock further out.
people: 3.2 million hands, Contract farmers, in planned farm villages on the river banks; the water-rights office in the largest village is the only stone building on the planet.
story: The smaller half of the double planet. Mud-flat farms feed Bina Major's foresters, and the two worlds have quarrelled over water rights since before the Hand.

world: A cold world slowly warming, mid-sized, with ice caps still covering most of both hemispheres. Along the equator the ice has drawn back from low rolling land, and birch forest creeps over it in pale belts broken by grey meltwater lakes. The villages are small and unplanned, strung along the rivers where the pulp mills can use the water.
from_space: White caps reaching far toward the middle, a broad band of pale green birch at the equator, and grey thawing lakes scattered through it, under light cloud. At night a thin scatter of village lights along the rivers, nothing more.
moons: None.
people: 5 million villagers in river villages along the birch belt, most of them paper makers, foresters and beekeepers.
story: Forest villagers make paper the old way, from birch pulp, and seed the thaw line with new birch every spring as the ice draws back. The Collective buys the paper because Praevisio cannot read what was never digital.

world: A mid-sized desert world of pale sand and low worn hills, with grey dead lake beds where the acid rain gathers and dries. The seeded sky never cleared: a yellow-white cloud deck lies over much of it, and the rain from it eats stone. The chemists live in a few planned dome towns, every building coated in wax, with the distilling sheds in rows beside them.
from_space: Sickly yellow-white cloud over pale sand, with the dead lake beds showing grey through the gaps. At night a few small dome towns glow faint and yellow under the cloud.
moons: None.
people: 50,000 dome chemists and their families in a few wax-coated dome towns.
story: A Republic firm seeded this sky to make rain, and the rain came down acid. Nothing lives outside the domes. Every building is coated in wax renewed monthly; the oldest house has four thousand coats, and the chemists distil the rain and sell acid to every refinery in reach.
history: Bitterwell was a dry but breathable world when its first settlers came during the Settlement, with salt lakes and thin grass in the basins. Around pre-R 125 the Republic paid a contractor, with borrowed money, to seed its sky and bring rain. The rain came, and it came down acid. It killed the grass, ate the lakes down to grey beds and stripped the paint off every house. The families who stayed built domes and learned to coat their walls in wax; the oldest house still standing has been rewaxed every month since then, four thousand coats. The contractor's own chemists were the first to see that the rain could be sold. They stayed, formed a guild and began distilling it into industrial acids, and the guild has run the world ever since. The Republic never repaired the sky, and the Receivership inherited the failure without wanting it. Under the Hand, Bitterwell stayed free because nobody else wanted to live under that rain, and Lode became its great buyer: every refinery in reach uses Bitterwell acid, at a price Lode sets. In R.212 about fifty thousand people live under the domes, and the rain still falls.

world: A small volcanic world of jagged black obsidian crags, still warm, with grey ash plains between them and thin vents glowing in the cracks. There is no water and no air worth breathing. The knappers' and moneychangers' houses are sealed and cut into the cliffs above the vents, grown up the crags over generations with no plan.
from_space: Glossy black crags and grey ash plains, cut by thin orange cracks that glow on the night side. The cliff houses show only as a few warm points high on the crags.
moons: One small moon of cratered grey rock, unused.
people: 500,000 knappers and Runner families in sealed cliff houses; the moneychangers among them keep every account on paper.
story: Obsidian crags, still warm, knapped by hand into blades and mirrors. The Runners' moneychangers live in sealed cliff houses above the vents and keep their accounts on paper: the one set of books nobody wants burned.

world: A toxic marsh world of black water and dead reed beds, low and flat, poisoned by a dead Republic chemical works. The one city stands on stilts over the poisoned delta, sprawling and grown ward by ward, its towers sealed against the air. The rest of the marsh is empty.
from_space: Black water and grey city sprawl along one delta, under yellow-grey haze. At night the delta is one bright crowded patch, and the rest of the world is dark.
moons: None.
people: 700 million marsh-city residents, packed into the stilt city on the delta.
story: A city on stilts over the poisoned marsh of a dead Republic chemical works, its towers sealed against the air. The Hand won't take it because the clean-up would cost more than the yield, and the residents know their poison is their armour.

world: A hot ash world, once forest, its plains fused to black glass in the Last War and its volcanoes woken by the bombardment. Lava still breaks through the glass in long cracks, and grey ash storms sweep the plains. The prospectors work from sealed crawler camps that roll across the glass, cracking it for metal seams. There is no surface water; every drop is shipped in.
from_space: Black glass plains split by orange cracks of lava, under grey ash storms. At night the cracks glow, and the crawler camps are tiny moving lights.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock, where the water tankers unload.
people: 18,000 prospectors in sealed crawler camps on the glass plains; few stay more than a few years.
story: A forest world burned in the Republic's last war, its plains fused to black glass and its volcanoes woken. Eighteen thousand prospectors crack the glass for metal seams from sealed crawler camps, and the water shipped in costs more than the metal.
history: Blackglass was a forest world before the Last War, settled in the Settlement and green from pole to pole. When a league of outer worlds tried to leave the Republic rather than share its debt, about pre-R 30, Parliament voted to keep them in by force and paid for the war on credit, with a navy Mordant built on account. The fighting reached Blackglass. The bombardment burned the forests, fused the plains to black glass and woke the volcanoes under them. Most of the people died or left, and by pre-R 12, when the war ended, nobody was left to rebuild. For generations it was a grave that nobody visited. Then prospectors found that the heat had driven metal into seams under the glass, gold among it. They came in sealed crawler camps, eighteen thousand of them now, cracking the glass for the seams and selling to anyone. The water shipped in costs more than the metal. Neither side holds the world: the camps are unaligned, and each looks after its own. Wreckage from the war still turns up under the glass, and the prospectors sell that too.

world: A hot, humid swamp world of ordinary size, of mud flats, rainforest and shallow brown seas, with low hills and heavy cloud nearly all the time. The swamp towns are built on mounds and stilts in the mud flats, unplanned, and the moon crew keeps its camp by the landing field.
from_space: Murky green-brown under constant grey cloud, the brown seas barely different from the mud. The moon beside it is one vast grey open pit, its terraced walls lit by work lamps.
moons: One moon, a single vast open pit cut in terraces and worked by the free crew; when buyers come, they flood it.
people: About 1 million: swamp settlers in the mud-flat towns, and a few thousand moon miners.
story: Its moon is one vast open pit, worked by a free crew that sells a rare heavy crystal. Twice the Hand has sent buyers. Twice the crew flooded the pit and waited in the swamp below until the buyers left.

world: A dry, windswept world smaller than most, with no open water: high tan plateaus, deep dry gullies, and dust plains where the managed climate once held lakes. The weather satellites used to steer rain onto the plateau farms; since they were smashed, the wind blows the soil away in long streaks. The pilgrims live in grown stone villages beside the grain stores on the plateaus.
from_space: Pale tan with long dust streaks and the dry beds of old lakes, under a thin ring of satellite wreckage. By night only a few dim lamp lights on the plateaus.
moons: Two small moons, both captured lumps, and a thin ring of wrecked weather satellites: fresh wreckage spread round the planet.
people: 400,000 Unwritten faithful in plateau villages round the grain stores.
story: Unwritten pilgrims came here to live without machines and smashed the world's weather satellites in their first year; the wreckage still circles the planet. The managed climate collapsed, and the harvests have failed three times since. They call it a test of faith.
history: Blind Eye was given a managed climate long before the pilgrims came: a ring of weather satellites steered rain onto its plateau farms, and the climate held only as long as they did. In the R.170s Unwritten pilgrims came to live without machines. In their first year they smashed the weather satellites, and the wreckage still circles the planet. The managed climate collapsed within a few seasons. The lakes dried, the wind took the soil, and the harvests have failed three times since. Wick was born here in R.187. In one of the failed years Sister Wake found her starving in a grain store and raised her as a daughter in the faith, and Wick grew up watching her neighbours go hungry for want of a machine that could tell them when it would rain. At nineteen she went to the Walkout yards to learn to fly, and Wake disowned her the day she flew. The pilgrims call every failure a test of faith. They still plant each spring, and fill the grain stores when they can.

world: A deep indigo gas giant with fourteen sharp bands and violent weather: six white storms at a time, strong shear where the belts meet, and a fast equatorial jet. The skimmer crews' hangar towns ride that jet round the planet, a lap every few days, and race the storm bands for bets.
from_space: Deep indigo and blue bands torn by white storm spots, inside a wide faint ring of ice dust that glows when the sun is behind the planet. By night a few small lights in the equatorial cloud, where the hangar towns ride.
moons: Dozens of small moons. The eight biggest, out from the planet: a small geysering ice moon inside the ring, which feeds it; five captured lumps of dark rock; and two dark ice-rocks further out. One ring: moon-fed ice dust, very wide and faint, sprayed by the geyser moon.
people: About 5,000 skimmer crew, pilots and mechanics with their families, in a few hangar towns riding the equatorial jet.
story: Its skimmer crews live in hangar towns that ride the equatorial jet round the planet, and race the storm bands for bets. The winners fly for the Runners, the losers fly for Lode.

world: A cold world about 5,000 km in radius, mostly land, of blue sand deserts, dark conifer forest and snow plains, with a few small frozen seas. The blue sand is a crushed mineral that blows into dunes across the high plains. The settlers live in sod-walled huts dug half into the ground at the forest edge, in scattered hamlets nobody planned. Winters are long and dry, and cloud is thin.
from_space: Blue deserts and white snow plains with dark green forest belts, small frozen seas and thin cloud. At night it is nearly dark, with a few dim sparks at the forest edges.
moons: None.
people: 8,000 settlers, most of them run from Hand debt, in sod-walled huts in scattered hamlets; nobody asks names.
story: Fewer than ten thousand people, most of them run from Hand debt, living in sod-walled huts dug half into the ground. They grind the blue sand into glass and sell it to anyone who doesn't ask where they came from.

world: A cool, green forest world of rolling uplands and old worn mountains, where forest covers almost all the land and silver lakes fill the glacial hollows. The settlers' towns are clearings in the forest, small and grown, each ringed by orchards and mushroom beds and run by its own forest council.
from_space: Deep green forest with silver lakes and grey-blue seas under broken cloud. At night the towns are small, soft clusters of light scattered through the dark forest.
moons: One pale moon of frozen plains, cream ice with a darker band.
people: 450 million settlers in forest towns, who plant two trees for every one they cut; Growers come to learn from them.
story: Forest settlers who never cut a tree without planting two. They sell food down the Trunk Line and buy nothing they can't repair. Growers come here to learn, and the forest families quietly teach them.

world: An amber-banded gas giant of hydrogen and ammonia storms, its belts crowded with small pale and brown ovals. The Brandt family lives on a single skimmer platform that rides just above the cloud tops on its own lift cells, tethered by the scoop cables it lowers into the cloud. The platform has been rebuilt piece by piece for nine generations, and looks it.
from_space: Honey amber with brown bands and pale storm ovals, inside a faint dust ring. Eleven small moons circle it; at night the platform is one tiny cluster of lights on the clouds.
moons: Eleven small moons, the eight largest drawn: innermost a small captured rock that orbits inside the ring and feeds it, next the largest, a smooth icy moon, and beyond them dark ice-rocks, cratered rocks and captured lumps. Ring: a faint dust ring fed by the innermost moon.
people: About 3,000 skimmer crew on the tethered platform, nearly all of them Brandts by birth or marriage.
story: An amber-banded giant whose clouds the Brandt family has skimmed for nine generations, living on a platform that lowers its scoops into the cloud tops on cables. Lode has offered to buy them out every year for forty years, and every year the offer is lower.

world: A temperate world of two large continents in a wide blue sea, one in each hemisphere. The northern continent has been opened by Lode's mines for a generation: open pits and spoil terraces cut into its hills, company towns laid out in grids beside them, its rivers running grey. The southern continent is grain country, wide fields and old villages that grew where they pleased, and its harbours on the strait face an empty ferry dock across the water.
from_space: Two green-brown continents in a blue sea, the northern one torn by grey-brown mine scars, the southern one patterned with golden fields. At night the north shows tight grids of company lights round the pits, and the south a soft scatter of village lights.
moons: None.
people: 30 million, about half of them Lode contractors in the northern mine towns; the rest are free farmers on the southern continent, who have not spoken to the north since the ferry stopped.
resources: ore in the north, grain in the south
story: Two continents, two fates: the northern one sold its ore rights to Lode a generation ago, the southern one refused. The ferry between them stopped running the year the mines opened, and families on both shores have not spoken since.

world: A temperate world of rolling plains and mixed forest, about half land, with two mid-sized oceans and low ranges between the grain belts. Lode laid it out as a farm-and-freight hub: depot towns sit every hundred kilometres along straight freight roads, each a grid of silos and sheds. The Locals have kept the grids and painted over the stencils. Summers are long and dry, winters mild.
from_space: Green forest and gold grain plains under light cloud, two blue oceans, and grey depot towns strung along the freight roads like beads. At night the depots show as evenly spaced points of light joined by faint lines.
moons: None.
people: 26 million people, most of them former Lode farm and depot hands, now organised by Local committees in the depot towns; a militia guards the main depot against the Continuity force massing two jumps away.
story: Once Lode's farm-and-freight hub. The Locals took the depots in one night and now feed four Collective worlds, while Continuity masses two jumps away.

world: A hot, airless world of dark mountain ranges with wide white salt flats between them. The breakers beach dead hulls on the flats in long rows and cut them up where they lie. The guild towns are sealed, sprawling yards along the edges of the flats, grown hull by hull from the ships they took apart.
from_space: White salt flats between black mountains, with the dark shapes of beached hulls lined up across them. At night cutting torches and yard lights spark along the edges of the flats.
moons: Seven small moons, in order outward: two captured lumps, a cratered grey rock, a third captured lump, a second cratered rock, and two more small rocks, one captured and one cratered. Ships waiting to be broken park beside the two inner ones.
people: 2 million ship breakers in the guild yards along the flats.
story: Ships from every side come here to die. Hulls are beached on the hot salt flats and cut up by breakers in cooled suits, and the metal is sold back to whoever is winning that year.

world: A hot, crowded city-world under thick, smoky air, with small brackish seas and no open country left. Engine halls and test stands cover the old industrial plains, their stacks feeding the brown haze, and the housing districts climb the low hills round them in a maze of streets rebuilt on top of itself for centuries. Breath masks are advised everywhere outdoors, and most people take the advice.
from_space: A brown haze over grey-brown sprawl and a few dark seas, the haze thick enough to blur the coastlines. At night the whole land glows orange through the smog, brightest over the engine halls.
moons: None.
people: 16 billion people, most of them engine-hall workers and their families, under the engine guild, which sells the same drives to the Hand, the Runners and the Collective.
story: The best hyperdrives outside Mordant's yards are built here in hot, smoky engine halls. The engine guild sells to the Hand, the Runners and the Collective, and swears the drives are identical.

world: A small volcanic world with a thin crust, its plains crusted mustard-yellow with sulphur round a great field of geysers. Grey lava flats and low cones surround the field, and vents glow orange wherever the crust has cracked. The sealed mining towns stand in a planned ring round the geyser field, each the same distance from its centre.
from_space: Mustard yellow and grey, with a pale plume of steam over the great field and orange vent glow in the cracks. At night the ring of towns shows as a circle of lights round the dark field.
moons: One moon of cratered grey rock, unused.
people: 800,000 miners and their families in a ring of sealed towns round the geyser field.
story: Sulphur miners live in a ring of sealed towns around the great geyser field. The geysers blow on a schedule the towns set their clocks by; nobody trusts any other time, and a late geyser empties the streets.

world: A large, temperate world of endless flat plains, with shallow seas over less than a third of it and only low hills. Grain belts run across the continents in wide gold and green bands. The farm towns are many and evenly spread, laid out by the cooperative on a regular plan, and seven billion people live among the fields.
from_space: Gold and green bands under thin cloud, with blue seas at the edges. At night an even field of farm-town lights covers every continent.
moons: One moon of cratered grey rock.
people: 7 billion farmers in a planet-wide cooperative, living in towns spread evenly across the plains.
story: Seven billion farmers feed half the sector. The planetary grain cooperative sells to Lode at a fixed price every year, and the Hand buys rather than takes, as long as the price stays low enough.

world: A dusty green and grey gas giant on the Trunk Line, with eight bands, moderate turbulence and one small brown storm. In its upper cloud float the gate's old tender hulls, refloated by heating gas in their fuel tanks, where the salvagers live; they drift in loose rafts near the equator, under the wreck.
from_space: Dusty green, olive and grey bands, circled by a glittering ring of wreckage, the toll gate's girders and plates catching the sun in sparks. A few dim lights in the cloud by night where the hulls float.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock beyond the wreck. One ring: fresh wreckage, the remains of Lode's toll gate, still tumbling and spreading.
people: 800,000 in refloated tender hulls in the clouds: salvagers, Unruled crews and Runners, and the families that came with them.
resources: free passage, gate salvage, fuel gas
story: The Unruled blew up Lode's toll gate here; its wreck still tumbles round the giant as a glittering ring. The salvagers live in the gate's old tender hulls, kept afloat in the clouds by heating gas in their fuel tanks. Ships have passed the Trunk Line here free ever since, and Lode has sworn to rebuild the gate.
history: Lode built its toll gate here when it finished the Trunk Line in R.68, where the lane meets the Salt Lane, so that no ship could go down either without paying. For more than a century it was one of Lode's surest earners. Its tender crews lived in hulls moored to the gate and scrubbed the freighters that queued to pay. Jackdaw was born among them, a Lode hand, in R.178, and spent eighteen years watching the toll counter tick over in the gate hall. At nineteen he came off the pill, sick on stolen remedy in a tender hold, and took his name from the bird that steals shiny things. Then, with the friends he had made in the holds, he blew the gate up, in about R.197. Its wreck still tumbles round the giant as a glittering ring. The tender hulls fell into the cloud and were refloated by heating gas in their fuel tanks, and the salvagers live in them still, stripping the wreck for parts. Ships have passed the Trunk Line here free ever since, and the Unruled hold it with the Runners, with nobody in charge. Lode has sworn to rebuild the gate, and in R.212 it has the war as its reason.

world: A dun gas giant wrapped in a dense layer of ochre dust haze above its cloud tops, with muted bands and one small storm. The refit rafts drift in the haze: open platforms of scaffolding and paint gantries, each big enough to take a freighter, with the painters' bunkhouses lashed to their edges. They are moved, rebuilt and renamed as often as the ships they work on.
from_space: Dun and pale green bands blurred under ochre haze, with a faint white ice ring fed by its one geyser moon. At night a scatter of small work lights drifts in the haze where the rafts are.
moons: One moon, a small icy geyser moon whose spray feeds a faint, wide white ring.
people: About 1 million painters and crews on the rafts, with Runners always passing through; every hull that leaves has a new registry.
resources: ship refits, new registries, fuel gas
story: A gas giant on the Trunk Line where crews repaint and rename ships on open rafts drifting in the ochre haze. Every hull that leaves has a new registry, and the painters swear they have never seen it before.

world: A crowded world, 7,000 km in radius, whose old forests have been grown over by one continuous city, leaving dark mountain spines and a few forest belts. Shallow seas cover a fifth of it. The city was never planned: districts climbed the valleys and spilled over the passes, each with its own street pattern.
from_space: Grey-green sprawl broken by dark mountain spines and small grey seas. At night it is lit end to end, brightest along the valleys.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock and a dark ice-rock with bright crater splashes. No rings.
people: 40 billion free citizens, crowded into the world-city from the coasts to the mountain spines.
story: A crowded forest world grown into one city, which sells itself to the Hand in bad decades and buys itself back in good ones. The paperwork is kept ready in both directions.

world: A temperate world smaller than most, about a third land: rainforest on the lowland coasts, with wide plains above it terraced into coffee fields, and small ice caps. Cloud lies over the forest and clears over the terraces. The co-op farms are grown, small hamlets along the terrace edges.
from_space: Green forest and blue sea, with brown terraced plains inland. By night only faint scattered lights on the terraces.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock.
people: 800,000 free farmers in the coffee co-ops.
story: Coffee co-ops grow beans on terraced plains above the rainforest. Sacks of Cafetal beans are the one currency every Runner port in the sector accepts without argument.

world: A dun-brown gas giant of middling size, with broad, slow bands and one rust-coloured storm. Nobody lives in its clouds. The herding clans live on its living moon, a world of grassy uplands and deep valleys under fast white cloud, where stone hearth-houses stand alone on the high pastures and the valleys flood every spring.
from_space: A dun and buff banded giant with one rust-coloured storm, and beside it a green-brown moon streaked with fast white cloud. On the moon's night side only scattered hearth lights show on the uplands.
moons: Two moons: the living highland moon of the herding clans, green-brown, with grassy uplands and narrow valley lakes; and a small grey cratered rock farther out.
people: 9 million herders on the living moon, in clan steadings scattered across the uplands; the valley towns hold markets and little else.
story: Highland herders on the giant's green moon keep the Republic's old land titles framed above every hearth: the last legal papers the Hand never got round to voiding. Continuity posted a garrison here once and withdrew it as a poor use of contract hours.

world: A rocky world somewhat larger than most, its land crusted from coast to coast with trading towers, clearing houses and docks, and its shrunken seas walled into harbours. The trading floor itself covers most of one continent under a single roof. Every district is planned, and the old mountains have been cut down to building platforms.
from_space: Grey-brown under a crust of towers and docks, with dark harbour seas and the vast flat roof of the trading floor; lit end to end by night. One large grey moon.
moons: One large moon, a grey cratered rock with dark plains, left bare. No rings.
people: 65 billion hands, mostly Staff grade brokers and clerks, in planned tower districts; the floor runners who carry the bundles between desks are children, as they have always been.
story: The debt exchange. Birth Debts are bought, bundled into tranches and sold to Continuity on a trading floor the size of a continent. A hand's whole life can change owners three times in one afternoon.
history: Cambium lies at the crossing of two lanes beside the capital, and it was a market town in the Settlement: grain first, then, under the Republic, the bonds the Republic sold to pay for its famine and its war, bought by the creditors who would one day own it. At the Receivership the Board's own office took the exchange and renamed it. When the receivers divided the Republic's debt among its citizens, from R.0 to R.30, the accounts were cleared here, and after R.31, when Alma began billing every birth to the newborn, Birth Debts became the floor's main stock. Continuity buys them by the bundle and turns each tranche into a regiment, so the Tranches begin here; Stabilis raises its regiments from debts bought on this floor. Lucrio Vance ran bundles between the brokers as a boy, his lane number inked on his hand, and in R.178 he bought his own Birth Debt in a bundle rated likely to default. Cassia Ravilla's debt changed owners here three times before she could walk. In R.174, a Staff clerk of nineteen, she found a tranche sold to Continuity twice; the floor manager was restructured within the week, and the Chair's office hired her. The floor has never closed. In R.212 the war has every desk buying.

world: A hot volcanic world of black lava plains, grey ash fields and glowing vent lines, with ranges of dark rock. Mordant built its foundries straight over the vents, which heat them for free. The yard towns are planned blocks of barracks and shops round each foundry, joined by covered roads across the ash.
from_space: Black rock and grey ash cracked with glowing orange lava under thin brown smoke. On the night side the yard lights spread across the plains in planned blocks between the red glow of the vents, and the nearer moon is ringed with dry docks.
moons: Two moons: the nearer an industrial moon ringed with dry docks, where drone frames and assault shuttles are finished and launched; the farther a dark cratered rock.
people: 1 billion hands, most of them Indentured yard lifers signed to the yard for life.
resources: drone frames, assault shuttles, hull plate
story: Mordant's oldest outer-rim yard, built over lava vents that heat its foundries for free. The shift siren has sounded every eight hours for a hundred and forty years; it stayed silent for one day only, the day of the great walkout at Navalia, when Caminus walked out too.
history: Caminus was a volcanic world nobody wanted, too hot to farm and too far out to trade. Mordant wanted it for the vents. In R.72 Mordant's new outer yard sounded its first shift siren, and the siren has sounded every eight hours since. The foundries were built over the lava vents, which heat them for free, and the yard took its crews from the clinics and the debt market: Indentured lifers, signed to the yard for life and recycled into it when they die. The nearer moon was ringed with dry docks for the small hulls, the drone frames and assault shuttles, while the foundries rolled hull plate for the bigger yards. For more than a century Caminus was Mordant's model outer yard. Then in R.189 twelve thousand crew walked off the main yards at Navalia in one shift, led by Marta Sobel. Caminus walked out the same day, and the siren was silent for the only day in its history. The next shift it sounded again. Mordant has never said what it did to bring Caminus back, and the lifers who know do not say either. In R.212 the siren still sounds every eight hours, a hundred and forty years after the first, and the Walkouts count their years from the one day it did not.

world: A broad temperate upland world, mostly land, with high wheat plateaus split by steep valleys and a few small inland seas. Wheat runs to the horizon on every plateau, worked from farm towns laid out in squares along the old survey lines. Summers are dry and clear, winters short and cold, with snow on the highest ground.
from_space: Golden wheat plateaus under clear skies, cut by dark green valleys, with small blue seas and thin cloud. At night the farm towns form a loose grid of lights over the plateaus, brightest round the one lane port.
moons: None.
people: 300 million free farmers in square-planned farm towns across the wheat plateaus, and a port town that handles every sack Lode buys.
story: Free wheat farmers who must sell to Lode at Lode's price, because Lode owns the only lane out. They feed half the sector and cannot afford new boots.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, about three-fifths land, of rolling grassland and low forest. The training grounds are planned grid camps laid across the plains, and on the largest continent stands the copy: a full-size Hand city of towers, plazas and queues, with a bakery at its heart. Firing ranges and churned exercise fields scar the land between the camps.
from_space: Grey and green, with square grid camps across the plains and one large grey city that is lit at night with almost nobody in it. Pale scars of exercise ground show round every camp.
moons: None.
people: 25 million: Pacifier recruits and instructors in the grid camps, and Indentured hands hired by the day to riot in the copy city.
story: Continuity trains its Pacifiers here, rehearsing riots on a full-size copy of a Hand city. The rioters are Indentured hands, paid by the day.
history: Campus was settled as grassland farms, and after the Receivership Continuity took it to train its garrisons in open country, naming it for the drill field. As the Hand's cities grew in its second century, Continuity built a full-size copy of one on the largest continent: towers, plazas, clinics and tram lines, all of it empty. Pacifiers rehearse riots there against Indentured hands paid by the day to be the crowd. Constans Ordo came here from the Long Strike, which began in R.182 on a Lode holding; he held its cordon for three years without a shot, the strike never ended, and Continuity moved him to Campus. He ran it for sixteen years. He put a bakery queue at the heart of the copy, because every riot he had ever seen began in a queue, and he taught every class that noise kills and calm keeps people alive. He had learned it in R.166, on his first deployment, in a bread-queue crush that killed thirty-seven people without a baton touching any of them. In R.201 he was sent to Standstill, and he is still there. The bakery still bakes, and the day rioters still queue at it.

world: A frozen high mountain world about 5,200 km in radius, with no open sea, only ice-filled basins between granite ranges. Continuity's garrison is cut into the peaks above the Yard Road, its barracks and families buried in heated galleries under the snow and its watch posts on the summits. Cold winds scour the ridges bare.
from_space: Dark granite grey with snow-white ridges and broad ice under thin cloud, and at night a few garrison lights in the passes, in tidy rows.
moons: None.
people: 2 million hands, mostly Contract grade soldiers and their families, in heated galleries under the peaks.
story: Continuity's mountain garrison, cut into the peaks above the Yard Road, its barracks and families buried in heated galleries under the snow. Its watch posts can see every toll beacon in the sector, and its gunners fire on any ship that skips a toll, with Lode paying a bonus per hit.

world: A city-world larger than most, its land built over from coast to coast in one planned grid of barracks blocks, parade squares and module shops, the same block repeated millions of times. Its small seas are walled into cooling basins for the yards. The two great dock complexes stand at the poles, on what were once the ice caps.
from_space: A grey grid from pole to pole, so regular it looks printed, with hazard-yellow dock complexes capping both poles and dark cooling basins between. By night the grid lights in square blocks that switch on and off with the shifts.
moons: None.
people: 60 billion hands, mostly Indentured yard crews, in barracks blocks laid out like one endless army camp; every block is numbered, and every hand sleeps in the block of the shop they work in.
story: Sixty billion yard hands live in barracks blocks laid out like one endless army camp. The shift sirens are so loud they can be heard from orbit, people say.
history: Castra was a yard world under the Republic, and its barracks first went up in the Last War, when Mordant needed crews faster than any town could raise them and billed the Republic for every bunk. At the Receivership Mordant renamed it in its own army Latin: the camp. Through the Hand's first century the camp was simply extended, block by identical block, until it covered the land and walled the seas into cooling basins. The polar docks build hull modules for the Mandates laid down at Classis, and the barracks send crews to every yard on the Yard Road. Decimus Varo was born here in R.154, in a numbered block like all the others, and at sixteen he was measured for a gunnery suit and sent to load turrets on new Mandates. He has survived three restructurings by never being the tenth; the third came after Lockout in R.193, when he signed the order that sealed that system off. When Navalia and Caminus walked out in R.189, Castra's sirens kept sounding, and Mordant has never let its other yards forget it. In R.212 the war has every dock working all three shifts.

world: A hot jungle and ocean world, about a fifth land, its big islands steep, wooded and full of big game. The family keeps the islands as a hunting reserve, with lodges for its Hand renters on the coasts and the interior left wild. Rain falls in heavy afternoon storms, and the seas are deep and dark.
from_space: Dark green islands in a blue-black sea, with white surf on the coasts and towers of afternoon storm cloud. At night only a few lodge lights show along the shores.
moons: Two moons: a grey cratered rock and a dark ice-rock moon flecked with bright craters.
people: 4 million, nearly all guides, beaters, cooks and lodge staff working for the landholding family; the family itself numbers a few hundred.
story: Jungle and ocean full of big game, kept as a hunting reserve by a free-world family that rents it to Hand executives by the week. Guides whisper that some hunts are for animals that walk on two legs.

world: A volcanic world whose one great continent is grey ash slopes and black lava flows round a dozen live volcanoes. On the old flows of half that continent the families' ash terraces have turned green, field above field up the slopes, and fresh flows still cut through the farmland after every eruption. The villages are small and unplanned, moved and rebuilt each time the ground does.
from_space: Grey ash and black flows with green terraced farms spreading over them, and red glow on the night side where the lava runs.
moons: None.
people: 4 million people in farming families, each family holding a share in a volcano and working the ash on its slopes.
story: Every family owns a share in the volcanoes and farms the fresh ash on their slopes until the grey turns green; the fields now cover the old flows of half a continent. When a volcano erupts, the lost shares are redrawn by lot, and nobody has ever won one twice.

world: A city-world somewhat larger than most with no wild ground left: one city covers the surface in planned districts of towers and office grids, and the climate is run from engines under the crust. The old seas survive only as a few regulated basins between the districts, and there is almost no ice. The Board sits in the old Parliament hall at the centre of the oldest district.
