Thin dust storms blow off the day side and settle in the twilight valleys, round a few small lakes.
from_space: A dusky violet ring of twilight between a dim mauve day face streaked with pale dust storms and a black night face rimmed with frost. At night only a few lamp-lit cave mouths show along the twilight edge.
moons: One small moon of cratered grey rock, unused.
people: 2 million weavers, all in family caves under the twilight highlands, one family and one tapestry to a cave.
story: In deep caves under the twilight highlands each family weaves one tapestry over a lifetime, knotting in every name it has lost; dyes dry in the glare of the day side, wool keeps in the night side's cold. Alma buys the finished pieces for executive resorts, never asking whose names hang on its walls.

world: The last charted gas giant in the west: green-grey bands pocked with dark round storms, rough and turbulent. Its one town is a raft that drifts with the wind, lowering wells into the deep cloud for water and fuel. The town follows no plan, decks lashed to decks round the well-heads.
from_space: Green-grey bands pocked with five dark round storms. At night a single small cluster of lights drifts across the bands.
moons: Two moons: a dark ice-rock and a small captured rock.
people: 200,000 townsfolk and drifters on the one drifting raft town.
story: The last charted world in the west. Its one town is a raft that drifts with the wind, and the wells it lowers into the deep cloud for water and fuel belong to whoever holds them this week. Beyond it the Hand's maps go blank, and the town sells charts of the dark that nobody can check.

world: A warm golden gas giant with soft cream zones and one red storm. A chain of festival barges circles its equator at the breathable layer, each barge a small town with its own square and its own weekly holiday, joined end to end by cable bridges into one loop round the whole planet. The barges are added and rebuilt by their own crews, so no two look alike.
from_space: Golden and cream bands with a red storm, inside a broad pale icy ring. At night the barge chain is a dotted line of light round the equator, brightest where the festivals are on.
moons: One moon, cratered rock, and a broad pale icy ring.
people: About 600 million on the barge chain, run by a city assembly; Locals from across the sector meet here, hidden in the crowds on the cable bridges.
story: A cheerful festival chain of barges strung end to end round the giant's equator, every barge with its own holiday each week. It is also where Locals from across the sector meet, hidden among the crowds that cross the cable bridges.

world: A cool, dry world a little smaller than most, with low mountains and wide dim plains. A failed thickening left the upper air so dense and heavy that it would crush a ship, and the ground below lies in permanent dusk. Everyone lives in the crystal caves under one plateau, reached by a single deep lift from the only landing field.
from_space: An opaque pale violet haze hides almost everything; through thin places the ground shows dim tan and grey. By night there is nothing to see but one faint light where the lift head stands.
moons: None.
people: About 30,000 cave dwellers, all in the crystal caves at the foot of the lift; the Runner crew that holds the lift lives at its head.
story: A failed thickening left the upper air heavy enough to crush a ship, so everyone lives in crystal caves below, reached by one deep lift. Whoever holds the lift holds the world. It has changed hands nine times.

world: A dry industrial world of grey-tan plains and low eroded hills, with no seas and only a few muddy reservoirs. Factory towns sprawl across the plains in loose belts, chemical works, pill presses and workers' blocks thrown up wherever a factory boss could buy land, under a yellow smog that hangs over every town. Old dump scars and quarry pits mark the ground between them.
from_space: Grey-tan land under a yellow smog, thickest over the factory belts. At night the belts glow yellow-white through the haze in long, ragged sprawls.
moons: None.
people: 3 billion factory workers and their families in the factory towns, run by the factory bosses; the pills they press sell across the Heartland.
story: Factory towns that make cheap copies of Alma's happiness pill and sell them across the Core. Alma calls it theft; the buyers call it the only way to afford feeling fine.

world: A cool, wet moorland world smaller than most, with low rounded hills, peat bogs, small grey seas and modest ice at the poles. It rains or drizzles most days. The settlers live in scattered farmhouses and parish villages, none of them planned, with the peat cuttings in long dark strips behind them.
from_space: Olive and brown moor under constant grey cloud, the seas dull pewter where the cloud breaks. By night a thin scatter of farmhouse lights.
moons: None.
people: About 3 million settlers, in parish villages and farmhouses spread thin across the moors; at any time a few hundred of them are the Collective's wounded.
story: Peat-cutting settlers on a damp, quiet moor world. Nothing much happens here, which is why the Collective's wounded are sent to recover in its farmhouses.

world: A pale blue-green gas giant with soft bands and one copper storm, crowded by eighteen moons. Nobody lives in its clouds. The raft towns float on the seas of its largest moon, a warm living world of rainforest, swamp and ocean with a few smoking volcanoes, whose tides are pulled every way by the other seventeen.
from_space: Blue-green bands, quiet and hazy, with one copper storm. The big living moon shows green and blue with white surf along every coast; the other moons are a crowd of bright and dark specks.
moons: Eighteen moons; the eight biggest drawn: the living moon of rainforest, swamp and sea where the raft towns float; a volcanic sulphur moon; two smooth bright ice moons; two cratered grey rocks; and two small captured lumps. The other ten are small rocks and ice.
people: About 20 million raft-town folk, all on the living moon's seas.
story: Eighteen moons pull at the living moon's seas, and its tides are impossible to predict. The raft-town fishermen publish a tide almanac every year and are wrong every year, and betting on it is the moon's favourite pastime.

world: A small, dense, airless iron world with no water and no air worth the name. Its plains have been cut into stepped red pits so wide that whole districts sit on their terraces, with cratered black highland between them. The sealed towns are cut into the pit walls in planned rows, and ore trains run from the pit floors straight to the launch rails on the ridges.
from_space: Dark red and black, cratered on the high ground, with huge stepped pits across the plains. By night every pit is outlined in rings of terrace lights, and straight lit launch rails run up the ridges.
moons: None.
people: 150 million hands, Indentured miners and rail crews, in sealed towns cut into the pit walls; the shifts ride the same trains as the ore.
story: An airless iron world that exists only to feed Classis's yards. The miners live in sealed towns cut into the pit walls. Ore trains run straight from the pits to the launch rails, and so do the miners' shifts.

world: An airless rocky world about 4,200 km in radius, of dark hills and broad plains, with scrapfields on every plain where Mordant's dumped hulls have come down or been dragged. The Walkouts live in pressure domes welded from old hull plate, grown in clusters beside the biggest wrecks, and they strip every hull to the frame. Nothing grows and nothing weathers; a hull dropped here generations ago still shows its paint.
from_space: A patchwork of grey wreck fields and dark hills, with a ring of dumped hulls in low orbit, lumpy and glinting, waiting to come down. At night the domes glow in small clusters by the wrecks, and cutting torches spark among them.
moons: No moons; a ring of dumped hulls in low orbit, fresh wreckage, thickest where Mordant's barges last let go.
people: 300,000 Walkouts and salvage families in welded hull-plate domes beside the wreck fields.
resources: salvage, refitted ships, tractor gear, scrap metal
story: Mordant pays to dump its scrapped hulls here and never asks where they go. The Walkouts live in pressure domes welded from old hull plate, strip every wreck and send it back out as a fighter, often with its registry number still visible under the new paint.
history: Mordant has dumped its scrapped hulls on this dead world for longer than anyone can say. Barges tow them in, cut them loose into low orbit and leave; Mordant pays the fee and never asks where they go. For most of that time nobody lived here. After the walkout at Navalia in R.189 the Walkouts went looking for hulls they could build from unseen, and before long a crew found the dump. They welded pressure domes from old hull plate beside the biggest wrecks and began to strip them, and Make Do grew into the strand's home yard. Every wreck is stripped to the frame and sent back out as a fighter, often with its Mordant registry number still showing under the new paint. Niko Sava, who walked off Navalia with Oz Petrenko's turret crew, built a gunship here over four years, rivet by rivet, from three dead hulls. A coolant fire while he was stripping one left burn scars up both his arms. He named her Second Shift, for the time Mordant did not own. Mordant still pays the dumping fee, and the Walkouts call it the only fair wage the dynasty ever paid them.

world: A cold volcanic world of ordinary size, almost all mountain: black basalt ranges with snow on their shoulders and lava vents in the valleys, where the foundries are built over the heat. There is no sea. The foundry towns follow the anvil lines up the valleys in long planned terraces, and the slag heaps between them have grown into hills of their own.
from_space: Black peaks and grey snowfields by day, with smoke trailing from the valleys. By night the valleys glow orange with furnace light and lava, and the foundry towns show as hard white grids beside them.
moons: None.
people: About 1.5 billion hands, Indentured and Contract grade, in foundry towns along the anvil lines; most families have worked the same line for nine generations.
story: Mordant's oldest forge, where hull plate is hammered in mountain foundries. Yard families have worked the same anvil line for nine generations and are buried in its slag heaps.
history: Mordant opened the first foundries at Malleus in about pre-R 30, when Parliament ordered the Last War navy on account and the yards at Incus needed more hull plate than they could roll. The vents gave free heat and the mountains gave iron, so the forge was built where the two met. The war ended, the Republic never paid in full, and the forge kept working through the default and the Receivership without losing a shift. After the Birth Debt came in R.31, every child born on an anvil line was billed at birth and signed to its parents' line, so the yard families became lines of numbers as much as lines of blood. The oldest lines now count nine generations. Malleus hammered the riveted plate of the Statutes in the Hand's first century and hammers Mandate plate today. Its dead are buried in the slag heaps beside the line they worked, and the heaps are terraced now, one terrace to a family, so that a hand going to shift walks past every generation before it.

world: A hot desert world whose old seas have dried into deep basins of pale salt, cut by ravines that once carried rivers into them. The land between is orange-tan rock and sand with worn ranges. The towns are dug into the ravine walls, grown level by level, and the metal workings lie in the dry sea beds below.
from_space: Orange-tan with pale salt beds filling the old sea basins and dark ravines branching into them, almost cloudless. At night small lights line the ravine walls.
moons: Two cratered moons: a tan-grey rock and a smaller grey rock.
people: 8 million settlers in towns dug into the ravine walls, rationing water by the bucket.
story: A desert world whose old seas have dried into deep ravines and salt beds. Its people live in towns dug into the ravine walls, mine metal in the dry beds and ration water by the bucket, and they sell to the Collective for water instead of credit.

world: A temperate world of flat fields and managed forest on land Lode built from ground mine tailings, with low relief, regular rivers and moderate seas. Every field is a numbered rectangle, and the farm towns are planned to match, one to each block of fields. There are few mountains; the highest ground is old bare rock that Lode never covered.
from_space: A patchwork of green and pale yellow fields in rectangles, dark blocks of managed forest, grey bare uplands and blue seas. At night the farm towns show as evenly spaced points of light, one to each block.
moons: One small moon, a cratered grey rock.
people: 400 million hands, mostly Contract grade farm crews assigned field by field.
story: Lode built this farm holding on bare rock, spreading ground tailings from its mines until the land would grow. Every field has a Hand number like a hand does; when a field underperforms it is retired, and the crew who worked it is reassigned with it.

world: A lively gas giant of turquoise and white bands, thirteen of them, curling into spirals round three white storms. At the breathable layer the foam-glass raft cities are lashed together into archipelagos, which their people sail through the clouds by trimming their lift and still call islands.
from_space: Turquoise and white bands curling into spirals, scattered with pale foam-glass archipelagos that catch the light. By night the raft islands glow warm white in long chains.
moons: Two moons: a smooth bright ice moon close in, and a dark ice-rock further out. No rings.
people: 5 billion islanders on the foam-glass raft cities, under their own elected government: songwriters, musicians, weavers and the crews who trim the rafts.
resources: music, art, fine textiles, fuel gas
story: Its people live on raft cities of foam-glass lashed into archipelagos, which they sail through the clouds by trimming their lift and still call islands. Their songwriters supply half the music on Alma's broadcasts, under contracts nobody read. In lean years Alma buys the government too, and the songs get happier.

world: A warm, wet farm world a little larger than most, flat almost everywhere, its old marshes drained by Lode a century ago and seeded as fields. A shallow sea covers about two fifths of it. The farm towns are company grids laid along the canals, and every field is the same size.
from_space: Neat squares of green and gold between straight canals and a shallow blue sea. By night the canal towns make regular dotted lines of light.
moons: One moon, grey and cratered.
people: About 1.5 billion hands in canal towns, renting their fields by the furrow.
story: Lode drained these marsh plains and seeded them a century ago to feed the city-world next door. Fields are rented by the furrow to the families who work them, and the rent rises with the yield, so a good season is the most frightening thing that can happen.

world: An ocean world smaller than most, almost all deep sea, with a scatter of small white marble islands rising steeply from the water. The quarry cuts step down every hillside in bright terraces, and the quarrymen's villages are planned blocks at the foot of each cut, beside the loading quays.
from_space: Deep blue sea scattered with white islands, the quarry cuts bright and square on their hills, under broken cloud. A few small lights on each island by night.
moons: None.
people: 16 million hands, Contract quarrymen and stone-boat crews, in quarry villages on the islands; the blocks go to Charter and the dust stays in their lungs.
story: Island quarries cut white marble for Charter's facades. The islanders say the Board walks on their hills; they mean it as a curse.

world: A pale sea-green gas giant of middling size, with gentle bands and a pair of small storms. Nobody lives in its clouds. The herbalists' guild grows its cures in the rain forest of the giant's living moon, a warm, wet jungle world of steep green hills and short rivers, where drifting bands of rain cross the canopy every day.
from_space: A pale sea-green giant with soft cream bands and two small ochre storms, and beside it a jungle moon streaked with drifting white rain bands. The moon's night side shows the scattered lights of guild villages.
moons: Six moons: the living jungle moon of the herbalists, then five small grey moons, three of them cratered rock and two captured lumps.
people: 70 million descendants of the first settlers on the living moon, in canopy villages and hill towns across the rain forest; most of the adults belong to the guild.
resources: medicinal plants, foodstuffs, dyes, rare botanicals
story: Its herbalists' guild grows half the cures sold in the sector in the rain-forest canopy of the giant's living moon. Alma offered to license the whole canopy; the guild burned its own seed vault the night before the vote, so there was nothing left to sign away.

world: A dry savanna world of tawny grass plains and low rocky hills, with no seas, only watering holes that swell in the wet season and shrink in the dry. The Hand's border fence runs across the plains as a line of sensor posts. The herders' villages are small and unplanned, spread thin and gathered round the water.
from_space: Tawny grass with dark watering holes scattered over it. At night a thin scatter of village fires shows, and one straight dotted line of sensor posts across a continent.
moons: Three moons: two cratered grey rocks and one small captured lump.
people: 90 million herders in villages round the watering holes.
story: The Hand's border fence ends here: a line of sensor posts across the savanna. The herders cut it every dry season and the Hand repairs it every wet one.

world: A world a little smaller than most of acid seas, with grey stone plateaus standing out of them like shelves. The air is thin and sour and nothing grows. Praevisio's factories are sealed over the plateau tops in rigid grids, and the workers live in pressure halls cut into the shelves below them.
from_space: Yellow-green seas and grey plateaus under a sour haze, the factory roofs pale grey grids on the plateau tops. By night the factories are lit in hard white blocks that never go dark.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock and a small captured rock.
people: About 8 million hands, mostly technicians, in the pressure halls inside the plateaus.
story: Praevisio's robot factories stand on sealed stone shelves above the acid seas, building Proxies by the million. The workers live in pressure halls cut into the shelves and are paid in performance points that lose value each month.

world: A tidally locked world with a brown desert day face, an ice night face and a twilight band between them that Alma is turning green one strip at a time. The finished strips are young rainforest and fields, watered by rain that mirrors on the day side drive across the band; ahead of them, herb farms grow under domes on bare tan soil awaiting its turn. The picking towns are planned settlements at the edge of each new strip, moved on as the green advances.
from_space: A ring of green and tan twilight between a brown desert face and a white night face, the green in broad strips with tan between. The day side flashes where the mirror fields catch the sun, and on the darker edge of the band the picking towns show as neat rows of light along the green.
moons: One moon, cratered grey rock.
people: 400 million hands, mostly pickers and garden staff, who get free medicine and are billed for it later.
story: Alma's botanical gardens: the twilight band is being greened a strip at a time, and herb farms grow under domes ahead of the new soil. Mirrors on the day side drive the rain; the night side keeps the harvest frozen. The pickers get free medicine in return, which they are billed for later.

world: A tidally locked world of ordinary size. Its towns are strung along the twilight band among red mesas and green river valleys, where meltwater from the night-side glaciers runs toward small warm seas. The day face is scorched rock and dust, its rim covered in the mirror farms that make the fuel; the night face is ice. The market towns are old and crowded, grown along the rivers without a plan.
from_space: A red-orange belt of mesas threaded with green valleys and a few blue-green seas, between a scorched brown day face glinting with mirror farms and a white night face. Along the twilight the market towns make a long chain of lights.
moons: One moon, a pale cratered rock.
people: About 300 million traders, in market towns along the twilight rivers; the mirror crews live at the edge of the day face.
story: A trading world strung along the twilight band, where Hand money is refused and everything is bartered or paid in fuel. Mirror farms on the day side make the fuel, and the night side's glaciers feed the rivers. Lode's toll collectors leave with purses full of goods they can't account for.

world: A large, dry rocky world whose plains are crusted with quartz, so the ground glitters white and pale blue in the sun. Small shallow seas lie in the lowest basins, and dozens of city-states crowd the plains between them, each an old dense core with its own walls, its own grid and its own style, set apart from its neighbours by bands of bare glittering quartz. Each city was planned once, centuries ago, and has grown past the plan ever since.
from_space: Sparkling white and pale blue plains with grey city sprawl, a few small dark seas and thin cloud. At night the lights fall into dozens of separate bright clusters with dark quartz between them.
moons: One moon, cratered grey rock.
people: 35 billion in dozens of city-states, each with its own council, its own militia and its own vote, every year, on whether to pay Lode's toll.
story: The largest free world on the old trunk route: dozens of city-states packed onto the quartz plains. Lode's toll lane runs straight through, and every year the cities vote on whether to pay.
history: Meridian was settled long before the Republic, in waves: each ship that landed founded its own city on the quartz plains and kept to it, and by the time the Republic's census arrived the plains held dozens of city-states that agreed on nothing but their borders. Under the Republic each city sent its members to Parliament, and all of them grew rich on the old trunk route that crosses the world. The Receivership in R.0 changed nothing on the ground; the freighters landed the next morning as usual. The change came with the toll lanes, between the R.50s and the R.70s, when Lode beaconed the route and ran its fast lane straight through Meridian's space. The cities could not agree on whether to pay, so each one put the toll to a vote, and each has voted on it every year since. In some years most of them pay and the lane runs smoothly; in others half refuse, and Lode's freighters land elsewhere for a season. The Hand has never forced the question, because foreclosing on thirty-five billion people would stop the very route it wants to tax. By R.212 the vote is the biggest day in Meridian's calendar, and the Hand still wants the world.

world: A dry rocky world with no seas, its ochre gravel plains broken by hundreds of flat-topped red buttes and mesas. The towns are carved inside the buttes to escape the heat, room behind room back into the rock, with the dead walled up in the deepest rooms behind the kitchens. Rain falls a few days a year and floods the washes between the mesas.
from_space: Rust-red buttes and mesas over ochre plains, with dry washes and almost no cloud. At night the butte towns show as small separate points of light, each mesa its own spark.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock.
people: 18 million settlers in independent towns carved into the buttes; Lode's surveyors have mapped every one.
story: The towns are carved inside the red buttes to escape the heat. The dead are walled up in the rock behind the kitchens, so every family lives with its grandparents.

world: A gas giant whose upper cloud layer is cold, thin and windy, and whose warm green layer below is unbreathable: the first colony settled down there and choked. The settlers live high in the cold layer in towns hung under great balloons, with barley gardens hung in tiers beneath them. The oldest town carries the first colony's dead in a gondola at its edge, facing the drop.
from_space: Pale violet and grey bands, fast and streaky, over a deep green haze that shows through the gaps. A faint dust ring and three small moons. The balloon towns are white flecks high on the cloud tops.
moons: Three small moons: a captured lump orbiting inside the ring, whose dust feeds it; a cratered grey rock; and a dark ice-rock further out. Then a faint dust ring.
people: About 8 million settlers, all in the balloon towns of the high cold layer.
resources: wind power, fuel gas, hanging-garden barley
story: Its settlers live high in the cold, windy cloud layer, in towns hung under balloons, and never go down: the warm green layer below is where the first colony choked. They keep that colony's dead in a gondola hung from the edge of the oldest town, facing the drop.

world: A hot, forested world of steep mountain ranges and long green valleys, with warm seas over about a third of it. The resin woods climb the slopes, and where the tapping is heaviest the bark runs amber. Snow lies only on the highest crests. The towns are old and grown, each a cluster of sap houses and family stands along a valley floor.
from_space: Deep green ranges streaked amber along their slopes, between warm blue seas and white cloud. At night small strings of town light run down the valleys.
moons: None.
people: 12 million settlers in valley towns, nearly all of them families who tap their own named stands.
story: Resin forests where every tree is tapped by a named family, some for three hundred years. The resin seals half the hulls in the rim, and Mordant pays a year in advance, which means Mordant owns most of next year's sap.

world: A gold gas giant of bright, even bands with a few small storms, and nobody living in its air. Round its equator, high above the clouds, runs Lode's toll ring: a band of docking stations, customs halls and berths joined into one structure, where every ship on the lane docks and pays.
from_space: Gold-yellow bands with a rusty storm or two, behind a thin bright ring of station lights girdling the planet. On the night side the toll ring glows in one continuous line, brighter where the queues are longest.
moons: None; the toll ring is the only habitation.
people: About 300,000 hands on the toll ring: toll clerks, dock crews and customs staff, all on Lode's books.
story: Lode's toll ring on the trade route: every ship on the lane docks at one of its stations and pays. Toll clerks keep a share of what they collect, so new fees appear every quarter, among them a fee for queueing.

world: A hot junk world where Mordant drops its slag, spoiled alloy and failed castings from orbit. Fresh drops pool and glow for years in craters of their own making, and older heaps have cooled into black scrap mountains. Acid rain falls out of brown smoke. The salvage clans live in towns dug under the cooled heaps, grown tunnel by tunnel.
from_space: Rust-brown and black scrap mountains cracked with orange slag glow under brown smoke, and now and then a fresh drop flares as it lands. At night the slag pools glow orange, and the towns show only as pinpricks at the heap edges.
moons: None.
people: 4 million salvagers in clan towns dug under the cooled heaps.
story: Mordant's waste world: slag, spoiled alloy and failed castings are dropped here from orbit, and glow for years where they land. Salvage clans live in towns dug under the cooled heaps and pick through the rest in the acid rain. A third of the Collective's fighters started out as something Mordant threw away.

world: A large, cold gas giant of pale blue-grey bands with no great storms. The settlers do not live in its cloud: they live aboard a Republic-era customs hulk parked in low orbit and skim fuel from the upper cloud with tethered scoops.
from_space: Pale blue-grey bands, and close above them one bright hulk of plating in low orbit, its customs lights still lit.
moons: One, and not a natural one: the old customs hulk, a bright speck of plating in low orbit. The giant has no natural moon big enough to see.
people: 50,000 settlers, nearly all aboard the hulk.
story: Settlers live in a Republic-era customs hulk parked low over a gas giant on the Trunk Line, skimming fuel for passing ships, and still stamp passports that nobody needs.

world: A small temperate river world, more land than sea, of green valleys, low hills and many fast rivers. Water mills stand on every river, and the mill towns are old and small, grown along the banks round the millraces.
from_space: Green valleys and blue rivers running down to small seas, under light cloud. At night small warm lights strung along the rivers.
moons: None.
people: 5 million millers and farmers in mill towns along the rivers.
story: Water mills grind grain from the plains worlds. The millers have kept the same price for a century and refused every buyer; the joke is they are the last honest business in the galaxy.

world: A world-city larger than most, mostly land: silver cities spread across high plateaus, cut by deep tan canyons and set round broad blue lakes, with small seas and small ice caps. The cities are a mix of old grown cores on the lake shores and planned districts on the plateaus, built under the assembly's own codes.
from_space: Blue lakes and tan canyons between silver cities under light cloud. By night the plateaus are a near-continuous field of white and gold light, broken by the dark canyons and lakes.
moons: Five moons: a cratered grey rock, a dark ice-rock, a smooth ice moon, a small captured lump and a second cratered rock. None is built on.
people: 19.7 billion citizens in the plateau cities and lake towns.
story: Twenty billion people under their own elected assembly: the biggest world the Hand never acquired. Lode tolls every ship that leaves, and the assembly pays rather than fight.

world: A gas giant whose cloud deck will kill a person in a day: a murky stack of olive bands, fast and turbulent, under yellow haze, with two dull yellow storms. The pump towns ride the current of one band, circling the planet every forty days and lowering pipes into the deep methane layer the crews call the bogs. The towns are old and grown, decks bolted to decks.
from_space: Murky olive and brown bands under a yellow haze, with two dull yellow storms. At night faint lights run in a single line along one band, where the pump towns drift.
moons: None.
people: 6 million in the drifting pump towns, all of them masked from birth.
story: The air here will kill you in a day. The pump towns ride the current of one band, circling the planet every forty days; everyone wears a mask from birth, a bare face on deck means a visitor or a corpse, and Lode buys the methane they pump.

world: A tidally locked desert world a little smaller than most. The day face is tan sand and rock under a sun that never moves, and a third of it is covered by the Republic's mirror fields, row on row. The night side is frozen. The mirror families live in the twilight in small towns of salvaged glass and cut their water from the night-side ice.
from_space: A tan day face flashing with vast mirror fields, a dark frozen night side, and a thin twilight band between them with a chain of small lights. The mirrors flash as you pass over them.
moons: None.
people: About 1 million mirror tenders, in twilight towns; work crews live out on the day face for weeks at a time in shaded huts.
story: Republic-era solar mirrors still cover a third of the burning day face and beam power to whoever pays. The mirror families live in the twilight, cut their water from the night-side ice, and have kept the mirrors running for two hundred years without a spare part they did not make themselves.
history: The Republic had the mirror fields built in its last century, on contract and on credit, to beam power to the worlds round it. The contractor laid mirrors over a third of the day face and was still owed for them when the Republic defaulted. At R.0 the payments stopped, and the contractor's crews were left behind with a field of mirrors and no spares. They stayed. They learned to grind glass from the day-side sand, cast frames from salvage and cut water from the night-side ice, and they began selling the power to whoever paid, Hand or free. Two centuries later their descendants, the mirror families, still keep every mirror running without a spare part they did not make themselves. Each family tends its own rows and hands them down. The Hand wants the power, and Lode has offered more than once to buy the fields. The families reply that the Republic still owes them for the work, and ask whether the Hand would care to settle that debt first.

world: A dry plains world nearly 6,900 km in radius, of golden grassland and low rolling hills, with no seas, only lakes that shrink in every dry year and leave pale beds behind. Farm towns sit on every rise, grown over centuries, and the fields round them are watered in circles from deep wells. Cloud is thin, and rain is the subject of every vote.
from_space: Golden grassland with pale dry lake beds and green farm circles under thin high cloud. At night the towns make an even scatter of light across the plains.
moons: Two moons: a grey cratered rock and a dark ice-rock moon.
people: 2 billion free farmers and townsfolk in grown farm towns across the plains; the elected assembly splits three ways, and the farmers' third decides.
story: A broad plains world whose assembly is a third Collective sympathisers and a third the Hand's friends. The last third are farmers who vote with the weather, and both sides pray for rain.

world: A rainy world, 6,300 km in radius, of grey marsh plains and shallow lakes broken by ridges of bare rock full of caves. It rains most days under heavy cloud. The mining towns cling to the rock ridges above the marsh, grown shaft by shaft, and the forgers work deep in the caves below them.
from_space: Grey-green marsh under heavy cloud, with dark rock ridges showing through. At night dim town lights along the ridges.
moons: One moon, a barren grey cratered rock. No rings.
people: 100 million free miners and forgers, in the ridge towns and the caves beneath them.
story: Forgers in its caves sell clean Hand numbers to anyone running from a debt. The Hand lets them work, because Praevisio tracks every number they sell.

world: A temperate world, 6,000 km in radius, about half ocean, its land folded into steep forested mountains and long green valleys. Snow lies on the high ridges and at the poles; cloud gathers along the mountain walls and rains into the valleys. The mill towns are old and grown, strung along the valley rivers beside the silk-moth farms, and only the Alma mill compounds are laid out on a grid.
from_space: Green valleys and dark forested ridges under white cloud and snow, with deep blue sea around them. At night only a faint scatter of mill-town lights along the valley floors.
moons: One moon, a plain cratered grey rock with no use. No rings.
people: 800,000 hands, Contract grade weavers, spinners and moth farmers, in mill towns along the valley rivers.
story: Its valley mills spin the soft cream fabric of every gown in every Alma clinic. The weavers are not allowed to wear it, and each finished bolt is checked for hairs, which are traced back to the hand who shed them.
history: Silk-moth farmers settled Mollis's valleys long before the Receivership and spun for whoever would buy. At the Receivership in R.0 Alma took the mills to supply its clinics and named the world Mollis, soft. Since then every clinic gown in the Hand has been woven here in soft cream cloth that the weavers may not wear. Every finished bolt is checked for hairs, and each hair is traced back to the hand who shed it. Nell Kovač was born here in R.132 and went to the looms as a child; at fourteen, in R.146, a loom took the tip of her left forefinger and the dressing went on her bill. In R.152, when a girl on her row was fined a month's pay for a single hair, twenty-year-old Nell stopped her loom. By evening the whole valley mill was silent, and three days later Alma dropped the hair fines. It was the first strike of the woman the Collective now calls Gran, and she left Mollis to lead many more. The hairs are still traced and logged. The weavers no longer pay for them, and they still say the girl's name.

world: A temperate world of rolling green hills, vineyards and old forests, with moderate seas and modest mountains. The old stone cities are walled and stand on hilltops, grown over centuries round their banking houses and law courts, their streets winding to fit the hills.
from_space: Green hills and walled cities, blue seas and scattered cloud. At night each hill city is a tight bright knot, with dark vineyard country between.
moons: None.
people: 700 million citizens, most in the walled hill cities: bankers, clerks, lawyers and wine growers.
story: Old banking families who lent the Republic money and lost it at the Receivership. They still hold the notes and sue the Board in Hand courts every year. They always lose, and pay the court fees gladly.
history: Montefosco was settled before the Republic by families who grew wine on its hills and lent money to their neighbours. Under the Republic its banking houses grew rich lending to Parliament. In the Last Famine, about pre-R 60 to pre-R 40, and the Last War, about pre-R 30 to pre-R 12, they lent again, each time Parliament voted for something it could not pay for. In pre-R 1 the Republic defaulted, and its creditors stopped supplying it: five corporations and a crowd of smaller banks, Montefosco's families among them. The fleets stopped, then the freighters. At the Receivership in R.0 the Bench appointed the five biggest creditors as receivers, and the smaller creditors got nothing. Montefosco's families kept their notes. Soon after, they filed their first suit against the Board in a Hand court, and they have filed one every year since, two centuries of suits, and lost every one. They pay the court fees gladly, because paying them keeps the case alive. The Hand tolerates the world: it is small, it is polite, and its lawyers are useful. In R.212 the banking houses still sit in council, and the Republic's notes are still in their vaults.

world: A damp, warm world of low ground and shallow grey lakes, covered in fungal forest: stands of pale caps and mauve gills as tall as trees, under a mist that rarely lifts. The grower families live in villages in the clearings where the grey mushroom grows best, and the villages have spread along the old trackways without any plan.
from_space: Grey-white and mauve, soft and misty, with dull grey lakes showing through the haze. At night only small, scattered village lights glow through the mist.
moons: None.
people: 25 million growers in family villages, who sell every crop to Alma and have only just learned what it goes into.
story: Fungal forests where one grey mushroom yields a compound in Alma's happiness pill. Alma buys every crop and owns none of the land, and the growers have just learned what their crop is for.

world: A calm, pale gold gas giant with thirteen soft bands and two small amber storms, its winds gentle and its belts barely curling at the edges. Nobody lives in its air and nothing floats there; every farm is on the grain moon.
from_space: Pale gold and cream bands, quiet, with two small amber storms. Beside it the grain moon is striped gold and green: wheat belts running round it between hedged pasture and small blue seas. At night the moon's cooperative towns are faint warm dots.
moons: One moon, a living moon of wheat belts, hedged pasture and small cold seas, where every farm and every one of the grain cooperative's towns stands. No rings.
people: 200 million farmers, all on the grain moon, in cooperative villages strung along the wheat belts and a few silo towns at its harbours.
story: A grain moon whose crop is bought before it is planted: Lode lends the seed and owns what comes up. In good years the farmers are free; in bad years the Hand owns the moon without sending a single soldier.

world: A mild, wet world of low rolling forest, smaller than most, with long shallow inland seas and no high mountains. Moss a metre deep covers the ground under the trees, so the land is green right down to the shorelines, and small ice caps sit at both poles. The settlers live in timber villages in forest clearings, unplanned and far apart, linked by rivers more than roads.
from_space: Deep moss green from coast to coast under drifting wet cloud, the seas dark blue-grey between. At night there is almost nothing, a faint dusting of village lights along the rivers.
moons: None.
people: 2 million settlers in forest villages, most of them cutting and baling moss for export.
story: A forest world carpeted in moss a metre deep that holds water like a sponge. The settlers sell the moss to desert worlds as soil, and Lode is lobbying to have the old forest treaty declared legacy.

world: A volcanic world of ordinary size, with no water at all: about a third of its surface is black islands of cooled crust, and the rest is open lava flowing slowly between them. The islands drift, crack and sink, and a new one hardens every few years. The oldest islands, near the middle of the drift, carry the domed towns of former fishing families and a few Runner crews, grown one dome at a time, with quays of lava glass along the shores.
from_space: Black island crusts in a web of glowing orange lava, with grey-brown smoke over the active rifts. By night the lava lights the whole face orange, and the domes show as small warm clusters on the oldest islands.
moons: None.
people: 6 million settlers in domed island towns, most from the old fishing families, with a few Runner crews who keep a landing field on the largest island.
story: Islands of cooled crust drift in seas of lava. Fishing families who once worked a real sea now live in domes on the oldest islands, beside a few Runner crews. A new island hardens every few years, and the first family to land on it owns it, until it sinks.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, half grey shallow sea and half low mudflat, with hardly any high ground. The huge close moon drags the sea back and forth across the flats, so the coastline moves by tens of kilometres in a day. The towns are built on sledges and stand wherever they were last hauled, without plan; each storm season the whole population drags them inland on ropes.
from_space: Brown mudflats and grey sea under shifting cloud, the shore never in the same place twice, with a huge cratered moon hanging close. By night small scattered town lights on the flats.
moons: One large close moon, a grey cratered rock with dark plains, big enough to fill a wide patch of the sky. No rings.
people: 3 million in sledge towns on the mudflats, each run by its harbour master; most gather shellfish at low tide, and a few work the tidal mills.
story: A big close moon drags the sea back and forth across the mudflats, and the flats are thick with shellfish. The towns are built on sledges, and each storm season the whole population hauls them inland on ropes.

world: A mild swamp world half drained: Lode cut drainage channels across the old wetland, and the peat flats it left are dry and brown. The Growers' dams are flooding them back from the edges, so green marsh and new open water now cover a third of the old wetland. It is low and flat, with almost no mountains and soft cloud over the wet side. The villages are built on the dams themselves.
from_space: Dry brown flats cut by straight drainage channels, giving way to green wetland and bright new water. At night a few lights show along the dams.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock, unused.
people: 1 million Growers in dam villages, with a small Kiru exile camp working beside them.
story: Lode drained these swamps for peat; the Growers are flooding them back, one dam at a time, and the green now reaches a third of the old wetland. A small Kiru exile camp shares the work.

world: A polluted world, 7,000 km in radius, where centuries of industry have eroded the land into gullied brown wastes between the factory cities. Small oily seas cover a fifth of it. The cities were never planned: they grew along the old rivers and round the docks until they met, and thick yellow smog hangs over all of it.
from_space: Brown and grey under thick yellow smog, the seas dull and dark. At night a dim orange city glow through the haze, brightest round the docks.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey-brown rock and a small captured lump. No rings.
people: 12 billion free citizens, dock crews, factory hands and traders, crowded into the industrial cities.
story: A filthy industrial world of twelve billion, and the biggest free market off Lode's lanes. Smoke hides the docks, which is how the Runners like it.

world: A cold, airless rock about the size of a large moon, with low hills and pale dust plains between old craters. The only settlement is the mooring field on one dust plain: rows of landing pads, pressurised sheds in tidy lines beside them, a control tower and the captains' cairn.
from_space: Dull brown rock with pale dust plains and grey craters. On the night side one small cluster of pad lights shows, and often a dozen convoy ships holding above it.
moons: None.
people: 12,000 dock hands and mooring families in pressurised sheds by the pads, under three Runner families.
story: A bare rock where convoys bound for the twin free ports gather before the last jump, and the mooring families live in pressurised sheds by the pads. Every captain who musters here leaves a stone on the cairn by the landing field; the cairn is now taller than the control tower.

world: A warm ocean world larger than most, with only a scatter of land: volcanic islands under jungle, ringed by wide reefs and shallow lagoons. There are no ice caps, and tall cloud builds over the islands every afternoon. The fishing villages are old and grown, strung round the island shores on stilts over the lagoons; the Kiru live on one outer reef the villages gave them.
from_space: Emerald islands and pale reef rings on deep blue, with heavy white cloud over the islands. By night a few loops of village light round the coasts and one small dim cluster out on a reef.
moons: One pale moon, a cratered rock bright enough to fish by.
people: 300 million villagers on the islands, and a small Kiru exile community, one ark crew of a few hundred, on an outer reef.
story: A warm sea world where a small Kiru ark crew settled on a reef, and the fishing villages let them stay. Hand broadcasts say the reef is empty.

world: A warm ocean world a little larger than most, almost all sea, with low scattered islands ringed by broad pale reef shallows. There are no real mountains and only thin polar ice. The islanders' towns are old and grown, stacked along every reef lagoon, their workshop streets following the shore rather than any plan.
from_space: Bright blue sea, turquoise and cream reef shallows round the islands, and scattered fair-weather cloud. At night the island chains glow warm and dense, every lagoon lit along its rim, with dark sea between.
moons: Three moons: a bright smooth ice moon nearest, then a grey cratered rock, then a small frozen-plains moon, cream with a dark red band. The divers time the pearl harvests by their three tides.
people: 3.5 billion islanders, packed on the reef islands: pearl divers, lacquer workers and the families of the guild.
resources: pearls, lacquer, shell goods, luxury goods
story: Ocean world of pearl beds and lacquer workshops, selling luxury to the core by the shipload. The pearl divers' guild sets the price, and it has turned down three Alma offers to buy the beds and rename the sea.

world: A cold dark world of ice and bare rock, with rugged mountains and frozen seas. One sheltered valley is warmed enough to live in by hot springs, and the valley town is built round the dry house: wards, bathhouses and small gardens kept green by the spring water.
from_space: Dark blue-grey ice and rock, with one bright valley. At night the valley town is the only light on the planet.
moons: None.
people: 600,000, nearly all in the valley town: people going dry, their carers, and a handful of Ilmar volunteers on the night wards.
story: A free house where anyone can go dry, from either side, no questions asked, in the one valley that hot springs keep warm enough to live in. A handful of Ilmar volunteers run the night wards.

world: A large brown gas giant of tight tan and umber bands, turbulent and stormy, with one long-lived dark storm in its southern belts. Nobody lives in its air. Lode's skimmer barges dive from the refinery moon into the cloud tops, fill their tanks in one fast pass and climb back.
from_space: Tan and umber bands with a dark storm spot, and beside the planet one moon lit up like a factory, its plating and slag glowing. On the night side the barge runs show as faint moving sparks between the moon and the clouds.
moons: One moon carrying the refinery: an industrial moon of bare mined rock and steel-plated works, where the crews live and breathe refinery air.
people: About 90,000 hands, mostly Contract grade, on the refinery moon and its skimmer barges, billed per lungful for the air they breathe.
story: A brown gas giant Lode skims for fuel: barges dive from the refinery moon into the cloud tops and climb back full. The moon's crews breathe refinery air and are billed for it per lungful under Lode's atmosphere contract.

world: A mild world of high mountains over steaming lowland jungle, about 5,900 km in radius, with just over half its surface land. Alma terraformed the frozen peaks into cool green valleys, warming them and seeding them with grass, and only the highest summits still carry snow. The clinic terraces climb the valley sides in white tiers, planned to the metre. The jungle below is left alone, and cloud lies in it all day.
from_space: Deep green jungle under heavy lowland cloud, green mountain valleys above it, and white clinic terraces bright on the peaks, with small snowcaps on the highest. At night the terraces glow in neat lines along the valleys, the jungle dark below them.
moons: One moon, a pale cratered rock; Alma's transports park in its orbit while mothers clear quarantine.
people: 40 million hands, mostly clinic staff and their service crews in the planned valley towns, with several hundred thousand mothers at any time, flown in to give birth.
story: Alma softened the frozen peaks above the jungle into cool valleys for its frontier birth clinic. Mothers are flown in from all over the sector and flown home alone. The newborns go into Alma's books with interest from the first breath.

world: A calm gas giant with soft, wide bands and little turbulence. Alma's clinic cities hang under heated gas balloons at the warm layer where the air is breathable, in the quiet mid-latitudes, each a planned ring of wards round a central maternity hall.
from_space: Soft cream and blue-green bands, pale and quiet, with one blush-pink storm. The balloon cities show as white platforms on the cloud by day and rings of cool light by night.
moons: One moon of smooth white ice, where the incoming liners refuel.
people: About 200 million hands in the balloon cities, mostly clinic staff and mothers under contract; forty million newborns pass through each year.
resources: births, medicine, Birth Debt contracts, some fuel gas
story: Alma's birth clinic for the sector hangs in the giant's cream clouds, its wards slung under heated gas balloons at the layer where the air is warm and breathable. It bills forty million births a year. Every newborn is issued a Hand number and a first statement before it is washed.
history: Natalis was only a skimming post before Alma came: a few crews drawing fuel gas from the upper clouds, and nobody living below them. After the Birth Debt was introduced in R.31, Alma set out to put a birth clinic within reach of every sector, and its surveyors found the warm, breathable layer under Natalis's cream clouds: clean air, no ground to buy and no local claims to settle. The first ward was slung under a heated balloon in the Hand's first century, and the clinic cities grew round it as the sector's births were routed in. Since R.88 the mothers under contract have been issued the happiness pill on arrival, and the wards have been quiet. Natalis bills forty million births a year now. Every newborn is issued a Hand number and a first statement before it is washed, and the first line of the statement is the cost of the gas that keeps the ward in the air. The newborns ship out within the month; the mothers stay for the next contract.

world: A cold gas giant of pale orange haze over faint, gentle bands, with little turbulence and one small rust-coloured storm. Its air is hydrogen and helium with nothing to breathe. Lode's refinery platforms float in the upper cloud on engines that burn the gas they skim, set out in planned rows along the calm mid-latitude bands.
from_space: A soft pale-orange ball, the bands so faint they read as haze, with one dull red-brown storm. By night the refinery platforms show as rows of lit decks, each with the glow of its engines beneath. The bottling depot moon is plated steel and open pits, lit along its rim.
moons: One moon: an industrial moon, Lode's bottling depot, cut into open pits and plated with tank farms and loading docks.
people: 670 million hands, Contract gas crews living on the refinery platforms in the clouds; a few thousand more work the bottling depot moon.
story: Lode bottles helium from an atmosphere no one can breathe. Crews live on refinery platforms held up by engines that burn what they skim, and work outside in sealed suits rented by the shift. A crew that tears a suit pays for the suit before the doctor.

world: A temperate world of plains and forests a little larger than most, about half land, with long shallow seas between its continents. The plains are built over in planned yard towns and foundry districts in Mordant's grids, and the forests survive only in the hills. A slipway cable rises from the equator by the main yards, and hulls climb it to the line of slipways strung out to the two yard moons. The weather is mild, and the air carries foundry smoke.
from_space: Green and gold land ruled by grey yard grids, blue seas and light cloud, with a bright line of slipways running up from the equator to two plated yard moons. At night the yard districts blaze in strict rectangles, and the slipway line is lit end to end like washing on a cord.
moons: Two moons, both plated over as yards, steel-grey and lit, with a line of slipways strung between them and the planet; the inner one holds the dry docks, the outer the fitting basins.
people: 3.6 billion hands, mostly yard crews of every trade, in planned yard towns on the plains and on the two yard moons; the dynasty lives in its tower above the slipways.
story: Seat of the Mordant dynasty and its main yards, where the slipways hang in a line from the planet to its two moons like washing on a cord. Here twelve thousand yard crew downed tools in one shift and walked off; the Walkouts were born that day, and the dynasty still has the names.
history: Mordant built ships here before the Receivership. The dynasty drove its first hull at Incus, but Navalia became its home and its main yards, and at R.0 the world took the yard name it has carried since. The slipways were strung out one by one until they hung in a line from the equator to the two moons, and both moons were plated over as yards. Children came to the yards as soon as they could hold a tool and were measured at sixteen for one trade for life. Tiberius Mordant, ninth of the dynasty, was born in the family tower above the slipways in R.138, and his son Lucan in R.176. Marta Sobel, a hull fitter who became the youngest foreman on the main yards, spent four years building a network nobody could see. In R.189 she blew her whistle, and twelve thousand yard crew downed tools in one shift and walked off. Oz Petrenko walked with his turret crew, Niko Sava among them; Quintus Ferro stayed at his post. Ballast came to break the line, and a young captain, Hostilia Varr, refused to fire and took a thrown bolt to the face. The Walkouts date themselves from that day, and the dynasty still has every name. Marta's network never left the yards. In R.209 it got a welder called Nobody off the yard moon in a crate.

world: A mid-sized gas giant buried in grey-white fog from the cloud tops down, with only faint dark green bands showing through. The wind is slow and steady and there are no great storms. The villages float in the fog banks on gas bags and fuel burners, sinking slowly and climbing back, and the villagers call the clear troughs between the banks valleys.
from_space: A smear of grey-white haze over faint dark green bands, with no clear edge to the cloud tops. At night the villages show as scattered pinpricks of burner light that drift and fade in the fog.
moons: Three small moons, all captured lumps of dark rock; nobody lives on them.
people: About 11 million by the Board's estimate, though nobody has counted; they live in floating villages that are never in the same place twice.
resources: hired labour, smoked goods, fuel gas
story: The fog never lifts, and its villages float in it, sinking slowly and burning fuel to climb back, so none is ever where it was. The Hand's census is a guess: whole villages appear on no list, and nobody there was ever billed for being born. The Board's estimate has changed by a million in each of the last five years.

world: An unbreathable storm world smaller than most, all bare dry mountains worn into needle-thin spires, with no water and almost constant lightning-charged dust storms. The masts stand on the tops of the spires, and the crews' sealed huts are bolted to the rock below them, in clusters wherever a spire is wide enough.
from_space: Purple-grey dust storms swirling over grey needle spires, with lightning flickering in the cloud. By night a few tiny lights cling to the spires.
moons: One small moon, a captured lump of dark rock.
people: About 30,000 mast climbers, in sealed huts on the spires; most of them are young.
story: Rare gases are drawn from the lightning-charged storms by masts on needle-thin mountain spires, and the crews live in sealed huts bolted to the rock below them. Mast crews are paid by the strike: a good year is a short life.

world: An airless world, 6,200 km in radius, of grey-amber rock, broad cratered plains and low mountains. Its cities and ground yards are domed or dug in under the plains, laid out by the shipwrights' council in tidy grids round the launch pits.
from_space: Bare grey-amber rock with clusters of dome lights. Its moon is ringed with dock frames whose yard lights sparkle on the night side.
moons: One moon, an industrial moon ringed with dock frames where freighters are fitted out. No rings.
people: 2 billion free citizens, in domed cities and buried towns.
story: A free world of domed cities whose own small shipyards build freighters for anyone, on the rock and on the dock frames round its moon. Mordant has offered to buy the yards four times; each time the yards built something faster that year.

world: A dry canyonland world smaller than most, with no open water at all. Tan plateaus cover it, cut by nine great canyons hundreds of kilometres long and dark at the bottom; water runs only in the caves and along the canyon floors. The cave towns are cut into the canyon walls by the families who live in them, each stretch of wall its own clan's, with no plan but the rock's.
from_space: Tan and ochre plateaus under very little cloud, cut by nine dark canyons. By night almost nothing: the cave towns are inside the walls.
moons: Three small moons, all captured lumps of dark rock. No rings.
people: 30,000 people, canyon families, in cave towns along the nine canyons; each family mines its own stretch of wall by hand.
story: Thirty thousand people live in cave towns along nine canyons, each family hand-mining its own stretch of wall and drinking from the cave springs. They will not sell to Lode. Lode's surveyors keep having climbing accidents, and the canyon families keep sending polite condolences.

world: A city-world larger than most, built over almost every square kilometre of land round a few dark inland seas, with old mountain ranges worn into terraces of housing. The city grew outward from nine old lane ports, the gates, and each district keeps its own grid, so the streets change direction at every district line. Smog thins the light, and the cloud is low and brown.
from_space: Grey-brown sprawl round dark inland seas, under a brown haze, with ships stacked in orbit over every gate. At night the whole land surface is light, with nine brighter knots where the gates are.
moons: None.
people: 200 billion free citizens in the city's dense districts; the merchant senate counts every one, because each will owe a share of the last instalment.
story: A free city-world of two hundred billion that is buying its independence from the Hand in instalments. The last payment falls due in nine years, and nobody on the planet believes the Hand will accept it.

world: A cool ocean world of dark grey seas, with one long continent like a broken spine and its single long coast facing the prevailing storms. The harbour city sprawls along that coast for thousands of kilometres, an old grey city of quays, warehouses and steep stone streets that grew one harbour at a time until the harbours met. Inland the ground rises quickly to moorland and bare hills where few people live.
from_space: Dark northern seas under heavy grey cloud, and one long coast lined with grey urban sprawl. At night the city is a single unbroken ribbon of light along the shore.
moons: None.
people: 1.4 billion citizens in the one harbour city, under an old harbour council that pays the Hand's taxes and keeps its own police.
story: A grey harbour city on the Trunk Line that pays the Hand's taxes and keeps its own police. Continuity has offered to 'assist' with security three times. The city council has politely declined three times.

world: A small frozen world of snowfields and ice sheets over low hills, its old seas frozen solid. There is almost no weather, only thin ice-crystal haze. The few station families live in heated shafts dug down into the ice, so nothing stands on the surface but the shaft heads.
from_space: White ice and snow, the frozen seas a pale blue-grey. Most nights a green glow of aurora rings both poles and spills over the dark side, and under it there is not a single light.
moons: None.
people: 3,000 settlers in a few hundred station families, living in heated shafts under the ice.
story: An ice world where the sky burns green most nights. A few hundred families mine ice from heated shafts under the lights and believe the lights are their dead, so nobody flies at night for fear of disturbing them.

world: A temperate gas giant of calm, broad bands, with gentle winds at the breathable layer and few storms. The market city rides there: ten thousand lift-hulls of every age and size lashed into one mesh hundreds of kilometres across, warehouses on the outer hulls and the oldest merchant houses at the centre. Nobody ever planned it; hulls are added at the edge whenever a new house can afford one, and its streets are the cables and gangways between them.
from_space: Grey-brown and sage-green bands, softly blurred, with one pale oval storm. By day the city is a single pale patch on the clouds; by night it is a great sprawling web of light, the only light on the planet.
moons: None.
people: 2 billion free citizens, all in the floating city: merchants, warehouse crews, clerks, fuel skimmers and their families. The merchants' guild runs it, and its first law caps every loan at one year and forbids any debt to pass to a child.
resources: trade goods, finance, warehousing, fuel gas
story: A free market city of two billion, ten thousand lift-hulls lashed into one mesh at the breathable layer, undercutting Hand prices across the sector. Its merchants' guild has one law above all others: no loan may run longer than a year, and no debt may pass to a child.

world: A dark gas giant banded grey-green and near black, with slow, heavy turbulence and a few dark brown storms. There is no settled place: the Unruled camps drift on rafts of salvaged gas cells in the upper cloud and go wherever the wind does.
from_space: Dark grey-green bands, almost no lights. By night a handful of faint flickers move across the bands, too few and too scattered to call a city.
moons: None.
people: 80,000 people on drifting rafts, by Praevisio's count; nobody here has ever counted.
story: The Unruled call it nothing, so the map calls it Nowhere. Their camps drift on rafts of salvaged gas cells and go wherever the wind does; nobody answers hails and nobody signs anything. Debt registries have burned at the hands of people who trained here, three of them in a single night.
history: Nowhere has no history it will admit to, which is the point of it. It was charted under the Republic as an unnamed fuel stop and never settled, and under the Hand it was a line in Lode's survey books that never paid enough to work. The Unruled came in the years after R.182, when the Long Strike began and Lode closed its gate at Pennygate, and people who would not go back had nowhere else to go. They lashed salvaged gas cells into rafts and let the wind take them, because a camp that does not know where it will be tomorrow is hard to forecast and harder to find. They call it nothing, so the map calls it Nowhere. Nobody answers hails and nobody signs anything. When the Table first sat in R.201 the Unruled sent a voice to it and refused to call themselves part of anything; Nowhere is their seat only in the sense that this is where they can be found when they choose to be. In R.203 a Lode Hand number who had stopped paying interest at fifteen turned up here and trained; she calls herself Static, and in R.209 she burned three debt registries in one night. Praevisio files every report from Nowhere as low confidence.

world: A big gas giant of pale green and brown bands, with strong turbulence where its deep heat rises. The brokers' cities float on that heat, each riding over a chimney drawn up from the deep, a cluster of exchanges and counting houses wired to every relay in reach. The grain comes from the living moon, a wide farm world of plains and shallow seas.
from_space: Pale green and brown bands with turbulent edges and two dark brown storms, beside a big green-blue living moon. On the night side the floating cities light up in dense clusters through the mid-latitudes.
moons: Two moons: the living farm moon, green-blue with wide plains and shallow seas; and a small grey cratered rock.
people: 3.5 billion: about 3 billion brokers, clerks and their households in the floating cities, and 500 million farmers on the living moon.
resources: information, grain from the moon, fuel gas
story: A gas giant of information brokers, whose cities float on heat drawn up from the deep and whose grain comes from its living moon. Anything can be learned for a price. Praevisio is its biggest customer and buys the Hand's own leaks back before Continuity can find them.

world: A warm gold gas giant about 66,000 km in radius, banded gold and amber, with a single small red-brown storm. Nobody lives in its clouds. Its largest moon is a warm living world of orchards, small seas and old estate towns, where the families who own it have held the same land for centuries.
from_space: Gold and amber bands, with nine moons visible from orbit. The largest is green and blue under thin cloud, and at night its estate towns glow densely.
moons: Nine moons. The largest is a warm living world of orchards and small seas; the other eight are rock and ice. Drawn with the orchard moon: a small cratered rock close in and a second further out, a dark ice-rock, a smooth bright ice moon, a cream frozen-plains moon and two small captured lumps. The smallest is not drawn. No rings.
people: 9 billion, nearly all on the orchard moon: landholding families, orchard hands and fruit traders.
story: Nine moons circle a gold giant, and the largest is a warm, rich world of orchards and old families who sell fruit to the yards and refuse to sell one hectare of land. The only free world in Mordant's home sector, and proud of it.

world: A cold world somewhat larger than most, its tundra and glaciers giving way valley by valley to green lowland where Alma's warming plants run. About two-fifths is open grey-blue sea that no longer freezes in summer. The clinic cities are planned clusters of cream domes along the warmed valleys, each with its maternity wards on the sunny side and its billing floors behind.
from_space: White tundra and glaciers, with green lowland spreading up the valleys from the coasts and open grey-blue sea. By night the clinic domes glow soft cream in chains along the valleys.
moons: None.
people: 2.1 billion hands, clinic staff and mothers, in domed clinic cities along the warmed valleys; most of the people on Nutrix on any day are there to give birth and leave.
story: Alma's birth clinic for the sector, under domes on a tundra Alma is warming one valley at a time. Most hands in this sector were born here, and each left with a bill. The maternity wards play soft music all day; the billing floors play none.

world: A pale gas giant of ochre and white bands, nine of them, with two small brown storms and steady winds. Nobody lives in its air; the herders are all on the living moon.
from_space: Ochre and white bands, and beside them a large yellow-green moon of savanna with green river lines and small blue seas. At night the moon shows only the faint scattered lights of the herders' camps.
moons: Two moons: a large living moon of yellow savanna, green river lines and a few shallow seas, where the herding clans ride; and a small grey cratered rock further out. No rings.
people: 5 million herders on the living moon, in clan camps that move with the herds and a few salting towns on the rivers, where the beef is packed for the Collective's fleet.
resources: cattle, salt beef, hides from the living moon
story: Herders ride the endless savanna of the giant's living moon, and their cattle are the best-fed meat on the rim. The Collective's fleet eats it salted, and Lode's agents pay twice the price to keep it away from them.

world: A hot, mid-sized world of flat red plains and low rock hills, with no seas. The oasis cities sit far apart, each green round its own deep well. They are old and crowded, grown with no plan, and caravan roads run between them across the open plain.
from_space: Red-ochre plains with pale dust blowing across them; the oases are too small to see by day. At night the oasis cities show as bright points, far apart.
moons: None.
people: 800 million in the oasis cities, every city loyal to its own well.
story: Oasis cities linked by caravan across hot red plains, each green round its own well. Each oasis sells its red pigment dust; feuds between wells are older than the Hand.

world: A cold dry world, 5,200 km in radius, with no open water: rust-brown plains and flat-topped mesas, with frost on the high ground in winter. Old hulls are towed down onto the plains between the mesas and torn apart where they land, so the ground round each breaking pit glitters with scrap. The crews sleep inside the hulls they strip; the only planned buildings are Mordant's sorting sheds.
from_space: Rust-brown mesas under thin dust, glittering with scrap. At night small lights inside the half-stripped hulls and the brighter sheds.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 1.5 million hands, mostly Indentured yard crews, living inside the hulls they strip.
story: Mordant's breaking yard: old hulls are towed down to the cold mesas and torn apart for steel, and the crews sleep inside the hulls they strip. Mordant's lifers are signed to one hull for life, so when a hull is broken here, its crew is broken up with it and resold.

world: A cool forest world a little smaller than most, with dark conifer forest, fast cold rivers, cold seas over nearly half of it and broad ice caps. The vaults lie under the forest along the rivers, and the technicians' towns stand over the vault heads in planned rings.
from_space: Dark blue-green forest and sea, with white steam plumes rising from the vent fields along the rivers. By night the vault towns are small rings of steady light.
moons: One moon of cratered grey rock.
people: About 10 million hands, mostly Staff technicians, in the vault towns; the locals in the forest villages are fewer and quieter.
story: Praevisio's data vaults lie under a cold forest, cooled by its rivers. Locals are forbidden to cut trees, light fires or speak above a whisper near the vents.

world: An amber gas giant about 61,000 km in radius, banded amber and cream, with one great dark storm in its southern mid-latitudes wide enough to swallow a small world. The skimmer families' refinery rafts ride the fast winds round the storm's edge, never inside it, and their skimmers dive from the rafts into the cloud tops for fuel gas.
from_space: Amber and cream bands bent round one dark brown storm. At night a scatter of small raft lights circles the storm's rim.
moons: Eleven small moons, the eight largest drawn: a dark ice-rock, a cratered grey-brown rock, a smooth bright ice moon and five small captured lumps. The three smallest are captured lumps too small to show. No rings.
people: 600,000 skimmers and their families, living on refinery rafts that ride the winds round the great storm.
story: Free skimmer families live on refinery rafts that ride the winds round the edge of the great dark storm. They dive their ships into the cloud tops for fuel gas and sell it at half Lode's price, and Lode's freighters keep accidentally ramming their skimmers.

world: An airless rock barely 3,800 km in radius, grey-blue and heavily cratered, with no water and no weather. Its one settlement is the court dome, a Republic building raised on a crater rim, cracked across the top and patched from inside, with archive halls dug into the rock beneath it. The clerks' and pensioners' quarters are cut as galleries under the dome's foot.
from_space: Blue-grey cratered rock with dark plains and bright crater rims, and one lit dome on a crater rim, the only light on the whole world at night.
moons: One moon, a small grey cratered rock, unnamed and unused.
people: 60,000 clerks, archivists and pensioners under the dome and in the galleries beneath it; the judges are a handful, all past ninety.
story: The last court of the Republic still sits here, under a cracked dome on a dead rock. Its judges are all past ninety and hear the cases nobody files; the Board has never quite dared to close it.
history: Old Bench was a Republic court archive before it was a court: a domed hall on a dead rock, where the Bench kept copies of its rulings far from any crowd. In R.0, when the Bench ruled the Republic bankrupt and handed it to its creditors, three of its judges dissented. They left with the court's seal and came here, to the one building that still belonged to the Bench and not to the receivers, and sat again. Their successors have sat ever since. They hear the cases nobody files, issue rulings nobody enforces, and keep a register of every one. Each judge chooses the next from among the clerks, which is why all of them are past ninety. A meteorite cracked the dome long ago, and it has been patched from inside so many times the patches have patches. The Board has never quite dared to close it: the judges hold the Bench's own seal, and no Hand lawyer wants a court to argue over which bench is the real one. Around the judges live sixty thousand clerks, archivists and pensioners, who keep the archive dry and the lights on.

world: A cold slate-blue gas giant with eight soft bands, one wide violet-grey storm and little turbulence. Nothing lives in its air and nothing has ever been built there.
from_space: Slate-blue and grey-blue bands with one dusky violet storm. Beside it a green and blue moon with no city lights at all; on its night side, at most the few lamps of a pilgrim camp.
moons: Two moons: a living moon of empty forest, grassland and clear lakes, where the stone rings stand on the hilltops; and a small dark ice-rock further out, unvisited. No rings.
people: Uninhabited; a few hundred pilgrims are on the living moon at any time, camped by the stone rings, most of them landed illegally.
story: Empty forests and stone rings on the giant's moon, older than anyone can date. The Unwritten say the first war against thinking machines ended here, and pilgrims land illegally to leave broken circuit boards on the stones.

world: A small barren world about the size of Mars, with thin breathable air that was made, over soil that never took. Bleached grey plains and low hills, old craters softened by the made air, a little frost at the poles and no water. The dead seeding grids still stripe the plains in long straight bands, and the telescope stands on the highest ridge with the astronomers' houses below it.
from_space: Bleached grey and pale stone, striped by faint straight bands of dead seeding grid, with a thin blue rim of air at the edge. By night a single small cluster of lights round the telescope.
moons: None.
people: About 3,000 astronomers and their families, in a village under the telescope on the highest ridge.
story: A Republic-era telescope on a rock whose air was made breathable two centuries ago. Nothing ever grew in it, and the dead seeding grids still stripe the plains. The astronomers who refuse to leave see farther than Praevisio's probes, and sell what they see.
history: The Republic built the Old Lens telescope late in its life, on a small airless rock chosen for its still sky, and paid a contractor on credit to make the rock livable for its staff. In the last years before the Receivership the contractor thickened the air until it could be breathed and laid seeding grids across the plains to start a soil. The air took. Nothing else did: the seed died in the grids, and the grids are still there, stripes of dead lattice across the grey. At R.0 the astronomers stayed. When the receivers' clerks came to wind the observatory up, they found it cost nothing to run and that nobody would buy it. The astronomers have lived there ever since, grinding their own mirrors and teaching their own children. They see farther than Praevisio's Speculator probes, and they sell what they see: star charts to Runners, comet warnings to free worlds, survey plates to whoever pays. Praevisio has offered to buy the telescope more than once. The astronomers answer by post, slowly.

world: A small airless rocky world, grey and cratered, under a ring of wrecked ships from a battle nobody now remembers.
