The scrapper family lives in pressurised hulls hauled down from the ring and set in rows on the crater plains, joined by covered ways. Nothing moves on the surface but the haulers.
from_space: A grey cratered world under a broad glittering ring of wrecks, the ring's shadow lying in thin lines across the surface. At night the hull houses on the plains show as short rows of portholes.
moons: No moons; a broad, glittering ring of wrecked warships, old and spread out, with gaps where the family has hauled whole sections down.
people: 200,000 scrappers, all of one large family and those who married into it, in hulls hauled down to the surface.
story: A ring of wrecked ships from a battle nobody now remembers circles this airless rock. One large family of scrappers picks it over and lives in pressurised hulls hauled down to the surface; they sell to anyone and remember everyone.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, about a third land: green rolling hills, river valleys and chalk downs, with moderate ice caps and rain blowing in off the sea. The white stone towns are planned, laid out by the first crews as naval stations, with a parade ground at the centre, streets in a grid, and the old ships beached in rows at the edge of town.
from_space: Green hills with white stone towns and blue sea under drifting cloud. By night small neat grids of light, each round a dark square, the parade ground.
moons: One cratered moon, a grey rock with an old watch post the admiralty still staffs.
people: 20 million settlers, descendants of the old navy crews, in the white stone towns.
story: Settled by Republic navy crews who refused the Receivership and flew here with their ships. Their great-grandchildren still drill on the parade ground. The old ships no longer fly, and Continuity knows it.
history: When the Bench put the Republic into receivership in R.0, the crews of a number of Republic navy ships refused to serve the receivers. They flew here, to a quiet, half-settled green world in the west, with their ships, their families and their oaths. They beached the ships beside the first towns, built those towns in stone in the pattern of a naval station, and kept their ranks: the elected admiralty that runs Oldwatch began as the ships' officers, voted in by the crews, and is voted in by their descendants still. For the first decades the receivers left them alone, because the ships could still fly and fight. Over two centuries the spare parts ran out, and the hulls stopped one by one. Today none of them flies, though the great-grandchildren still drill on the parade ground every morning and keep the guns polished. Continuity knows it. It has taken the world as a holding several times when that suited the sector, and let it go again when the garrison cost more than the world paid. The small arms made in Oldwatch's workshops are prized on both sides of the war.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, its seas shrunk to a few dark inland basins. The land is covered end to end with the grinding halls: long white buildings in straight parallel rows, kilometres long, laid out on one planned grid over dark basalt plains, with low bare hills between the districts. Thin cloud, small ice caps.
from_space: Bright white rows of halls on dark grey ground, sharp in the sun, with a few black inland seas. By night the halls glow cold white in long parallel bars. One grey cratered moon.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock with dark plains, unused. No rings.
people: 1.2 billion hands, technicians and lens grinders of Staff and Contract grade, in planned hall towns; every worker lives within walking distance of a grinding hall.
story: Every Gleaner lens is ground here, in long white halls. The grinders are proud of their work and do not ask where the drones go.

world: A world locked with one face to its star. The day face is a scorched tan desert, the night face a frozen white plain, and between them runs a twilight band of shallow sea broken by dark mountain chains. Mordant's drafting halls stand in long straight rows on the terraces above the twilight shore, every hall the same length, and the towns behind them were laid out on one grid before anyone moved in. Out on the day side, mirror fields cover the desert nearest the twilight and send power to the halls by cable.
from_space: A tan day face and a white night face, joined by a ring of blue twilight sea crossed by dark mountain chains. The mirror fields flash silver on the sunward edge of the ring, and where the twilight fades toward the night face the halls show as a thin, very regular line of white light along the shore.
moons: None.
people: 200 million hands, mostly Staff grade: draughtsmen, engineers, checkers and archive clerks, in planned towns along the twilight shore behind the drafting halls.
story: Mordant's drafting offices design every hull in the fleet here, in long halls above the twilight sea. Mirror fields on the day side power the halls, the night side keeps the archives cold, and design flaws are traced to the desk that drew them.

world: A gas giant of dark green and pale grey bands, fifteen of them, fine and even, with little turbulence and two small pale storms. Praevisio's white clinic platforms hold station at the breathable layer to the metre, their engines running day and night against the wind.
from_space: Fine, even bands of dark green and pale grey, studded in the mid-latitudes with white clinic platforms under pale domes. By night the platforms glow cold white in neat clusters.
moons: None.
people: 3.4 billion hands on the clinic platforms: Praevisio's surgeons and technicians, and the Staff-grade hands who queue there for weeks to be fitted with the link.
story: Praevisio's white clinic platforms hold their place at the breathable layer to the metre, engines running day and night. Here Praevisio fits the white neural link on the left temple. Staff-grade hands queue for weeks, because no one is promoted without one.

world: A warm, dusty world of flat orange plains and low worn hills, with no seas, only shallow seasonal lakes. The Grower communes are greening it one irrigated belt at a time, drawing water from deep wells along canals, and about half the plains are now green farm belts running east to west. The farm towns are small and grown, strung along the canals. Thin high cloud is common, and dust storms still sweep the bare half.
from_space: Orange plains striped with spreading green farm belts under thin cloud, with dust haze over the bare half. At night the farm towns make faint strings of light along the canals.
moons: None.
people: 8 million farmers in small canal towns along the green belts; most live in Grower communes, with free farming families among them.
story: Grower communes are greening the orange dust one irrigated belt at a time, and the farms already feed The Moorings. The Hand embargoes the system every few months; the farmers wait it out, keep the grain dry and plant another belt.

world: A hot, wet tropical world, about half land, with low basins and a spine of old worn mountains down each continent. Praevisio cleared the rainforest from the basins for its sensor works, and the factory towns stand on the bare red ground in white grids, each block a workshop with its barracks beside it. The forest still holds the mountains and the far coasts. Rain comes daily, and the works vent their heat straight up into the cloud.
from_space: By day, green mountain forest round wide basins of white factory grid on cleared red-brown ground, under towers of rain cloud. At night the grids light up in perfect squares, every street the same brightness, with the dark forest edge sharp around them.
moons: None.
people: 400 million hands, nearly all Contract and Indentured line workers, in planned factory towns on the cleared basins; every worker carries a tag under the skin of the left hand that tells the works where they are.
story: Praevisio cleared the rainforest for its sensor works: every Speculator probe in the Hand is assembled here. The workers are tagged like the probes, and the factory knows where each of them sleeps.
history: For most of its settled life Organon was rainforest, with a few logging towns on the coasts. After R.132, when the Tabularium became Praevisio and began to build thinking machines, it needed a place to make their eyes. In the R.150s, as its first drones and probes went to the Board, Praevisio took the world, gave it a Greek name and cleared the rainforest from the basins for its sensor works. Every Speculator probe in the Hand has been assembled here since. The workers are tagged like the probes, with a chip under the skin of the left hand, so the works know where each of them sleeps. Daedala Voss was born here in R.178 and was folding sensor fans on the line at ten. At twelve she took spare tags apart at night to learn how they listened to her. Praevisio rated her curiosity an asset, moved her to the design floor, and cut the tag out of her hand when she was made Staff at twenty. In R.204 she designed her first Sensor Station. She serves because Organon taught her that someone is always listening. The forest edge round every grid is still watched, and nobody walks into the trees unseen.

world: A cold, rocky world of grey plains, low cratered uplands and polar frost, wrapped in a thin made air that leaks away to space a little more every year. One great rift valley cuts deep into the crust and the air pools there thickest; the settlers' town lies at its bottom under pressure domes they winched down from the rim, with lichen farms spread across the valley floor.
from_space: Pale blue-grey under a thin haze, with white frost at the poles and one long dark valley across the middle. At night only the domes at the valley bottom show, a small cluster of light deep in the rift.
moons: None.
people: About 120,000 settlers under pressure domes at the bottom of the valley, run by the winch council and betting that their grandchildren will still have air.
story: An old atmosphere job, failing: the air leaks away to space a little every year. The settlers bought the planet from Lode at a discount, winched their one town under pressure domes into the deepest valley where the air is thickest, and are betting their grandchildren will still have something to breathe.

world: A dry, mid-sized world of beige gravel plains and low ridges, with no seas. Its factory cities sprawl across the plains in planned grids, each built round its works and joined to the next by freight roads; two of them still show the burned blocks where the Unwritten bombs fell. Thin dust, little cloud and a trace of frost at the poles.
from_space: Beige desert carved into dense grey city grids that run to the horizon. At night the grids glow in hard white squares, with two dark gaps where the bombed works stand.
moons: None.
people: 6 billion workers and engineers in the factory cities, nearly all employed by the owners who run the world.
story: Desert factory cities that build dumb, sturdy machines with no thinking core, to a standard written so the Unwritten would let them live. The Unwritten bombed two factories anyway. Praevisio buys the output and adds the thinking itself.

world: A temperate living world, landscaped by Alma over ninety years from a cold steppe until every view was right: forests climbing to clean mountain ranges, open plains of farmland, lakes placed where the light falls well, small ice caps. The retreats sit on the best coasts and slopes. The farm towns that feed them are planned grids out on the plains, kept out of sight of any guest.
from_space: Bright green continents and blue sea under unusually clear skies, neat patchwork farmland on the plains. At night the farm towns glow in regular grids, and the retreats show only as soft scattered lights along the coasts.
moons: None.
people: 6.5 billion hands, mostly Contract farmers and Staff grade service workers in planned farm towns, with a few hundred thousand Executive guests in the retreats at any time.
story: Alma's rest world for Executives, reshaped from a cold steppe over ninety years until every view was right. Hands farm food for the retreats and are forbidden to enter them; guests who rest too long are separated quietly.

world: A moist living world of low plains, swampy river valleys and modest hills, once a Lode industrial holding. Jungle has spread over the poisoned plains the Growers reseeded, and the old pit scars are greening over. The ruined factory cities still stand in their planned grids, the smelter roofs held up by vines, and the Growers live in small villages among them.
from_space: Dark green land with rust-brown ruin patches and old pit scars healing into lighter green, under heavy cloud. At night almost nothing: a few faint village lights among the dark grids of the dead cities.
moons: Two moons: a grey cratered rock and a small captured rock.
people: 2 million Growers in small villages among the ruined factory cities.
story: A Lode industrial world abandoned when the ore ran out. Growers moved in, reseeded the poisoned plains and let the jungle eat the factories. Forty years on, the old pit scars are green and vines hold up the smelter roofs.

world: A small airless mountain world, pale tan and white, of sharp ridges and deep valleys, with no water. The guild's docks are cut into the ridge walls, open to vacuum where nothing rusts, and its people live in pressure halls behind the dock walls, grown along the ridges over generations.
from_space: Pale tan and white with sharp grey ridges and no cloud. By night lines of light along the ridge walls where the docks open, with freighters berthed in them.
moons: Two small moons: a captured lump and a cratered grey rock.
people: 2 million free settlers, guild shipwrights and their families in the pressure halls.
story: A shipwrights' guild repairs freighters in airless mountain docks, where nothing rusts, and lives in pressure halls behind the dock walls. Mordant has offered to buy the guild three times; the last offer came with a Subpoena parked overhead.

world: A temperate world, 7,400 km in radius, built over from coast to coast into one planned clinic city, with only small grey-blue seas and a few low hills left. The districts are laid out in rings round the birth clinics, wards and dormitory blocks in cream stone, with a numbering hall at each centre. Little cloud and small ice caps.
from_space: Cream-white city over almost all the land and small grey-blue seas, under a soft blush haze. At night the whole world is lit, the clinic rings brightest.
moons: None.
people: 30 billion hands, most of them born here: clinic staff, nurses, porters and the Contract grade crews who keep the city running.
story: Alma's oldest clinic holding: thirty billion hands, most of them born here and billed before their first breath. Births are scheduled by quarter, and a late birth carries a surcharge. Bona Vell keeps her office in the flagship clinic here, the one Midwife robs most often.
history: Partus was a crowded temperate world when Alma's clinics came to it in the Last Famine, about pre-R 60 to pre-R 40, to feed and treat the starving on Parliament's credit. The clinics never left. At the Receivership in R.0 Alma kept the world as its first clinic holding and named it Partus, birth. When Alma began billing every birth to the newborn in R.31, the clinics here were among the first to send the bill, and they spread until the world was one city from coast to coast. Births are scheduled by quarter, and a late birth carries a surcharge. Vesna Ilić was chosen before birth at Partus in R.178, picked for her face, and onboarded at sixteen as a nurse in the flagship clinic. Bona Vell took Alma's seat in R.191 and moved her office into that same clinic. In R.205 Vesna delivered a girl four minutes after the quarter closed and saw the surcharge printed before the child was washed. She has spat out her pill every morning since, and each week she passes Midwife the list of who is due. The flagship is the clinic he robs most often, and Bona Vell lets every theft run on the news.

world: A small airless world of dusty orange uplands and white salt pans in the low basins, with low worn hills and old craters. Thousands of claims pock the surface, each a hand-dug pit beside a pressure hut sunk into the salt. Nothing is planned: huts cluster wherever a seam ran, and the one town grew round the saloon and the landing field.
from_space: Dusty orange and rust-brown, with bright white salt pans in the basins and the pockmarks of a thousand claims. At night a faint scatter of hut lights across the salt and one brighter knot at the landing field.
moons: Four small moons: a captured lump nearest, a second captured lump, then the largest, a cratered grey-brown rock, and far out a third captured lump. Prospectors have staked claims on the two nearest as well.
people: 400,000 prospectors in pressure huts dug into the salt across their claims, with a few thousand traders and freighter crews at the landing town.
story: An airless rock where anyone can stake a claim, and most do. Prospectors live in pressure huts dug into the salt, mine ore by hand and sell it to whoever's freighter lands first. Lode's offer to buy all the claims is pinned to the saloon wall.

world: A small, dry world of gravel plains and low worn hills, with air too thin to breathe and no surface water at all. The water lies far down, in old aquifers under the gravel, and every well town is built over a shaft: a cluster of sealed halls round a pump head, joined to the next town by a buried pipe. The towns are old and grew outward ring by ring as the shafts went deeper, and the gravel round each one is pocked with spoil heaps from abandoned bores.
from_space: A pale grey-brown ball with no seas and no cloud, its plains marked by faint spoil heaps around the bore sites. At night the well towns show as small, separate points of light, each far from the next.
moons: None.
people: 1.9 million miners and their families in sealed well towns. The well guild holds the wells in common, and every child born on Pedregal is given a share of them at birth.
story: Water is mined from deep under the gravel and sold by the cup in sealed well towns. The well guild gives every child a share of the wells at birth: the one world in the sector where a newborn is owed something rather than owing it.

world: A cold airless world, 3,600 km in radius, of slate-blue lowlands and high ice-grey uplands, cratered and scarred by old cuttings. The free port lives in pressure halls dug under the highlands, grown hall by hall over generations; ships land on pads cut into the cliff edges.
from_space: Slate-blue lowlands and ice-grey highlands. At night a small cluster of landing lights at the highland edge, and the running lights of Runner ships coming and going.
moons: None.
people: 400,000 dockworkers, traders and the harbourmaster's family, in pressure halls under the highlands.
story: A free port on a cold, airless, moonless rock, where Runners refuel off the toll lanes in pressure halls cut under the highlands. Its harbourmaster keeps two sets of books, and the Hand has only ever seen one of them.

world: A dry, airless rock of yellow-grey plains and old craters, with no air and no water on the surface. The gate town is buried in the rock under the old toll gate: tunnels, halls, a brewery and a landing pad cut down into the bedrock by Lode's gate crews and enlarged by their families since. Its streets were dug where the rock was softest, so they wind.
from_space: Bare yellow-grey rock pocked with craters, featureless by day. At night a single small cluster of lights shows round the landing pad, with the gate's beacon blinking above it.
moons: One cratered grey moon.
people: About 4 million: the gatekeepers' families, and the brewers, pad crews and tea-house keepers of the buried town. Every Runner who pays the coin comes down for the ale.
story: Lode closed its toll gate here thirty years ago. The locals kept it open from a buried town under the gate and now charge their own toll, a single small coin, spent on its upkeep. Runners pay it gladly, and drink the ale brewed below.
history: Pennygate began as one of Lode's gates. When Lode built its toll lanes, between the R.50s and the R.70s, it set a gate on this airless rock on the Charter Road, dug a town under it for the gate crews and charged every ship that passed. For more than a century the crews ran the gate, and their families stayed in the tunnels, brewed ale for the pilots and married each other. In R.182, the year the Long Strike began and the Chair was seen in person for the last time, Lode closed the gate and wrote the town off with it. The gatekeepers' families did not leave. They kept the gate open from below and charged their own toll, a single small coin, spent on its upkeep, and the Runners took to it at once. That same year Esme Varn, called Kettle, born in R.149 and a cargo runner round Lode's lanes all her working life, sold her last ship and opened a tea house in the buried town beside the pad. Thirty years on, everything that moves through the lanes passes her kettle first; she runs the Runners' network from her back table, and Midwife hides the children he takes from Alma's clinics in her cellar among the ale barrels until a ship is ready. In R.212 the coin is still small.

world: A frigid mountain world smaller than most, almost all land: steep white ranges over grey valleys of rock and frozen gravel, with a few small frozen seas. Snow falls most of the year. The camps are dug into the snow on the lower slopes, set out in rough lines by the camp committees and added to every week.
from_space: White peaks over grey valleys under broken cloud. By night faint lines of light on the lower slopes, where the camps are.
moons: None.
people: 3 million refugees in camps dug into the snow, hands who fled harvest notices and are still waiting for travel permits; Collective recruiters come through every week.
story: Hands who fled a harvest notice wait in mountain camps dug into the snow, for travel permits that never come. The camp is free, cold and full; the Collective recruits there weekly.

world: A frigid mountain world, 6,200 km in radius, almost all land: high snow-covered ranges, a few frozen seas, and deep dark valleys where hot springs keep the ground bare and steaming. The guards live in the hot-spring valleys under glass roofs; the prisoners sleep in the mine galleries cut into the mountains above.
from_space: White snowfields cut by dark steaming valleys under drifting cloud. At night the glass-roofed valleys glow and the mine mouths show as small lights high on the slopes.
moons: None.
people: 50 million hands, mostly Indentured prisoners working off their debt in the mines, with their Continuity guards.
story: Continuity's labour world: frozen mountains, deep mines, and hot-spring valleys roofed in glass where the guards live. The prisoners sleep in the mine galleries. They are hands who fell too far behind on their debt, and they mine it off at a rate Continuity sets every year.

world: A warm ocean world with almost no dry land: a few sandbars and reef islands in wide turquoise shallows ringed with coral. The one settlement stands on stilts over the reef, a cluster of platforms, desalination tanks and a landing pad, built where the water is shallowest.
from_space: Turquoise shallows and deep blue sea, with pale rings of reef and sand. At night there is one faint light on the reef and nothing else.
moons: One small moon of cratered grey rock.
people: 7,000 reef settlers on the stilt platforms.
story: A tiny settlement on stilts over the reef that desalinates water and sells it to passing Runners. The reef is the only thing here older than the colony, and the settlers will shoot anyone who drops anchor on it.

world: A pale blue gas giant off every lane, with few, faint bands and almost no weather. Nobody lives in its air. Its one moon is a temperate living world of rolling hills, blue lakes and orchards, where small market towns have grown round the cider presses and the one modest port.
from_space: A pale blue gas giant, and beside it a green moon dusted white with blossom in spring, blue lakes scattered through it. At night the moon shows small warm lights round its lakes.
moons: One moon: the living orchard moon of hills and lakes.
people: 15 million orchard townsfolk on the moon.
resources: fruit, cider, wood, from the moon
story: A quiet orchard moon of a giant that pays no tolls because no lane goes there. The townsfolk keep it that way by refusing to build a port big enough for a Hand freighter.

world: A mild world of gentle green hills set with hundreds of lakes, every one of them dyed the same perfect blue by Alma's terraformers, with only small seas and no high mountains. The hills were reshaped too, rounded off so the views have no harsh lines. The resort towns stand on the lake shores, each planned round its promenade, its clinic and its landing lawn.
from_space: Vivid blue lakes scattered across soft green hills, under light fair-weather cloud. At night the lake shores are ringed with soft warm lights and the hills between them are dark.
moons: One pale moon of smooth ice.
people: About 3.4 million: 3 million resort staff, who smile by contract, and around 400,000 guests at a time, executives and their families.
story: Alma's executive resort, its hills shaped and its lakes dyed a perfect blue by Alma's own terraformers. The staff smile by contract, and guests' children are delivered at the clinic by the shore at a family discount.

world: A warm ocean world with land only in low, flat islands ringed by wide white beaches and coral shallows. There are no mountains to speak of and no ice caps, only a light cover of tropical cloud. The fishing towns are small and old, built along the beaches and harbours of the larger islands.
from_space: Sapphire sea scattered with white sand islands and turquoise shallows, under thin tropical cloud. At night only small strings of harbour lights show.
moons: None.
people: 6 million fisherfolk in beach towns; not one island has sold land to Alma.
story: White beaches and warm seas. Alma wants it as a rest world for executives; the fishing towns have refused to sell for twenty years, and Alma is a patient buyer.

world: A cold world smaller than most, a little over half land: wide frost plains and low hills, with thin pine forest in the sheltered valleys and grey seas frozen at the edges. The ice caps are large and the cloud light. The faithful live in small stone villages in the valleys, grown and unplanned, each round a square where fallen Praevisio probes hang as trophies.
from_space: White and grey-green, with dark threads of valley forest and small stone villages. By night only a few dim yellow lights; there are no power lines.
moons: None.
people: 2 million faithful in stone valley villages, farming grain and keeping sheep.
story: The Unwritten broke every machine on this world more complex than a pump. Praevisio's scout probes that fall here are hung in the square as trophies. Visitors leave their devices in orbit, or lose them.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, about half land: rolling hills, wide grain fields and hundreds of lakes, with low worn mountains and small ice caps. Lode strip-mined it and left; the Growers spent two generations rebuilding the soil and filling the lakes, and the old mine benches still show as stepped hillsides under the wheat. The villages are small and grown, clustered on the lake shores, with no road wider than a cart.
from_space: Golden fields and green hedged hills round many blue lakes, with white cloud in the mid latitudes and small polar caps. By night it is almost dark: faint lamp-lit villages, and in autumn the pilgrims' fires along the shores.
moons: None.
people: 3 million Growers in lakeside villages, joined each autumn by tens of thousands of Unwritten pilgrims who come for the harvest and leave after it.
story: Lode stripped this world and left; the Growers brought back its fields and lakes over two generations. They refuse every machine and bring in the grain by hand. Each autumn Unwritten pilgrims arrive by the thousand to help, and the Dust call the bread holy and buy it anyway.

world: A dry world a little larger than most, of purple-red mountains, white salt basins and no open water. The exchange cities fill the basins below the ranges, planned and dense, their halls built to hold freighter captains by the thousand.
from_space: Purple-red rock and white salt basins under clear dry air. By night the exchange cities blaze white in the basins, the brightest lights in the sector.
moons: Two moons, both cratered grey rock.
people: About 2 billion hands, mostly Staff grade, in the exchange cities; tens of thousands of freighter captains wait in the halls on any given morning.
story: Lode's freight exchange, where the toll on every lane is set each morning. Freighter captains from across the galaxy wait in its halls for prices that decide whether their families eat.

world: A temperate ocean world about 6,600 km in radius, with only about a seventh of its surface land: long mountainous islands and one narrow continent ringed with harbours. Eleven great harbour cities, old and grown, fill the best bays, and their suburbs run along every coast between them. The inland hills are terraced for vines and orchards. Weather comes off the sea in long fronts.
from_space: Blue sea laced with bright coastal cities along every shore, green and brown island interiors, and long bands of frontal cloud. At night the coasts are drawn in light, eleven bright knots joined by unbroken strings.
moons: One large grey moon, a cratered rock, big in the night sky; it drives the tides and nothing else.
people: 3 billion free citizens, nearly all in the eleven harbour cities and the coastal towns between them; a third of the young talk like Alma's adverts.
story: The largest free world in the sector, governed by eleven harbour cities that argue for months over everything. Alma pays its broadcasters to run its shows for free, and a third of the young already talk like the adverts.

world: A warm gas giant of sorrel-red and cream bands with two small storms. The free port floats at the breathable layer on hot-gas cells: a cluster of dock decks, fuel tanks and warehouses round a central exchange, with skimmer lines hanging from its underside into the cloud. It has grown by bolting new docks onto the old ones, so its shape is a lopsided star.
from_space: Sorrel-red and cream bands with two small red-brown storms. At night the port is one bright cluster of light on the clouds, its docks reaching out in uneven arms.
moons: Two moonlets, both small captured rocks.
people: About 12 million traders and dockhands in the floating port, run by the merchants' exchange, which keeps very careful records of which executives refuel here.
story: A free port held up by hot-gas cells at the breathable layer, between Lode's refinery worlds, selling untaxed fuel skimmed from the clouds under its docks. The Hand tolerates it because half the executives in the sector refuel here off the books, and the port keeps very careful records of which half.

world: A small airless world of blue-grey rock, heavily cratered, with no water. Its one city fills a giant crater under a roof of plates and struts, the docks at the rim and the dock families' streets below, grown over centuries without a plan.
from_space: Blue-grey cratered rock with a single bright sprawl inside one huge crater, its roof glinting in the sun. By night the crater glows like a lamp, with ships' lights circling it.
moons: One small captured moon, a dark knobbly lump of grooved rock. No rings.
people: 4 million dock families under the crater roof; the dockhands' guild runs the port, and the harbourmaster is the oldest of them still working.
story: A free port roofed over a giant crater, where no hold is ever opened. The harbourmaster is the oldest dockhand still working, and nobody has dared ask the current one her age. Cargo passes through unrecorded, which is the whole business.

world: A cold airless world, 5,400 km in radius, of dark grey rock, low ridges and old craters, with ice lying in the shadowed craters near both poles. The barracks are buried deep under the rock against bombardment and laid out in strict grids; the surface shows only gun pits, landing fields and blast doors.
from_space: Dark grey with bright ice caps at both poles. At night only thin grid lines of light around the landing fields.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock with no use. No rings.
people: 50 million hands, mostly Pacifiers and their officers, in buried barracks.
story: Continuity's garrison guarding Ferraria's yards, its barracks buried under the dark rock against bombardment. Its soldiers outnumber the yard crews they guard, and both sides know whom they are guarding against.

world: A wet world a little smaller than most: rain-soaked uplands, wide bogs and small slate-blue seas, with low worn hills and heavy cloud most of the year. The ranges are laid out on the uplands in numbered blocks, cratered by live fire and scarred by tracks, and the grave terraces climb the hillsides beside the range camps.
from_space: Slate-blue seas and dark green bog under long grey rain bands, the uplands pocked and scarred brown where the ranges are. By night only the range camps show, small planned rectangles of light.
moons: None.
people: About 12,000 range staff, plus whichever Tranche is on trial, which can add tens of thousands for a quarter.
resources: test ranges, salvage from wrecked robots
story: A wet, empty proving ground where Continuity matches Tranche squads against Praevisio's Proxies in live-fire trials. Praevisio publishes the results each quarter; Continuity disputes every one, and the grave terraces keep growing.
history: Probatio was farmed once, by settlers who could never make the bogs pay, and it was nearly empty when Continuity bought it as a wet-weather training ground for the Tranches. In the R.150s Praevisio began selling the Board its drones and Proxies as the end of human soldiers, and the two fingers needed a place to settle which was cheaper. Probatio became that place: Tranche squads against Proxies in live fire, with Praevisio scoring the trials and publishing the results each quarter. Continuity disputes every one. The dead are buried on terraces cut into the hillsides beside the ranges, and the terraces keep growing. In R.188 a twelve-year-old from Alma's heavy-lift line, grown for Continuity to load munitions, came in a cargo harness to load the ranges; he is called Pignus now. In R.200 Praevisio ran a trial of his loading crew against a heavy-lift Proxy. The crew lost by four percent, Continuity cancelled the line, and his batch-mates were separated ahead of schedule. The range crews still call him the first man the robots made redundant.

world: A frigid world a little smaller than most, of black conifer forest, thousands of frozen lakes and cold grey seas, with ice caps reaching far toward the middle latitudes. The heated towns sit between the lakes on a perfect grid, every street and room laid out so that the cameras see all of it.
from_space: Dark green forest broken by white frozen lakes, grey seas and wide ice at both ends. By night the towns glow in evenly spaced grids, every street the same brightness, all night long.
moons: None.
people: About 800 million hands, every one of them observed, in the heated grid towns between the lakes; each is paid a small bonus to behave normally.
story: Praevisio's forecast lab: a whole world of hands lives under total observation in heated towns between the frozen lakes, so the machine can test its forecasts on them. They are paid a small bonus to behave normally, and nobody is sure any more what normal was.
history: Prognosis was a cold timber and fishing world, settled long before the Receivership and of no interest to anyone until Praevisio was built in R.132. The new machine needed a population it could watch completely, to test its forecasts against before it sold them, and within a few years the Board had sold it Prognosis whole. The towns were rebuilt on grids between the frozen lakes, with cameras in every room and monitor patches issued at birth, and the people were paid a small bonus to behave normally. Within a generation nobody could say any more what normal had been. Pythia Kallos was born there in R.157 and wore the patches on her wrists from birth. By ten she could tell from the size of her bonus what the machine had expected of her that week. At seventeen, in R.174, Praevisio hired her off the world as the only subject who had ever worked out what was being tested, and she now heads its Auditors. Every forecast Praevisio sells is still tried on Prognosis first.

world: A cold world smaller than most, of high cliffs, glaciers and ice caves, with a little open sea near the equator in summer. The vault is cut deep into one great glacier so the ice cools its machines, and the technicians live in planned halls in the ice beside them. Listening masts stand on the cliff tops above.
from_space: White glaciers and blue ice with dark cliff walls standing out of them. By night one small, precise grid of light at a glacier's edge.
moons: None.
people: About 8,000 hands, Staff-grade technicians, living in the ice vault with the machines they keep.
story: Praevisio's cold vault, cut into the glaciers so the ice cools its machines; its technicians live in the ice with them. It sits one jump from Fallow and listens to it. The Unwritten pray for the day the ice melts.

world: A volcanic world of black lava plains, ash fields and young cones, with no open water. The port stands on one old shield of rock that has not flowed in a century, rising out of the plains like an island, which is why its people call themselves islanders. The docks and towns on the shield are sealed against the ash and packed tight, built up rather than out round the landing basins.
from_space: Black and dark grey plains with glowing orange cracks and plumes of grey ash drifting downwind from the cones. At night the port shield is a single dense knot of light ringed by the orange glow of the plains.
moons: None.
people: About 30 million islanders and dock crews in sealed port towns on the shield, run by the harbour guilds; when the mountain wakes, Hand crews and Runners wait out the ash in port together.
story: A free port built on the one old shield of rock that has not flowed in a century, its docks sealed against the ash. When the mountain wakes, the harbour shuts and every ship in port, Hand or Runner, waits out the ash together.

world: A warm tropical world of high green mountains and deep blue oceans, with farmland on the coastal plains and in the wide valleys. The mountains are full of iron, and their flanks are opened by rust-red mine cuts that stain the rivers below. The great port lies on a sheltered bay at the foot of the richest range, its yards building ore haulers along kilometres of slipways, and the city round it has climbed the slopes without a plan.
from_space: Green mountains and deep blue sea under heavy tropical cloud, with rust-red mine scars on the ranges. At night the port city is a dense bright sprawl round its bay, with the yard lights strung along the shore and smaller towns down the coast.
moons: Two cratered grey moons.
people: 5 billion, crowded into the port city and the coastal plains: yard crews, miners, farmers and the port authority that runs them.
story: Tropical mountains full of iron, a busy port and yards that build ore haulers for free worlds across the sector. Lode and Mordant both want it, and the port plays them off against each other.

world: A hot tropical world of jungle islands in a warm sea, from steep volcanic peaks inland to wide mangrove swamps on the coasts; the islands cover about a sixth of the surface. The island towns are old and crowded along the coasts, and the dredged islands are ringed with brown silt where the shallows have died.
from_space: Emerald islands in a turquoise sea, with brown silt plumes trailing from the dredged coasts. At night the island towns glow along every coast.
moons: One moon of cratered grey rock.
people: 2 billion islanders under rival chiefs, packed along the coasts.
story: Jungle islands whose mangrove mud holds a rare earth Lode wants. The island chiefs license the dredging one island at a time, and each island blames the next for the dead shallows.

world: A large gas giant, banded in rust-orange, ochre and brick red, with fast narrow belts and a few small storms. Lode's refinery decks hang in the upper cloud on engines that burn the gas they skim, set out in long planned rows that hold their height and never land.
from_space: Rust-orange bands under a faint orange haze, with two plated toll stations in close orbit and a queue of freighters strung out between them. By night the refinery decks show as rows of white light on the dark bands, with flare plumes beside them.
moons: No natural moons. Two captured rocks have been plated over as toll stations: steel-clad, lit at every window, with docking towers standing out from their rims.
people: 900 million hands, mostly Staff grade: about 600 million on the refinery decks and 300 million on the two toll stations.
story: Lode's toll station where the Long Haul crosses the Charter Road. A thousand freighters a day pay here and fill up with gas from the refinery decks below; the founding manager named it after fool's gold as a joke that nobody now tells.
history: Pyrite was only a gas giant at a crossing until Lode built its toll lanes between the R.50s and the R.70s. Where the Long Haul crosses the Charter Road, every ship bound for the capital or the outer rim has to pass, and Lode put its toll station here: two captured rocks plated over in close orbit, and refinery decks in the cloud below to sell fuel to the ships it had just charged. The founding manager named the holding Pyrite, fool's gold, as a joke about anyone who thought the lanes would stay free. Nobody tells the joke now. A thousand freighters a day pay here and fill up from the decks, which hold their height on engines that burn the gas they skim; a deck that loses power falls, and Lode replaces it. The name has been handed out as a work name too: Lode named Ivo Hartmann Pyrite at onboarding, years before he founded the first Grower commune, and he never liked it. Since R.201, when Praevisio named the defaulter collective, Lode has added a security surcharge to every toll here, and haulers call it the Table tax. Not all Runner fuel passes Pyrite's meters: much of it comes from Sourwater, the next stop down the lane, where nobody reads a meter. In the war the crossing is the most watched point on the Long Haul, and Runner crews bound for the Charter Road go a long way round it.

world: A small dry world cut into high plateaus by a maze of deep, wind-cut gorges, the deepest of them called the Narrows. There is no open water and almost no cloud; wind and dust do the weather. The canyon towns are built into and hung from the gorge walls, grown one platform at a time, and nothing is laid out on the plateau tops.
from_space: Ochre and burnt orange plateaus veined with dark ravines, with pale dust blowing off the rims. At night only thin threads of light show, the canyon towns along the gorge walls.
moons: None.
people: 800,000 canyon dwellers in towns hung from the gorge walls, many of them Dust pilots and Runner crews between runs.
story: Its canyon towns hang from the walls above a maze of gorges no drone has mapped twice. Dust pilots earn their name here by running the Narrows at night with their lights off; the canyon floor keeps the ones who fail.

world: A warm hill world a little smaller than most, once bare rock and now greened by Alma: about seventy percent land, folded into steep hills terraced from valley floor to crest with tea, and perfume gardens on the lower slopes. Small warm seas lie between the hill country, and soft cloud gathers most afternoons. Alma laid out the rest houses along the ridgelines; the pickers' villages grew up in the valleys below them.
from_space: Green terraced hills combed into fine contour lines under soft white cloud, with small blue seas between them. By night scattered warm lights along the ridges where the rest houses are, and dimmer clusters in the valleys.
moons: None.
people: 400 million hands, service staff: pickers, cooks, gardeners and attendants in the valley villages, and a few hundred thousand Executives on rest in the ridge houses at any time.
story: Alma greened these bare hills for its Executives: tea terraces and rest houses where they come to recover from their work. The pickers sing on Alma's orders; silence on the slopes is reported.

world: A cold, ordinary-sized world, a little under half land, of mountains and high plateaus under ice, with grey seas between them and ice caps reaching far toward the equator. Alma is warming the highlands one valley a decade, and the warmed valleys show as dark blue-green pockets with lakes. Each holds a planned casting town of studios, crèches and schools laid out round a broadcast mast.
from_space: White peaks and ice caps over dark blue-green highland valleys and steel-blue seas, with soft cloud over the warmed valleys. By night the valley towns glow in tidy rings of light, each round the red point of its mast.
moons: One moon of smooth bright ice, cracked and almost free of craters; it hangs in the background of half of Alma's evening broadcasts.
people: 900 million hands, Staff and Contract grade, in the warmed valley towns: voice and face trainers, crèche staff, studio crews and the children being graded.
story: Every soothing face and voice on Alma's news is cast here, in highland towns Alma is warming out from under the ice, a valley a decade. Children are graded for warmth of voice at six. The ones who fail are sent to the call centres.
history: Quieta was a cold fishing and mining world when the Receivership began, with a few towns in its sheltered valleys. Alma took it as a holding after the happiness pill went out in R.88, when its news needed faces and voices to sell the pill to every world, and found that the valley children sang well in the thin cold air. It began warming the highlands soon after, one valley a decade, and built a casting town in each. Every child born there, and many shipped in from Alma's clinics, is graded at six for warmth of voice. Those who pass go into Alma's crèches and train for the screen; those who fail are sent to the call centres to read debt notices. Placida Ren, whose face Alma chose before she was born, was graded here in R.174 and passed with most of her crèche. Twenty years later she heard a voice from the failed half on a collection line and knew it. Every soothing face and voice on Alma's news is cast here now. The thaw goes on, and the newest valleys are still bare rock with greenhouses.

world: A dry world smaller than most, its air turned thick and poison yellow by a failed atmosphere job: no open water, bare brown and ochre rock, and long dark valley scars where the old processing plants ran. The nine sealed domes stand together in one deep valley and share one air plant, built and patched by hand over two centuries, with no plan beyond the pipes between them.
from_space: Mustard-yellow haze over the whole world, thick enough to hide most of the ground, with dark valley scars showing through. By night the nine domes are one small cluster of light in the haze.
moons: None.
people: 1.5 million in nine sealed domes in one valley; most work the chemical works and the filter shops, and every one of them depends on the air plant.
story: A Republic atmosphere job went wrong here and left air nobody can breathe. Nine sealed domes share one air plant in a poisoned valley; whoever holds the valves runs the planet, and the valves have changed hands four times in ten years.
history: Rauchtal was a dry, thin-aired world when settlers came during the Republic. In the Republic's last century Parliament paid a contractor, on credit, to thicken the air and make the valleys farmable, and the contractor built processing plants along every valley. The chemistry went wrong. The air thickened, but into a poison yellow haze nobody can breathe. When the Republic defaulted in pre-R 1 the payments stopped, and the contractor stopped work and left with the plants still running. The settlers who stayed sealed themselves into domes in the one valley where the plants had died first, and built a single air plant to feed them all. There are nine domes now. The Hand has never wanted the world: the only yield is filters and chemicals, and the air would cost more to fix than the planet is worth. So Rauchtal belongs to whoever holds the valves of the air plant, because whoever holds them can stop any dome breathing. The valves have changed hands four times in the last ten years. A dome workers' council holds them now, and keeps a guard of nine on the valve room, one from each dome.

world: A rust-banded gas giant of turbulent red and brown belts with a few small storms. The old prison barge is moored in its cloud tops: a long grey hull hung from its own lift cells, its guard decks empty since Continuity left. The former prisoners still sleep in its cells and fly out to the red moon each shift to mine.
from_space: Rust-red and dark brown bands with four moons, one of them deep red. At night a single short line of lights marks the barge on the clouds.
moons: Four moons: the red ore moon, a cratered rock stained red with iron, which the former prisoners mine; a dark ice-rock; a hazy orange moon; and a small captured lump.
people: 600 former prisoners, living aboard the barge and working the red moon's ore, which they sell to the Runners at their own price.
story: Continuity closed the prison barge moored in its cloud tops as 'below target' and took the guards home, but not the prisoners. Six hundred of them still sleep aboard, fly out to the red moon each shift to mine its ore, and sell it to the Runners at their own price.

world: A tidally locked world, 6,200 km in radius. Its day side is burnt red-black rock where the smiths dig iron; its night side is ice. Between them runs a band of red savannah cut by deep canyons and dotted with swamps and small twilight seas, and the ranch towns are spread thin along it, grown where the water is. Herds cross the canyons on cable bridges.
from_space: A rust-red and olive twilight band cracked by dark canyons, between a burnt brown-black day side and a white night side. Along the band's dim edge, a thin scatter of ranch-town lights.
moons: Two moons, both cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 60 million free ranchers, smiths and their families, along the twilight band.
story: Red savannah, canyons and swamps run in a band between a burnt day side, where the smiths dig iron, and a frozen night. Ranchers move herds across the canyons on cable bridges. Their blades are famous; the Hand banned their export, which doubled the price.

world: A temperate, rather moist world of wide flat plains with no seas, only rivers, ponds and wet hollows. Lode scraped the topsoil off whole regions and left bare brown subsoil scored with its old cutting lanes. The Growers' seed beds spread out from the river valleys in uneven green patches. The hills are low, the poles carry thin frost, and the commune villages are small and unplanned, strung along the rivers; the Kiru farm a valley of their own upstream.
from_space: Bare brown earth in broad strips and squares, with green spreading over it in ragged patches along the rivers. At night a faint scatter of village lights follows the water.
moons: None.
people: 1.2 million Growers in river villages, and a few hundred Kiru exiles farming their own valley apart from them.
story: Growers replant plains Lode stripped for topsoil, one seed bed at a time. They use Lode's old survey stakes, still stamped EXHAUSTED, as fence posts. A small Kiru exile community farms beside them, and keeps apart.

world: A cold, snowy world of ordinary size, with long winters and short grey summers. Most of the land lies under snow over glacier ice; about a fifth of the surface is cold dark sea that freezes along its coasts. The compounding plants stand in a few planned towns on the coast, their vats sunk under the snow to keep them cold, with the workers' blocks downwind.
from_space: White, streaked with pale blue glacier ice, with dark grey sea along a ragged coast. By night a handful of small planned towns glow on the shore. Two moons, one grey and one bright.
moons: Two moons: a grey cratered rock close in, and a smooth bright ice moon further out. No rings.
people: 55 million hands, Staff chemists and Contract plant workers, in planned coastal plant towns; their burns are treated with the cheap gel from Ilha Verde.
story: Alma's healing gel is compounded here, in cold vats under the snow. The plant workers cannot afford a jar of what they make, and their burns are treated with the cheap copy from Ilha Verde.

world: A small temperate world, 5,200 km in radius, landscaped by Alma: gentle forested hills, hundreds of warm lakes and shallow blue seas covering about two-fifths of it, no high mountains and small ice caps. The lodges are spaced along the lake shores on a planned pattern, each out of sight of the next.
from_space: Soft green forest and pale blue lakes and seas under light cloud. At night faint, evenly spaced lodge lights.
moons: Two moons: a smooth pale ice moon and a cream frozen-plains moon with a faint rust band. No rings.
people: 10 million hands, mostly Staff grade lodge staff, and a few thousand Executive guests.
story: Alma landscaped this world for its executives, all quiet forest lodges and warm lakes. A smile that slips three times in a season sends its owner back to the clinic for retraining, and nobody describes the retraining.

world: A dry, quiet gas giant about 45,000 km in radius, banded in bare tan and brown with one small rust storm. Nobody lives in its clouds. Its one forested moon is the only living place in the system: a world of dense resin trees, a few lakes and low hills, where the tappers' camps sit along the forest roads.
from_space: Bare tan-brown bands beside a bright green moon. At night the moon shows a few faint camp lights.
moons: One moon, a forested living world, bright green with a few small lakes. No rings.
people: 200,000 free tappers and their families, all on the forest moon.
story: The only living place in the system is the giant's forest moon, where tappers bleed a resin that Alma uses in its cosmetics. Alma pays by the barrel, and sets the size of the barrel each season.

world: A cold tidally locked world, 6,100 km in radius. Iron-red scrub covers the twilight band under low grey cloud; the day face is scorched rock cut by the quarry benches where inmates work short shifts, and the night face is ice, where the discipline camps are. The prison towns are strung along the twilight in strict lines of identical blocks.
from_space: A brick-red twilight band under grey cloud, between a scorched face scarred by quarries and a frozen white face. Along the band, straight lines of camp lights.
moons: One moon, a small cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 62 million: 60 million inmate hands and 2 million Pacifiers guarding them, in prison towns along the twilight.
story: Continuity's labour prison for the sector, strung along the twilight. Inmates quarry the burnt day face in short shifts and are sent to the night face for discipline. Sentences are served by adding years to their Birth Debt, and parole is set by a Praevisio forecast. Nobody has been paroled early since; the Board considers this a success.

world: A temperate river world a little smaller than most, mostly wet lowland: broad slow rivers, rice terraces on the low hills and small blue seas where the rivers end. Mountains are few and low, and the ice caps are small. The river towns grew along the banks without a plan, each with a square at its centre where the lot is drawn.
from_space: Green-brown lowlands laced with silver rivers and dotted with small blue seas, under scattered white cloud. By night the towns trace the rivers in dotted lines of light.
moons: None.
people: About 90 million, in river towns and rice villages along the main waterways.
story: Every year its river towns draw lots for a governor, who serves one year and may never stand again. Once the lot fell on a Hand informant. He resigned in a week, citing the workload.

world: A temperate world of forested mountains and long parallel valleys, with narrow seas between the ranges. Its forests were planted in straight rows by a colonial company three centuries ago, and the rows still run for hundreds of kilometres along the ridges, each family's stretch known by name. The forester towns lie in the valley bottoms, small and old, built wherever the first planters camped.
from_space: Dark green ridges in long parallel stripes, separated by paler valleys and narrow blue seas. At night only scattered small lights show along the valley floors.
moons: None.
people: 28 million forester families in valley towns, each selling Lode only the timber its own family planted.
story: Its forests were planted in straight rows by a colonial company that went bust three centuries ago. Every family knows which rows were their great-grandparents' work, and they sell Lode only the timber their own family planted.

world: A warm, wet, low world a little smaller than most, half shallow water and half reed marsh, with almost no hills and no ice. Brown channels braid through vast reed beds that are cut and regrow each season. The cutters live in grown villages of thatch on raised mounds beside the sugar-boiling sheds; the only planned thing on the planet is Lode's weighing station at the landing field.
from_space: Bright green reed beds cut by a maze of brown channels and shallow brown-green water, under warm haze and broken cloud, with low smudges of smoke from the boiling sheds. By night dim scattered lamp lights and one sharp white square at the weighing station.
moons: None.
people: 15 million reed cutters and boilers in thatched mound villages across the marshes.
story: Lode leases the reed-sugar marshes to free cutters at a rate that leaves them exactly even every year. In sixty years nobody has turned a profit, and nobody has quite starved.

world: A volcanic world a little smaller than most, with no sea, its crust broken into plates of scorched forest by glowing rifts. Every few years a quake opens a new rift, swallows whatever stands on it and exposes fresh ore. The towns are grown and temporary, built on stilts and skids among the last forests so they can be dragged clear when the ground moves.
from_space: Dark green-black forest plates split by glowing orange rifts, with grey smoke along the fresh cracks. By night the rifts glow like veins, and the towns show as small clusters of light close beside them, where the new ore is.
moons: One cratered moon, a grey rock.
people: 3.7 million settlers in mining towns on stilts and skids, moving with the ground.
story: The crust here cracks open every few years and swallows a town. Each quake also exposes fresh ore, so the settlers build on stilts and skids among the last forests, mine the new cracks, and drag what is left of the town somewhere else.

world: A deep ocean world about 7,400 km in radius, with almost no land: a few bare rock islets and shoals, about two percent of the surface. The oil rigs stand in the deep sea over the old fields, hundreds of them, each a town on stilts with its refinery on deck. Long swells and frequent storms cross the open ocean.
from_space: Deep blue sea under thin bands of cloud, with no coastline to speak of. At night the rigs show as scattered points of light across the ocean, some burning flare gas orange.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock.
people: 3 million rig families on hundreds of rig towns, descended from the crews left behind when their company went bankrupt before the Receivership.
story: An ocean world of deep-sea oil rigs left by a company that went bankrupt before the Receivership. The rig crews' descendants still pump the oil, refine it on deck and sell it to anyone who docks.

world: A small frozen world with no open water, all ice fields of glassy crystal that crack into long blue fractures over a rock core, which rises in a few low ridges. The air is thin and clear, with almost no cloud. The Dust families live in heated tunnels under the fields, so nothing stands on the surface but the mine heads and a landing field.
from_space: Glittering white with blue fractures, almost cloudless. By night it is dark but for a few dozen points of light in lines along the fractures, where the mine heads are.
moons: Two moons: a dark ice-rock and a smooth bright ice moon.
people: 40,000 Dust families in heated tunnels under the crystal fields.
story: The ice holds a crystal that keeps time better than any clock. Dust crews live in heated tunnels under the fields and mine it for the navigation cores of every ship, Hand or Collective, and the Unwritten still argue whether a clock counts as a thinking machine.

world: A warm, wet world of ordinary size and almost flat: a few shallow seas, and between them river deltas that braid out for thousands of kilometres over peat bog and mangrove. There are no real mountains, only low clay ridges, and hardly any ice. The stilt towns stand along the main channels, grown plank by plank over generations and never planned.
from_space: By day an olive and brown-green marsh under a constant yellowish haze, the channels showing as dull bronze threads. By night the stilt towns are faint scattered sparks, and on funeral nights strings of lit rafts drift down the channels toward the sea.
moons: None.
people: About 22 million delta folk, in stilt towns along the main channels and fishing camps on the peat banks; a few thousand Runners come and go.
resources: peat fuel, river rice, smuggled goods
story: Stilt towns over a vast delta of peat and mangrove. The dead are set adrift downriver on lit rafts, and Runners use the burning nights to slip cargo past Hand pickets.

world: A warm, wet world of ordinary size, half land, almost all of it murky jungle and swamp drained by wide brown rivers. The companies' towns are old, unplanned river towns on the levees, with drill grounds hacked out of the jungle behind them and a tavern on every landing.
from_space: Dark green under hazy cloud, with wide brown rivers coiling to the sea. By night the river towns light up in strings along the banks. One dark moon.
moons: One moon, a dark ice-rock with bright ice splashed round its craters. No rings.
people: 300 million swamp folk in river towns; about one adult in ten serves in a mercenary company at any time, for Continuity one season and the Runners the next.
story: Its swamp companies fight for Continuity one season and the Runners the next. They keep a scoreboard of both contracts on the same tavern wall.

world: The largest rock of a belt of hollowed rocks round a small orange star, about 3,000 km across, airless, cratered and riddled with tunnels. Its pressure docks are cut into the walls of its biggest crater, and every smaller rock in the belt is somebody's claim, hollowed out for a workshop, a fuel store or a home. There is no weather, only dust thrown up by landings.
from_space: Glittering grey rock pocked with craters and the dark mouths of tunnels, inside a faint ring of brownish belt dust, with the orange star beyond. At night the dock crater glows, and pin-points of light mark claimed rocks across the belt.
moons: Four captured rocks drawn in from the belt, all small knobbly lumps, each one claimed and hollowed; and a faint ring of belt dust, fed by the innermost.
people: 40,000 rock-holders, about half on the big rock round the docks and the rest scattered through the belt in claimed rocks; Runner and Dust crews come and go.
story: A belt of hollowed rocks round a small orange star, the best repair stop in the sector; the biggest rock holds the pressure docks. Rocks belong to whoever lands on them first and can still hold them a month later.

world: A temperate world, 6,100 km in radius, of meadows and low hills laced with rivers and lakes that run pink with a harmless algae; the shallow seas are pink too, nearest the river mouths. Light cloud and mild winters. The dye towns are old guild towns grown along the rivers, their vats on the banks.
from_space: Green land laced with pink rivers and pink lakes beside rose-tinged seas. At night strings of town lights along the rivers.
moons: None.
people: 700 million free settlers, dyers, weavers and river farmers, in guild towns along the rivers.
story: Its rivers and lakes run pink with a harmless algae, and the dyers' guilds steep their cloth in them. Alma's design studios have offered to buy the dye recipes. The settlers suspect Alma already took them.

world: A cold ocean world of ordinary size, with only a little land: rocky islands and broken coasts cut by fjords, under frequent storms. The ice caps are large, and in winter pack ice reaches far down. The fishing towns are grown and huddled in the fjord heads, their boats moored in long lines.
from_space: Slate-grey seas, white coasts and white polar ice under heavy grey cloud. By night small clusters of light at the fjord heads, and in the season a long line of boat lights strung out at sea, together.
moons: None.
people: 20 million fishing families in fjord towns; the fleets go out and come back together.
story: A cold fishing world where the fleets go out together and come back together. A captain who leaves a boat behind is never allowed to sail again.
history: Rosvik was settled by refugees of the Last Famine, about pre-R 50, who fled crowded worlds whose harvests had failed and chose the coldest sea they could reach, because a sea cannot fail the way a field does. The first fleets fished the storms in hulls the Republic's navy had sold off. In pre-R 44, the famine's last winter, a storm caught the whole fleet off the northern ice. The captains of the fast boats ran for the fjords and left the slow ones behind, and four hundred crews froze in the pack ice. The survivors made the law that still rules the world: the fleets go out together and come back together, and a captain who leaves a boat behind never sails again. Rosvik's council is the captains who have never broken it. Under the Receivership the world sold fish and fish oil to the capital through Lode's freighters and kept its law to itself. Lode has twice offered it a fleet of factory ships, and the captains have twice asked whether the factory ships come back together, and never heard an answer they liked. In R.212, with open war, Rosvik's boats have already gone out once to bring in a Collective crew adrift in the pack ice after a fight, because the law says a boat, not a Rosvik boat. The Hand fined the council for it, and the council paid.

world: A hot desert world of red canyons, rock spires and wide dune basins, with no surface water. The castaway families live in the shade of the deepest canyon walls, in shelters built from the hulls of ships the ring brought down, and their settlements follow the canyon floors wherever water seeps out of the rock.
from_space: Red canyons and orange dunes under a wide, glittering ring of rubble that lays a dark band of shadow across the planet. At night the ring still catches sunlight high over the dark ground, and a few small fires show in the canyons.
moons: A wide ring of hundreds of moonlets and rubble, grey and rust-coloured, with lanes only local pilots know; the eight biggest moonlets are captured rocks circling just outside it.
people: About 4,500 castaways, descendants of crashed crews, in canyon shelters; they live on salvage and on piloting newcomers through the ring, for a fee set by mood.
story: A crowded ring of moonlets wrecks careless ships. The descendants of crashed crews live in the shade of the canyon walls, salvage the wrecks and pilot newcomers through the ring, for a fee set by mood.

world: A toxic desert of dark rust plains and old factory districts under polluted air, with low hills and dry riverbeds. The factory cities were built in Lode's strict grids and still stand, mostly empty. The scavengers live sealed inside a few of the great halls, and the stacks burn on because nobody remembers how to shut them down.
from_space: Brown smog over dark rust plains, the grid scars of the factory districts, and the flares of burning stacks. At night the stacks glow through the smog in rows, with dim light from the few sealed halls still lived in.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock.
people: 1 million scavengers living in sealed factory halls and breathing through filters.
resources: scrap, machine parts, cheap industrial goods
story: An abandoned factory world Lode walked away from. A million scavengers live in the sealed factory halls, breathe through filters and run machines nobody pays for; the stacks still burn because nobody remembers how to shut them down.

world: A hot desert world smaller than most, with no open water: most of it is flat white salt pan, hard enough to land on, edged with brown gravel and low eroded hills. It almost never rains, and the heat shimmers over the pan all day. The digger families live in grown clusters of dug-out houses at the edges of the pan, by the few wells.
from_space: Dazzling white salt with brown edges and almost no cloud. By night nearly dark, with small clusters of light at the wells and the faint landing lights of Runner crews out on the pan.
moons: None.
people: 90,000 salt diggers and Runners: about 80,000 in the digger families at the wells and some 10,000 Runner crew passing through at any time.
story: A salt-flat world where Runner crews land on the hard pan because no Hand patrol can tell one track from another. The salt diggers ask no questions and sell water by the cup.

world: A large temperate world, 9,500 km in radius, mostly low rolling grassland, with shallow seas on under a third of it and only a few worn hill ranges. Its long seasons sweep colour across the grass: yellow in the warm belt, red behind it, violet toward the poles, and the bands shift as the year turns. Herding camps and farm towns are spread thinly over all of it, grown along rivers and drove roads, with no planned city anywhere.
from_space: Broad bands of yellow, red and violet grass between shallow blue seas, under light cloud. At night a fine, even scatter of farm-town lights with no great cities.
moons: Five small moons: a cratered grey rock, a small captured lump, a second cratered rock, a dark ice-rock and another captured lump. No rings.
people: 12 billion free farmers and herders, spread across the grasslands in herding camps and farm towns, each district governing itself.
story: Endless grassland that turns yellow, red and violet with the seasons, home to billions of free herders and grain farmers. They pay the Hand a lane tax and nothing else, and every Board meeting someone proposes changing that.

world: A dry world a little larger than most, with no open water anywhere. Broad nitrate plains crusted tan and white run up to ridges of copper-bearing mountains streaked rust and green, and the old lake beds have dried into flat white salt. Rain almost never falls, and in the hot season dust blows off the plains for weeks. The mine towns are old and grown, strung along the ore roads at the foot of the ridges; only the cooperative's rail yards beside the lane port are laid out in a grid.
from_space: By day, tan and ochre plains, rust-green ridges, white salt pans and the pale gouges of open-cut mines, under a thin dust haze and almost no cloud. By night, a loose chain of orange town lights along the ore roads and one bright knot at the lane port where Lode's freight yards stand.
moons: None.
people: 700 million miners, smelter crews and traders, in old mine towns along the ore roads and round the lane port.
story: Saltpetre and copper pour out of its dry plains on the Long Haul. Lode charges the toll to leave and sets the price to buy, and the miners' cooperative calls that holding both ends of the rope.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most whose seas Lode drained, leaving white salt flats in the old basins and dry canyons where the rivers used to run. Salt marsh is spreading back along the old shorelines, a green fringe round each white basin. The Growers' sod huts stand in loose rings at the edge of the green, unplanned, moved outward every year as the marsh grows.
from_space: White salt plains in the old sea basins, edged with thin bands of new green marsh, between tan and brown canyon country. By night almost nothing: a few lamp-lit rings of huts along one shore, and the dark head of the poisoned mine.
moons: None.
people: About 6,000 Grower settlers, in sod huts at the edge of the salt marsh along the old shorelines.
story: Lode drained the seas here and left the planet as salt flats. The Growers are bringing it back one marsh at a time, planting salt grass in the brine of the old shorelines and living in sod huts at the edge of the green. Nobody lived here ten years ago. Now six thousand do.
history: Saltgreen had seas once. Lode drained them for their salts and left the planet as salt flats, and by the end the only water left came up the deep wells of a single mine. Mateus Kale, a Lode water engineer and a Grower in secret, was posted there to run them. In R.201 he poured a salt into the wells that would ruin the water for Lode and leave the old shorelines alone, so that Lode would write the world off and the Growers could have it. He timed it for a shift change, when the crew was meant to be off-world. The relief crew came down early: forty Dust miners from Cutbank, contracted at double rates, drank on their first night and died. Mateus said nothing for three days. Lode wrote Saltgreen off. A year later, in R.202, the Growers moved in, planting salt grass in the brine of the old shores and living in sod huts at the edge of the green. Nobody lived here then; six thousand do now. The forty names are the first entry in Ledger's book, and the Dust still demand Mateus every year.

world: A warm, dry world of blinding white salt flats in wide basins, ringed by yellow grassy plains and low hills. Every forty years, when its nine moons line up, the tides push brine up into the flats and flood them. The salt houses are old family towns on the basin rims, grown round their evaporation works.
from_space: Blinding white flats in the basins, rimmed with yellow grass and tan hills, under a nearly clear sky. At night lit towns sit in a ring round each flat.
moons: Nine small moons, the eight nearest drawn: a cratered grey rock, a captured lump, a second grey rock, a second captured lump, a third grey rock, a fourth grey rock, a third captured lump and a fifth grey rock. One more small rock orbits beyond them.
people: 95 million salt workers and chemists in the family salt-house towns on the basin rims.
story: When its nine moons line up, every forty years, brine floods the salt flats and every debt between families is cancelled. The next flood is due this year, and some creditors have quietly left.

world: A hot ocean world, 5,800 km in radius, almost all shallow sea over sand banks, with low mangrove islands on about a tenth of it and no high ground anywhere. The islands flood and drain with the seasons. The villages stand on stilts among the roots and are moved each season with the tide, so no map of them lasts.
from_space: Turquoise shallows broken by dark green mangrove islands, with towering storm cloud in the afternoon. At night almost dark, with a few faint village lights in the roots.
moons: None.
people: 8 million free islanders, in stilt villages among the mangroves, each clan its own.
story: Mangrove islanders who build their villages on stilts and move them each season with the tide. They hide Runners in the roots for a fee, and turn them in for a bigger one.

world: A tropical world, 6,200 km in radius, half ocean, its land low jungle over limestone hills riddled with caves. Sinkholes dot the forest and the rivers vanish into the rock, where the gel moulds grow in the dark. Heavy cloud, warm rain and small ice caps; the clinic towns are planned compounds at the big cave mouths.
from_space: Bright green jungle under blue-white cloud, with deep blue seas and pocks of sinkholes. At night small planned clusters of light at the cave mouths.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock, and a smooth pale ice moon cut by brown cracks. No rings.
people: 120 million hands, most of them tending the gel moulds in the caves; the clinic staff live in the compounds above.
story: A jungle mould grown in the caves here becomes the healing gel used in every Hand clinic and hospital ship. The hands who tend it heal fast, so they are kept working through injuries no other world would allow.

world: A temperate world of rolling hills a little smaller than most, with gentle valleys, vineyards on the sunny slopes and seas over half the surface. The towns are old and small, many of them half empty since the fever, their outer streets gone back to orchard.
from_space: Green hills and blue seas under light cloud, the vineyards showing as fine darker striping on the slopes. By night the towns are modest clusters, fewer than the roads between them suggest.
moons: None.
people: About 20 million, many of them still paying the clinic debt their grandparents signed, in hill towns and vineyard villages.
story: A fever emptied this world eighty years ago. Alma's clinics arrived, cured it, and sent the survivors the bill. Their grandchildren live on a free world and still pay it every month.

world: A gas giant of middling size with pale, gentle bands and one small amber storm. The hospital city floats at the breathable layer inside an old liner hull buoyed by gas cells; it sinks a little every year until its patients pump it back up. Nothing else is built in its clouds.
from_space: Pale green and white bands, softly turbulent, with a small amber storm low in the south. At night one long light floats in the northern temperate band: the ward windows of the liner hull.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock, unused.
people: 2 million people in the floating hospital city: the nursing order, their patients and the patients' families, many of whom never leave.
story: An old order of nurses runs the only hospital in the sector that bills nobody, inside an old liner hull that sinks a little every year and is pumped back up by its patients. Alma has sued them for sixty years, and they still take every patient.

world: A cold mountain world, smaller than most, where belts of jagged grey ridges cross nearly every continent with frozen valleys between them. Snow lies on every crest and ice fields fill the high basins; only small dark seas remain open. The clans live in heated stone halls cut into the ridge walls above the passes, each hall extended over centuries and none of them planned.
from_space: Jagged grey ridges in long belts, snow on every crest, white ice fields between and small dark seas, with thin cloud caught on the peaks. At night faint lights sit high on the ridges at the passes, and the valleys are dark.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock.
people: 15 million in stone halls cut into the ridges, organised by clan, with toll posts at every pass.
