story: Lightning strikes here several times a minute. Settlers live in towns slung under balloons and farm it into batteries with rods hung kilometres below; Lode wants the batteries, and Praevisio wants the storms to cool its servers.

world: A warm jungle and mountain world terraformed by Alma from bare red rock two centuries ago, with steep forested ranges, terraced slopes and small warm seas. The rain is scheduled: every afternoon cloud builds over the mountains and empties gently into the valleys. The retreats climb the terraces in careful planned tiers, and the staff towns sit in the lower valleys, just as planned and kept out of the guests' view.
from_space: Rich green ranges and mist-filled valleys round small blue seas, with afternoon cloud piled over the mountains and the old red rock showing on the highest bare peaks. At night soft gold lights along the terraces, and brighter staff towns in the valley floors.
moons: None.
people: 520 million hands, mostly Staff grade service workers under contract never to leave, and a changing few hundred thousand executive guests.
story: Alma's rest world for executives, terraformed from bare red rock two centuries ago; even the rain is scheduled, warm and gentle, every afternoon. Terraced jungle retreats where nothing is billed and nothing is remembered. The staff are chosen for their beauty and their calm, and sign a contract never to leave the planet.

world: A cold gas giant banded dull blue and grey-blue, quiet except for one long storm band in the south where a single Lode gas rig rides on its engines. The reserve fleet is not in the cloud at all: old Mandates and Decrees are parked in rows in high orbit.
from_space: Dull grey-blue bands and a crowded orbit of dark hulls in rows. By night the hulls show only scattered window lights, a few to each ship, and the rig is a single red point in the storm band.
moons: Three small moons: two captured rocks that anchor the ends of the parking rows, and one dark ice-rock.
people: 500,000 hands, mostly caretaker crews who live aboard the parked ships for years, and a few thousand more on the gas rig.
resources: laid-up warships, spare parts, fuel gas
story: Mordant's reserve fleet sleeps here: old Mandates and Decrees parked in rows, crewed by skeleton teams who live aboard for years. One Lode gas rig rides a storm band below to keep the tanks full. In a crisis the Hand counts these ships; nobody counts how many still fly.

world: A temperate living world split by a great rift valley that runs a third of the way round the planet, deep and dark, with a narrow sea on its floor. Forested uplands and farmland lie on both sides, with mountains along the rift shoulders. The two nations build their towns facing away from the rift, each with a few old cities and many villages, grown rather than planned.
from_space: Green land and blue seas on both sides of a long dark scar, under ordinary cloud. At night the lights of both nations crowd toward their own coasts, leaving a dark band on either side of the rift.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock.
people: 70 million, split between two rival nations on either side of the rift.
story: Split by a great rift valley into two nations that have not spoken in a century. Each side sells the other's secrets to the Hand.

world: A rocky world a little smaller than most, with thin air and no ozone left: a terraforming job went wrong and stripped it. The ground is bleached white and pale brown, dry plains and low cratered hills with no water on the surface. The tunnel towns run under the hills, and their entrances face west so the people can come out at dusk.
from_space: Bleached white and pale brown under a hard, clear sky, with craters and old mine scars. By night faint strings of light where the tunnel towns open onto the surface and the night shift is out.
moons: None.
people: About 2 million underground miners and their families, in tunnel towns under the hills.
story: A terraforming job went wrong and stripped the ozone: the noon sun burns skin in minutes. Its people live in tunnel towns and go out only at night; they say 'good night' when they meet and 'good day' when they part.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, of gentle countryside rising to broad grassy plateaus, with seas over about two fifths of it and small ice caps. The villages sit in the valleys below the plateaus, unplanned and far apart. The only landing field is on the plateau above the oldest village, with a long table beside it.
from_space: Soft green valleys and gold plateau grass, blue seas and light cloud. By night the villages are small, dim and far apart.
moons: None.
people: About 4 million villagers, in farming villages in the valleys.
story: A rolling green world that trades with nobody. Visitors are met at the landing field with a meal and a full tank, and politely asked to leave by nightfall.

world: An ocean world of fresh water, with land only in chains of young volcanic islands. The islands are steep black cones, several still smoking, and the haze over them is yellow with sulphur. The island towns are small and old, built from black stone round the harbours.
from_space: Deep blue sea, darker than salt water, with chains of black islands trailing yellow-grey smoke. At night a few harbour lights show, and the red glow of one or two vents.
moons: None.
people: 3 million islanders in harbour towns, every island under its own council.
story: Its oceans are fresh water, rare enough that Lode's tankers come every season to buy. They go home empty: the island councils sell only by the bucket, to people who carry it themselves.

world: A temperate world, 6,000 km in radius, landscaped by the Board over its vaults. Sea covers three-fifths of it; the land is long sandy coasts, red canyons cut through low hills, and planted forests inland, with small ice caps. The clerks' cities are planned and run along the beaches, with the vault entrances set back in the canyon walls.
from_space: Blue sea and green land edged with pale beaches, under light cloud. At night the clerks' cities show as bright bands along the coasts.
moons: None.
people: 800 million hands, mostly Staff grade clerks and the staff who serve them, in the beach cities.
resources: debt registry, legal offices, food, tourism
story: The Board landscaped a dead world into pleasant beaches to sit on its frontier registry: every Birth Debt in the sector is filed in vaults under the sand. Its clerks are the best-paid hands on the frontier and the worst-guarded, because the Board considers paper boring.
history: Tabularium was a dead world on the frontier when the Board chose it. In the R.40s, while the Tabularium registry was numbering every citizen of the Hand, the receivers wanted the frontier's paper kept far from Charter, and they cut vaults deep under its plains. The Board then paid to landscape the surface over them, giving the clerks beaches, canyons and planted forest, and named the world after the registry itself. Every Birth Debt in the sector since the first bills of R.31 has a paper file under the sand. In R.132 the Tabularium built its thinking machine and renamed itself Praevisio. The paper here stayed where it was, the Board's own office took over the vaults, and the world kept the old name. Praevisio has never asked for the files, because it already holds every number in them. The clerks are the best-paid hands on the frontier and the worst-guarded, because the Board considers paper boring. Now that open war has come in R.212, the Unruled, who burn debt registries wherever they find them, know exactly where this one is.

world: A world locked to its star, one face always burning and one always frozen. Life and people keep to the twilight band between them, a belt of red mesas, highland plains and a few salt lakes. The mesa towns are cut into the butte tops all round the band, old and unplanned, linked by cable lines and stairways. Wind blows from the night side toward the day side without stopping, carrying thin cloud.
from_space: A tan and red ring of mesas with green highland patches round the dusk, between a scorched brown day face and a white frozen night face. The towns show as a broken string of lights all the way round the twilight.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock; Repossessor ships hold their catches in orbit near it until the market opens.
people: 300 million settlers in the mesa towns of the twilight band; most work for the Repossessor houses that run the market, or for the cells, kitchens and docks that serve it.
story: The Repossessors' market, where debtors caught on the run are sold back to whoever holds their debt. Its mesa towns line the twilight band, so a debtor who runs has the burning day or the frozen night to run into. Free, rich and quietly hated.
history: Tallow Mesa was settled long before the Receivership by herders and salt traders who kept to the dusk, where the air could be breathed and water ran down from the night-side ice. It stayed free when the Receivership came, too poor for any company to want. That changed after R.31, when the Birth Debt made every runaway hand a debt worth recovering. Repossessors needed somewhere outside the Hand's books to sell what they caught, and the free mesa towns became that place. The market grew into a world. A few Repossessor houses now run it: they buy catches from the hunters, hold them in cells and sell them back to whoever holds the debt, at a price that falls every hour past the due date. Catches lodged in the cells at Grimwall arrive by the day. Mora was born here in R.179 into one of the houses, a free birth owing nothing. She grew up on the market floor learning the clock, and in R.199, at twenty, she asked the visiting tracker Usura to take her on. The Hand pays the houses well and never says so. The Collective wants the market burned, and Tallow Mesa knows it.

world: An arid world of ordinary size with no water left: Lode drained the aquifers, and the old shallow seas are now dry seabeds of pale mud and white salt, with the old coasts standing round them as low cliffs. The empty cities still stand on those coasts. The holdouts live in a few dug-in hamlets on the old shores and plant salt-trees across the seabeds in long lines.
from_space: Pale tan and white salt flats with thin threads of grey-green in the basins where the salt-trees have taken hold, and grey patches of empty city on the old coasts. By night a few pin-pricks of light on the shores.
moons: Three small moons: a cratered grey rock and two captured lumps.
people: 7,000 holdouts in dug-in hamlets on the old shores; the other seven hundred million were relocated, the files say.
story: Seven hundred million people lived here until Lode drained the aquifers. Seven thousand remain, planting salt-trees across the dry seabeds, and the grey-green threads now show from orbit. The rest were relocated, the files say.

world: A temperate farm world of low hills, hedged fields and slow rivers, with grey-blue seas and gentle weather. The land is a patchwork of small fields bounded by old hedges and stone walls, and the villages are grey stone, grown over centuries round their parish halls and market squares. There are no big cities; the largest town is the port where the grain ships load.
from_space: A patchwork of green and gold fields with grey-blue seas and soft white cloud. At night the villages are an even scatter of small, warm lights, with one brighter cluster at the grain port.
moons: None.
people: 200 million farmers in parish villages, who sell their grain to the Hand and raise their own children.
story: A quiet farming world of hedged fields and stone villages. Its farmers sell grain to the Hand and children to nobody, and Alma's recruiters have learned not to visit.

world: A cool world, 6,800 km in radius, about half sea. Glacier tongues run down from the highland ice into a broad belt of grey-green marsh and low islands, where the old marsh towns stand on raised mounds above the tide. Praevisio's drone works are planned grids on the drier ground behind them; low cloud and drizzle most days.
from_space: Grey-green marsh and white glacier tongues round a dark sea, under drifting low cloud. At night the drone works glow in neat grids and the marsh towns in loose clusters between them.
moons: None.
people: 3 billion hands, Contract grade, most of them building and test-flying Gleaners in the works towns; the old marsh towns hold a small share.
story: Praevisio builds Gleaner drones here, and every drone is test-flown low over the marsh towns before delivery. The towns are told the passes are for calibration, and nobody has asked what is being calibrated.
history: Fishing families settled Techne's marsh islands before anyone kept a record of them, and built their towns on mounds above the tide. Under the Republic the drier ground behind the marsh grew small electronics works, and the world was a quiet holding when Praevisio took it over. In the R.150s, when Praevisio sold the Board its first Gleaners and Proxies, it made Techne its drone works, and the works have grown ever since into the planned grids that now fill the ground between the glaciers and the marsh. Every Gleaner built here is test-flown low over the marsh towns before delivery. The towns are told the passes are for calibration, and nobody has asked what is being calibrated. Ansel Mbatha was born a hand here in R.180 and onboarded by Praevisio at fourteen, in R.194, under the name Kriton. On Techne, with the link in his left temple, he learned to sign off a flight. In R.210 he walked out of a control room behind the front and went to the Collective. Techne's flight logs still carry his old name on thousands of sign-offs.

world: A dead airless rock, 3,200 km in radius, grey and saturated with craters, with nothing on the ground but the old anchor pads. Lode's toll ring circles it at the equator: a band of docks, fuel tanks and counting halls where the crews live, laid out module by module to Lode's standard plan.
from_space: Grey cratered rock circled by a bright orbital ring of docks, its window strip lit day and night, with ships queued at its gates.
moons: None.
people: 1 million hands, mostly Contract grade toll crews, nearly all living in the ring.
story: Lode's toll ring on the Charter Road, built round a dead rock; its crews live in the ring itself. Toll is charged by mass, so crews weigh their own dead and put them out of the airlock before the ring to save on the fee.

world: A warm, dry world of rolling red clay hills and shallow valleys, smaller than most, with no seas and only a few lakes that fill in the rains and dry out after. The towns are cut into the clay hillsides against the heat, terrace on terrace, and every wall is painted. Thin dust, a little cloud, and frost only at the poles.
from_space: Rust red and ochre hills from pole to pole, softer and redder than desert sand. At night small, warm clusters of light mark the clay towns.
moons: One moon of cratered grey rock, unused.
people: 2 million artists and their families in towns cut into the clay hills.
story: A painters' colony in the red clay hills, its towns cut into the clay against the heat. The painters make Alma's adverts by day for money and paint them over by night, and Alma pays them to paint them again in the morning.

world: A cold world larger than most, mostly land: flat grey steppe frozen most of the year, pale green grass in the short summer, and shallow frozen seas. The ice caps are large. Continuity laid the depot out as one planned grid of heated barrack blocks, parade grounds and rail yards that runs for hundreds of kilometres across the steppe.
from_space: Slate grey and pale green under frost. By night a hard grid of lit depots, and at its centre one large bright block where the debt board hangs over the parade ground.
moons: None.
people: 2 billion hands, half of them in Tranche barracks and the rest depot staff and rail crews who keep the regiments supplied.
story: The sector's Tranche depot, where new regiments muster in heated barrack grids and ship out. Above the parade ground hangs a debt board the size of a city block, showing every soldier's balance in lights. It goes down slowly, and some evenings the whole depot stands out in the frost to watch it.

world: A dry mountain world of high red ridges split by deep canyons, with no seas. Rivers run along the canyon floors, so each canyon is a thin green ribbon between red walls. The towns are built along the floors and up the walls with no plan, and the jar of ashes stands at the mouth of the largest canyon.
from_space: Red-brown ranges cut by canyons with thin green floors. At night faint threads of light run down the canyons.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock and a small captured lump.
people: 800,000 canyon dwellers in towns along the green floors, with Unruled cells among them more often than not.
story: Canyon towns where the Unruled once burned a debt registry. They keep the ashes in a jar at the canyon's mouth.

world: A warm world of ordinary size, with steep green mountains, rainforest on the slopes, salt marshes along the coasts and a dark inland sea. The great salt flats lie in a basin between the ranges, and every machine the Unwritten capture is carried there and smashed. The pilgrim towns round the flats grew shrine by shrine, without a plan.
from_space: White salt flats between green mountains and a dark sea, under broken cloud. In low sun the flats glitter with broken circuitry. By night the pilgrim towns are dim rings of lamplight round the white.
moons: None.
people: About 5 million, mostly Unwritten, in pilgrim towns round the flats and fishing villages on the coast.
story: The Unwritten bring every machine they capture here and smash it on the salt flats. After seventy years the flats glitter with broken circuitry, and pilgrims walk across them barefoot.

world: A hot desert world of orange sand and low rock ridges, with no water and little cloud. Lode's old refineries stand in a few tight clusters on the plain, laid out on the old company grids, their black stacks still smoking; the Dust families sleep in cellars cut under them.
from_space: Orange desert with black refinery stacks and a smudge of smoke drifting off them. At night the furnaces glow red, brighter than the few lamps of the cellars.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock and a small captured lump, both unused.
people: 150,000 Dust families living in cellars under the refinery stacks.
story: Lode abandoned the refineries here. Dust families moved in and run them for the Collective; the furnace has not gone cold in eleven years. The families sleep in cellars cut under the stacks, the one place the desert heat lets up.

world: A violent gas giant of deep indigo belts and white storm bands, fast-moving and torn by four large storms. The Dust crews live in pressure cans strung down one long tether that hangs from an icy moonlet into the upper clouds, and skim fuel gas in patched scoop ships. The main tether carries the painted names of every crewmate the storms have taken.
from_space: Deep indigo with white storm bands and a faint dark ring, small icy moons all round it. At night the tether is a thin string of can lights dropping from the nearest moonlet into the storms.
moons: Eleven icy moonlets, the eight largest drawn. Outward from the ring: the tether moonlet, a smooth bright ice moon; a dark ice-rock; a second smooth ice moon; a frozen-plains moonlet; a small dark ice-rock; then a third smooth ice moonlet, a third dark ice-rock and a second frozen-plains moonlet. Three more moonlets lie beyond them. Ring: a faint narrow dark ring.
people: 9,000 Dust skimmer crews and their families, in pressure cans on the tether.
story: Dust crews live in pressure cans strung down one long tether that hangs from an icy moonlet into the upper clouds, and skim fuel gas in patched scoop ships. Every scoop is christened with the name of a crewmate the storms took, and the list is painted down the main tether.
history: The Ladle's moonlets are ice and its storms never stop. Lode strung the first tether here as a fuel stop for haulers working off the lanes, and crewed it with Dust, Contract hands from its rocks who could live in low gravity and pressure cans. The storms took crews every year. The crews began christening each scoop ship with the name of a crewmate the storms had taken, and painting the names down the main tether. When the scoops were no longer worth Lode's insurance it wrote the station off, and the families stayed on, skimming for anyone who would buy. In R.167 Tove Lindqvist was born here. Her brother Anders went on the tether in R.183, when she was sixteen, and she flew the scoop that carried his name for the next ten years. After the Table first sat in R.201, the Ladle's families threw in with the Collective, and Tove moved from scoops to fighters. Her squadron flies without call signs: every pilot paints their own name on the nose, as on the Ladle, so Praevisio must print each one on its loss reports. Forty-One learned to fly fighters in it. In R.212 the Ladle skims fuel for the Collective, and the list on the tether is longer every year.

world: A small, hot, airless rock, heavily cratered, its surface baked grey-brown by a close star. Along the northern highlands a line of cliffs rises several kilometres above the crater plains, and the Runner town is cut into them: halls, docks and berths behind pressure doors, dug out level by level by every crew that ever needed a room. On the highest cliff the beacon burns day and night, the light the lane's pilots steer by on the last jump in.
from_space: Grey-brown cratered rock with no air and no cloud, and one bright point of light on the north cliffs that never goes out. On the night side the beacon is joined by a faint scatter of lit pressure doors along the cliff face.
moons: Three moons: a cratered grey rock, a dark ice-rock where the Runners cut water, and a small captured lump.
people: About 60,000 Runners and their crews, more when the lane is busy, all inside the cliff town. The captains' moot runs it, and any pilot who makes it in down the Lantern Run gets a drink, a berth and no questions.
resources: fuel, ship repairs, hidden cargo, pilots
story: The Runners' capital at the far end of the fastest unpaid lane in the galaxy, a path through gravity wells only Runner pilots can fly. A beacon burns on the north cliffs over the sealed town; a pilot who makes it in gets a drink, a berth and no questions.
history: Nobody settled The Lantern on purpose. Before the Receivership it was a hot, worthless rock beyond a stretch of bad space, a knot of gravity wells that wrecked any ship that tried to cut through, and the Republic's charts marked the whole region closed. When Lode built its toll lanes, between the R.50s and the R.70s, and began charging for the fast routes, the crews who would not pay went looking for routes the Hand did not own. Some of them learned, at great cost, to thread the wells, and the rock at the far end had cliffs to dig into and nothing anyone else wanted. A crew lit a fire on the highest cliff so the next ship would know where to land, and the fire became the beacon. Every crew that stayed cut its own rooms into the cliff, and the captains began meeting to settle quarrels over berths and fuel; that meeting is the moot, and it still runs the town. In time the path became the Lantern Run, the fastest unpaid lane in the galaxy, and Lode began offering the moot anything to close it. The moot has never answered. Since the strands first sat at one table, in R.201, The Lantern has been the Runners' capital, and in R.212 the beacon still burns.

world: A warm ocean world of ordinary size, with only a little land: low coral islands, long reef lines and wide lagoons on a deep sea, with no ice caps. Trade winds keep the cloud moving. The harbour towns are old and grown, strung along the inner shores of the lagoons, with slips and dry docks cut into the reef; the arks ride at anchor in the largest lagoons, each a city in its own right.
from_space: Deep blue with turquoise lagoons and white reef lines under scattered trade-wind cloud. In the largest lagoons the arks show as long pale shapes on the water; by night the harbour towns are a thin chain of light, and the arks stay dim, because the Ilmar keep their lights low.
moons: One large pale moon, a cratered rock that lights the lagoons at night.
people: 30 million harbour folk and Walkout yard crews in the lagoon towns, and several thousand Ilmar, Kiru and Nhal exiles living aboard the arks.
story: The arks of the Harvested ride at anchor in the lagoons while harbour folk and Walkout crews refit them as warships. The exiles live aboard and seldom come ashore; the harbour people know better than to invite them.
history: The Moorings was settled during the Settlement by reef fishers, and its harbour folk have built and mended boats in the lagoons ever since. Under the Republic and the Hand alike it was too far out and too poor to tax hard. The first Ilmar arks came in the years after R.178, when the Ilmar lifted their edge cities off their world and left: cities with no harbour, looking for somewhere to mend. The harbour folk asked for no papers and let them anchor. Walkout crews followed after the walkout at Navalia in R.189, with nowhere to work and hands that knew hulls. In R.194 a Lode lane picket fired on the ark Deep Count and killed nine people on a garden deck. The next year, R.195, Oz Petrenko came aboard here with his handwritten manual, and with the ark-wright Ushe he mounted the first guns an ark ever carried. The arks have been the Collective's heavy fleet since. In the autumn of R.201 one voice from each strand sat at one table here for the first time, and the Table began. Keth of Long Patience commands the ark fleet from these lagoons, and in R.206 young Isse of Last Shade watched the dawn come up over the lagoon from her ark's sunward wall, visor up. The exiles still live aboard and seldom come ashore.

world: A temperate world of steep mountain ranges and dark conifer forest, with small cold seas in the basins between them. One gorge, hundreds of kilometres long and in places barely wider than a hauler, cuts through the highest range, and the Walkout workshops are dug into its walls, hidden under forest and rock. The towns are cut into the same walls, grown room by room as the yards needed hands, and the graves of pilots who failed the gorge line its mouth.
from_space: Dark green forest and grey ridges with small grey-blue seas, and one dark crooked line where the gorge cuts the main range. At night the world is nearly black; the yards keep their lights inside the rock.
moons: One grey cratered moon.
people: About 300,000 Walkouts and their families, in towns and workshops cut into the gorge walls; most of the adults build fighters or fly them.
story: Walkouts build fighters in workshops cut into the mountains and fly them out through one narrow gorge. Every pilot learns the gorge first; the ones who don't are buried at its mouth.

world: An ocean world with no land at all, deep blue from pole to pole, with small polar ice and steady cloud. The Runner town is made of old hulls lashed together into floating rafts that drift on the currents, extended and rebuilt without any plan. The Nhal exile community moors at its edge.
from_space: Deep blue with a scatter of grey floating towns. At night a few faint clusters of light drift on the dark sea.
moons: One cratered grey moon.
people: 200,000 people, mostly Runners, with a small Nhal exile community moored at the town's edge.
story: A Runner town of old hulls lashed together on an ocean that has no land. A small Nhal exile community lives at its edge, and nobody asks them to move.
history: The Rafts has no land to settle, so for most of its history nobody did. Fishing crews worked its seas from passing ships and left. Under the Hand it was nobody's holding: no ground to number and no port to tax. Runners found it the way they find everything the Hand ignores, and began lashing old hulls together into a town that moves with the currents and never keeps an address. By the late R.190s, around the time the Nhal homeworld was harvested in R.196, a small community of Nhal exiles had moored at the edge of the town, and nobody asked them to move. Soon after R.196 a former Praevisio technician from Stochos came here, a man who had cut the link out of his temple and put out his own eyes. An old Nhal woman taught him to hear a room, to feel the hum of a drive through the deck and to find a man by the warmth of his breath. The first thing she made him find in the dark was an iron nail in the hull planks. He pulled it out, has carried it ever since, and goes by Brother Nail. After the Table first sat in R.201 the town came in with the Runners. In R.212 the Rafts is larger than it has ever been, and the Nhal still moor at its edge.

world: A large, pale gas giant with soft cream and orange bands and very little weather: no great storms, only gentle eddies along the belt edges. Nobody lives in its cloud. Its people are all on the moons, in camps dug into the ice.
from_space: A pale orange giant with soft cream bands, and a swarm of moons around it, the largest an orange ball of haze. At night there are no lights at all; the camps keep dark.
moons: Twenty-six moons, a dozen with hidden camps. The eight biggest, in order outward: a hazy giant moon wrapped in orange smog; a dark ice-rock; a smooth bright ice moon; a second and a third dark ice-rock; a small captured rock; a second smooth ice moon; and a second small captured rock. The other eighteen are small icy lumps, and the camps move among them by lot every forty days.
people: 30,000 Runners and Dust families in camps dug into the ice of a dozen moons.
resources: hidden camps, fuel gas, moon-ice water
story: A pale gas giant with twenty-six moons, and Collective camps dug into the ice of a dozen of them. Every forty days the camps move to another moon by lot, so the Hand's survey probes never find the same camp twice.

world: A dry world of low hills and plains covered in stumpfields, where Lode clear-cut every forest for pit props and the soil dried out behind it. Young forest is spreading again in patches from the Grower camps, already taller than a person. The communes live in plain timber villages at the edge of each plantation and move outward as it grows.
from_space: Pale tan stumpfields in grey-brown patches, with spreading patches of young green forest, under thin dusty cloud. At night a few scattered camp lights at the forest edges.
moons: None.
people: 180,000 Grower commune members in timber villages at the plantation edges.
story: Lode clear-cut every forest here for pit props and the soil dried out behind it. The Growers plant one sapling for every name in each debt registry the Collective burns; the new forest is already taller than a person.

world: A small frozen world of ice plains and glaciers over low mountains. In one valley, under salvaged mirrors parked in orbit, a glacier has melted into a lake and the first barley grows on its shore. The Growers live in greenhouses dug into the valley walls; the rest of the world is still ice.
from_space: White ice and glacier, with one dark green-blue valley and its lake, and a few bright sparks in orbit where the mirrors catch the sun. At night a faint warm glow from the greenhouses in the valley walls.
moons: Three moons: a cratered grey rock, a second, paler cratered rock, and a small captured rock.
people: 6,000 Growers, living in greenhouses dug into the walls of the thawing valley.
story: A Grower commune parked salvaged mirrors in orbit to warm one frozen valley, and lives in greenhouses dug into its walls. After twelve years there is a lake where there was a glacier, and the first barley. The rest of the world is still ice.

world: A warm, ordinary-sized world, about two thirds ocean, with two large jungle continents joined by a narrow mountain isthmus. Tall cloud stands over the jungles and the ice caps are small. The Unruled south is grown, villages and camps with no plan at all; the Locals' north is planned, towns in grids round the factories; and across the isthmus runs the wall.
from_space: Green continents in deep blue sea under heavy tropical cloud. By night the north is lit in neat grids and the south in loose scatters, and the wall shows as a thin bright seam of floodlights across the isthmus.
moons: None.
people: 700 million people: about 400 million in the Locals' north and 300 million in the Unruled south.
story: The biggest Collective population in the sector, and the worst neighbours. The Unruled hold the south, the Locals the north, and they built a wall across the isthmus to keep the peace.

world: A small hot world, 3,800 km in radius, locked to its star. The day face is burnt orange rock pocked with craters and a few slow lava seeps; the night face is frozen blue-black. Between them a narrow twilight band holds a little air, a few frozen ponds and the lab's string of white domes, spaced evenly along it, and the lab's waste heat is piped out onto the night side.
from_space: A burnt orange day face pocked with craters, a thin line of white lab domes along the twilight band, and a blue-black night face. The domes' lights run in a single even string.
moons: None.
people: 200,000 hands, Staff grade researchers and their support crews, all under the domes.
story: Praevisio's forecast lab sits in a string of white domes along the twilight line, models the next ten years of the frontier, and dumps its heat onto the frozen night side. The scientists here are the only hands who can read their own forecasts, and many of them choose not to.

world: A small frozen world under one unbroken glacier, with thin cold air and no open water. Low ranges show through the ice as faint ridges, and the wind keeps the snow moving in long streaks. The vault lies deep under the thickest ice, and its heated galleries and a single landing field are the only things built here.
from_space: Blinding white with faint blue seams where the glacier cracks. Nothing shows by night except, at most, the lights of the landing field.
moons: None.
people: 2,000 hands, all Staff grade, in heated galleries in the ice round the vault; through the winters no ships land and they see nobody else for months.
story: A Praevisio vault buried under a glacier, holding the backup ledger of every Birth Debt in the region. Two thousand staff tend it from heated galleries in the ice through winters with no ships; the Unruled would trade a fleet to burn it.

world: A warm, dry world a little smaller than most, with no open water: low rolling plains and old worn hills under dense thorn brush from pole to pole. Rain comes in one short season, and the brush grows back over anything cut. The settler clans live in grown hamlets in cleared hollows and cut their roads anew every year.
from_space: Olive and khaki scrub everywhere, with the pale lines of the year's new roads and a little dust haze. By night faint scattered lights in the hollows.
moons: None.
people: 3 million settlers in clan hamlets; a few hundred of them work as guides for Runner crews crossing the brush.
story: Dense thorn brush covers everything, and the settlers who live in it cut their roads anew every year. Runner crews pay well for a guide.

world: A warm, wet world of ordinary size, half sea, with jungle on the higher ground and swamp below it. Its great river breaks into a thousand channels across a delta the size of a small continent, and the silt moves the channels every season. The market town stands on stilts over the main channels and has grown without a plan; smaller stilt villages and fishing camps fill the rest of the delta, and the dredges that keep the channels open are moored along its edge.
from_space: A brown-green delta fanning out into blue sea, laced with silver channels, under warm hazy cloud. By night the market town is one bright knot of light on the delta, with fainter villages strung along the channels round it.
moons: None.
people: 120 million traders and fisherfolk: about 20 million in the stilt market town and its harbour, the rest in stilt villages and fishing camps across the delta and along the jungle coasts.
story: A great river delta where a stilt-town market trades anything to anyone. Whoever owns the dredges that keep the channels open runs the market, and the dredges change hands about once a decade.

world: A pale, quiet gas giant of blue-white bands with few storms, and nobody living in its air. Its three moons shine bright enough to be seen as lamps from the inner planets, and the biggest of them is a living sea moon of warm oceans and white sand coasts, where the harbour towns stand round sheltered bays.
from_space: A pale blue-white giant with soft bands and three bright moons: a blue sea moon with white coasts, a smooth white ice moon and a cream frozen-plains moon. At night the harbour towns on the sea moon show as tiny lights along its coasts.
moons: Three moons: a big living sea moon with white coasts and harbour towns, a smooth bright ice moon, and a frozen-plains moon of cream ice with a dark red band.
people: About 20 million on the sea moon, in harbour towns that fish, take in Alma's tour parties and still issue Republic-era licences.
story: Harbour towns line the white coasts of the giant's sea moon, the brightest of its three lamps. Its harbour masters still issue Republic-era licences. Alma tolerates the moon as a heritage destination and sells tours of it.

world: A mountainous world with long, narrow seas squeezed between brown ranges, so most of the coast is steep and the sea has nowhere to spread when the tide comes in. Twice a day the two moons pull the water metres up the narrow inlets, and every coastal city stands behind a sea wall of cut stone, the oldest walls grey and the newest still pale. The cities grew along the shore over centuries, crammed between wall and mountain; inland, smaller towns sit in the high valleys above the reach of any tide.
from_space: Deep blue seas in long thin channels between brown mountain chains, with white cloud banked against the ranges. At night the cities show as bright lines pressed tight along the coasts, each edged by a dark strip of sea where the wall stands.
moons: Two moons, both large cratered grey rock, whose pull together raises the tides; neither is settled.
people: 750 million, most of them in the walled coastal cities. The wall-builders' union counts a large share of the working adults as members and decides where every new wall goes.
story: Two moons drag tides high enough to drown a city, so the coastal cities live behind enormous sea walls. The wall-builders' union decides where the next wall goes, which makes it the real government.

world: A large temperate world of vast golden wheat plains under a big sky, with dark green forest belts along the rivers and on the slopes of a few long mountain ranges. The seas are moderate and the weather is steady. The grain cooperatives' towns sit at river crossings and rail heads, grown up round their silos, and the plains between them are farmed in long strips.
from_space: Golden plains with dark green forest belts and long mountain chains, blue seas and scattered cloud. At night the cooperative towns are a wide, even scatter of lights, densest along the rivers.
moons: None.
people: 2 billion settlers in cooperative farm towns; many of them quietly like the Hand's freighters, which have always come on time.
story: The breadbasket of the Trunk Line: endless wheat under a big sky. Its settlers' families have never forgotten the famine before the Receivership, which is why many of them quietly like the Hand's freighters.

world: A desert world of ordinary size, with hot days and freezing nights, wide ochre basins and long dark mountain ridges. There are no seas; water comes from deep wells and a few mountain springs. The towns grew out from the old prison blocks, so every city has a grim planned core of cell rows inside a sprawl of free streets.
from_space: Ochre and red desert crossed by dark mountain ridges, a thin frost on the peaks at dawn and very little cloud. By night the towns show as bright square cores with ragged rings of light round them.
moons: None.
people: About 300 million descendants of convicts, in towns grown out of the old prison blocks; the council is elected block by block.
story: A Republic penal colony whose prisoners were forgotten at the Receivership. Their descendants run it as a free world of former convicts, and are very proud of it.
history: The Republic opened Tierra Seca as a penal colony in its last decades: a dry world where escape meant dying of thirst. The prisoners worked the mines and were supplied from orbit on contract. When the Republic defaulted in R.0, the supply contract lapsed with everything else, and nobody among the receivers thought to renew it or to claim the prisoners. The colony was simply forgotten. The guards left on the last ship. The prisoners found the wells, broke the cell doors and kept the cell blocks, because they were the only shelter on the world. They elected a council from the blocks, and the blocks still elect it. Two centuries later the colony is a free world of 300 million that has never been numbered and owes nobody anything; the Hand has looked at it since and decided it is not worth an acquisition. Its people are proud of all of it. Their town crests show a broken lock, and every child learns the number of its family's block as a second name.

world: A brown and cream gas giant of moderate size, banded in earth colours, with two small storms. Nobody lives in its clouds. The logging families live on its big living moon, a world of hardwood forest and snowy mountains with cold narrow seas, where the timber is floated down the rivers to the mills.
from_space: Brown and cream bands with two small storms, and beside it a big green moon with snowy peaks. On the moon's night side the mill towns show along the rivers.
moons: Three moons: the big living moon of forests and mountains; a dark ice-rock splashed with bright craters; and a small captured rock.
people: 30 million settlers on the living moon, in logging and mill towns along its rivers.
resources: hardwood, rare minerals (both from the living moon)
story: Loggers on its forest moon cut the hardwood that panels every executive cabin in the Hand's fleet. Under the roots lie rare minerals, and the families know the day they sell the forest is the day it ends.

world: A dry world of low plains and worn hills where a Republic-era company planted a rainforest and the rain never followed. Every year the forest dries into savannah and the grass burns, so the land lies in bands of green, gold and burnt brown. The settlers' towns are light and movable, and move with the fire line.
from_space: Bands of green, gold and brown across the plains, with long smoke trails along the burning edge. At night the fire line glows in a long thin orange arc, and the towns' lights sit just behind it.
moons: None.
people: 6 million nomad farmers in towns that move with the fire line.
story: A Republic-era company planted a rainforest on this dry world and the rain never followed: every year the forest dries into savannah and the grass burns. Settlers move with the fire line, and children learn to read the smoke before they can read words.

world: An airless world, 4,800 km in radius, of grey-green rock broken by deep winding valleys. The repair towns fill the valley floors under long pressure domes, patched daily, and grew valley by valley without a plan; the uplands between them are cratered and scarred by small old mines.
from_space: Grey-green rock with dark valleys and the glint of dome roofs along them. At night the domed valleys glow in long winding strings.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 150 million free mechanics and their families, all under the valley domes.
resources: machine repair, simple robots, spare parts, ore
story: A free world of repair shops under pressure domes in airless valleys, keeping old, simple machines running long after Praevisio stopped supporting them. The domes leak and are patched daily. The Unwritten call it a den of machines; its mechanics answer that none of theirs can think.

world: A volcanic world of high grey mountains and deep furnace valleys, where lava wells up along the valley floors and the slopes are bare rock and ash. Mordant's arms works are cut into the mountainsides and forge their guns on lava heat, and the workers live in the same sealed valleys where the guns are test-fired. The towns are Mordant grids packed between the valley walls, all built to one plan, with siren towers at their corners.
from_space: Grey mountains with orange lava along the valleys and furnace glow in the mountainsides, under a thin brown haze. At night the valleys show as bright orange threads with hard white town grids beside them.
moons: One cratered grey moon.
people: 400 million hands, mostly Indentured, in sealed valley towns beside the works, where the warning sirens run on a timetable.
story: Mordant's arms works, cut into volcanic mountains: guns for every Hand hull are forged here on lava heat and tested in the sealed valleys where the workers live. The warning sirens are on a timetable.

world: A built ring round a white star, Lode's freight depot on the Long Haul. Its floor is a mild band of plains and shallow seas, about two-thirds land, given over to warehouse fields and docker towns; the towns are planned blocks along the freight roads that run the length of the loop to the lifts at each pier. The rim walls are low and carry the crane works.
from_space: A rust-orange band round a white star, hi-vis orange stripes along its edges, its outer hull bristling with freight piers and the ships queued at them. On the far side the floor shows tan plains, green strips and blue seas. At night the floor is one long sprawl of warehouse and town lights.
moons: None (a built ring round its star).
people: 4 billion hands, mostly Contract dockers and their families, in planned docker towns on the ring floor; a few million Lode staff live in the rim walls above the piers.
story: Lode built this freight ring when its depot on the Long Haul outgrew any planet. Cargo changes hulls at the piers on the outer hull and hands change contracts on the floor below. The dockers strike more often than anywhere else in the sector, and a Local runs the strike fund.

world: A small airless world of brown and grey-green rock, cratered and flat but for a few low ridges, with no water. It lies between two jump points too close to jump between. The ferry clans live in buried hangar towns under the plains, grown outward hangar by hangar, with only the hangar doors and landing lights on the surface.
from_space: Brown and grey-green rock with old craters and no cloud. By night rows of ferry lights on the plains where the hangar doors open, and the tugs' running lights lifting off toward the jump points.
moons: None.
people: 2 million people in the ferry clans, in buried hangar towns.
story: Two jump points on the Trunk Line sit too close to jump between, so ferry clans tow ships across from buried hangar towns on this airless rock. They charge less than Lode would, which Lode resents.

world: A temperate ocean world terraformed by Alma, with chains of green islands and a few low uplands in a warm, calm sea, and small polar ice. Alma shaped the coasts for beauty: white beaches, sheltered lagoons, gentle hills. The clinic towns are planned to the last path, set in rings round each island's clinic and landing field, and the dormitories where newborns wait to ship out stand back from the shore, where the sea cannot be seen.
from_space: Bright blue sea and green island coastlines fringed with pale sand, under light, even cloud. At night every island shows a planned ring of light round its clinic, and a steady line of shuttle lights climbs from the landing fields.
moons: None.
people: 600 million hands, mostly clinic staff and newborns; the newborns are shipped out to the yards as soon as they can hold a tool.
story: Alma made these seas beautiful and set its birth clinics on the islands. The yard crews of the next generation are born here, billed here, and shipped to the yards as soon as they can hold a tool. Nobody born here remembers the sea.
history: Before the Receivership Tranquilla was a warm sea world of bare volcanic islands, charted in the Republic's census and never settled. In R.31 Alma began billing every birth to the newborn, and it needed places to make births in quantity. Over the following decades it terraformed Tranquilla, planting and softening the islands and raising its island clinics. Its biggest buyer has always been Mordant, which takes the next generation of yard crew here and ships them to Navalia and the outer yards as soon as they can hold a tool. Each child is billed for the clinic, the licence and the first breath, and the bill travels with them. In R.184 two children were born here who matter now. One went to a yard ship by six, until a forecast from Pythia Kallos's office in R.193 said admiral; Mordant bought her out of her yard suit and named her Aurelia. She is Captain Aurelia Quell, Praevisio's golden child. The other went to the Navalia yards as a welder with a number for a name, until Alma took his face from a yard camera for its broadcasts in R.209; the walls now call him Nobody. In R.212 the clinics run at capacity, and nobody born here remembers the sea.

world: A warm, wet rainforest world, about seven tenths land, with broad river plains and narrow seas. The loggers hold the eastern river country and cut it in strips; the Grower commune holds the west and lets it regrow. The truce line between them runs down the middle of the largest continent, on a map nobody agrees on. Rain is heavy, and the cloud rarely breaks.
from_space: Dark green rainforest under heavy cloud, with paler strips of cut forest along the eastern rivers. At night a scatter of logging camp lights shows in the east, and the Grower side is dark.
moons: None.
people: 4 million loggers and Growers, the loggers in river camps and the Growers in forest villages; both sides keep surveyors, and the surveyors drink together.
story: Loggers and a Grower commune share the rainforest under a truce drawn on a map nobody agrees on. Both sides keep surveyors, and the surveyors drink together.

world: A wet temperate world a little larger than most, just over half ocean, its continents low and green. Three great rivers drain the largest continent's plains and meet the sea together in one huge brown delta; rain falls most days and the ice caps are small. The towns are old river towns grown along the banks, with grain fields and rice paddies running back from every levee.
from_space: Blue sea and green lowland under heavy, broken rain cloud, with brown silt fanning out where the three rivers meet the coast. By night only thin strings of town lights along the rivers and one bright cluster at the delta docks.
moons: None.
people: 70 million settlers, mostly farmers and river crews, in towns along the three rivers; the delta dock towns, where the Hand's buyers and the Runners' boats tie up, hold about a tenth of them.
story: A wet farm world where three great rivers meet the sea. The settlers sell grain to anyone, Hand or not, and every harvest season the Hand's buyers and the Runners' boats tie up at the same docks without looking at each other.

world: A cold world smaller than most, of high moorland frozen most of the year, with white snow uplands above and deep valleys below holding long silver lakes. The villages are old stone and turf hamlets in the valleys, grown without a plan; the truce field, a wide flat moor where the sects meet, has no buildings at all.
from_space: Grey-green moor under frost, white uplands and silver lakes in the dark valleys. By night only faint scattered hamlet lights; machines are not welcome here, and the lamps burn oil.
moons: None.
people: 800,000 villagers and pilgrims: about half a million villagers live in the valley hamlets all year, and the pilgrims come and go, most of them in the truce season.
story: Once a year rival Unwritten sects meet here in truce. No machine more complicated than a pump may land, and the villagers turn out every pilgrim's pockets at the field.

world: A built ring round a fusion lamp, its floor laid out as parkland, lakes and bamboo forest in a mild, even climate with no ice. The schools stand on the terraces of both rim walls, looking down over the parks. The Contract staff live in the hull decks under the floor, in planned corridors that never see the lamp.
from_space: A green loop round a rod of white light, the floor crossed by straight white roads and scattered with small lakes. The rim terraces are lit warm gold day and night; the outer hull is dull grey plate with a Hand-red stripe along each edge.
moons: None (a built ring round a fusion lamp).
people: About 90 million hands, mostly Contract staff living in the hull decks, and 40,000 Board children schooled on the rim terraces.
story: The Board built this ring to raise its children, the one childhood the Hand pays for. Forty thousand Board children are taught on the rim terraces above the parkland; the Contract staff who raise them live in the hull decks and were never schooled themselves.
history: Within a generation of the Birth Debt of R.31, nobody outside the Board raised children, and the Board decided its own should be raised apart. It had Tutela built for them: a ring round a fusion lamp, so that no star's weather could ever reach it, with parkland on the floor and schools on the rim walls. It is the one childhood the Hand pays for. Contract staff were hired into the hull decks to cook, clean and raise the children, and none of them has ever been schooled. Every heir of the five has been taught there since. Tiberius Mordant (born R.138) and Quintilla Dis (R.146) learned on its terraces, then Kassandra Oren (R.148) and Marius Stator (R.149). Kassandra wore a paper bracelet there as a girl, a guess about her own life that she wrote herself and hid from Sibyl. Bona Vell (R.157) was raised by her own mother on the ring. Lucan Mordant (R.176) fell from a racing skiff on its lakes at seventeen. Forty thousand Board children live there now, and the staff who raise them still live under the floor.

world: A dry world a little larger than most with no open sea. A belt of burning rock desert and dune fields girdles the equator, and nothing crosses it on foot. North and south of it the land climbs into cool forested highlands that run to both poles, with snow on the highest ranges. Each state's towns are old free towns grown along the highland rivers, with timber mills and hill mines above them.
from_space: A rust-red belt of desert round the middle, edged with tan, between two dark green highland caps flecked white on the peaks. Little cloud, except over the highlands. By night two separate webs of town lights, north and south, with nothing at all between them.
moons: None.
people: 700 million, about 380 million in the northern state and 320 million in the southern, almost all in the highland valleys; nobody lives in the belt.
story: A burning desert belt splits the world in half. North and south have been at peace for a century only because neither can cross it. The Hand has offered each of them a bridge.

world: A frigid world of snowfields and dark pine forest, about two thirds land, with grey seas that freeze over in the long winter. Its winters last nine years, and the forest that survives them is dark red-brown pine. The families sleep through the dark in shared longhouses dug half into the frozen ground, in clusters along the forest edge. Snow cloud covers much of the world for years at a time.
from_space: White snowfields with dark red-brown forest belts and frozen grey seas, under grey snow cloud. At night only a few dull clusters of light show along the forest edge, the longhouses.
moons: None.
people: 400,000 forest people in longhouse clusters along the forest edge, a few dozen families to a longhouse; every spring they count who did not wake.
story: Winter here lasts nine years. Families sleep through the dark in shared longhouses dug half into the frozen ground, and wake each spring to count who did not.

world: A small temperate world of rolling forest, low wooded mountains and long lakes, more land than sea. The craft towns are small and old, red-roofed, grown round their market squares in forest clearings, and nothing in them was laid out by machine.
from_space: Green forest and blue lakes, with flecks of red roofs at the clearings. At night faint warm lights in small clusters.
moons: None.
people: 5 million craftspeople and foresters in small towns and forest villages.
story: A small world that makes everything by hand and refuses machine-made goods. Hand traders sell it fake hand-made stock, and that is how the forgery charges started.

world: A red-brown and gold gas giant with broad, turbulent bands and two large rust storms. Nobody lives in its air. Its big living moon is grass steppe and dark hills with a few small seas, where the nomad clans herd and meet once a year in council under the giant.
from_space: Red-brown and gold bands with two rust storms, and a green-gold moon beside them. At night the moon shows only scattered camp lights, and one bright gathering ground in council season.
moons: Two moons: the big living moon of grass plains, dark hills and small seas, and a cratered rock.
people: 25 million nomads on the living moon, in clan camps that move with the herds.
resources: food, textiles, knives (from the living moon)
story: Nomad clans herd across the grass plains of its big moon and meet once a year in council under the giant. Their vote swings the whole sector, so the Hand and the Collective send envoys every season.

world: A tidally locked world where the wind blows without stopping from the burnt day face to the frozen night face. Between them lies a broad twilight ring of brown-gold savannah and windswept uplands with a few small lakes, and the herding clans graze it in a slow circuit. Their camps are tents and turf houses in the lee of the uplands, and on every ridge stand salvaged turbines, turning in the wind.
from_space: A brown-gold savannah ring between a scorched rust-brown day face and a white night face, with streaks of dust blown along the wind line. Along the night edge of the ring the camps show as a few faint lights.
moons: One moon, cratered grey rock.
people: About 3 million herders in clan camps across the twilight ring, who keep their meat in night-side ice caves and sell turbine power by cable to anyone who docks.
story: The wind from the burnt day side to the frozen night side never stops. Herding clans graze the twilight band, keep their meat in night-side ice caves and sell power from salvaged turbines by cable to anyone who docks. Lode has offered to take over 'maintenance', and the clans know what that means.

world: A hot jungle world of braided rivers and shallow seas, about half land, low-lying, with only a few worn ranges. The canopy is unbroken over the river country, and the Walkouts weld fighter hulls under it, in hangars roofed with netting and leaves where Speculators cannot see. The rain is warm, heavy and a little acid, and it eats bare steel within a week. A Grower commune farms the river islands and feeds the yards.
from_space: Deep green jungle braided with brown rivers and shallow olive seas, under steaming cloud that rarely clears. At night there are almost no lights, and those that show are on the river islands, not at the yards.
moons: One small grey moon, a cratered rock; half-built fighters are towed up to its orbit and finished there by whoever is free.
people: 3 million Walkouts and Grower families: the yard crews in camps under the canopy, the Growers on the river islands.
resources: salvaged steel, fighter hulls, river ore
story: Walkouts weld fighter hulls under the canopy where Speculators cannot see. The rain eats bare steel within a week, so every ship leaves half-built and is finished in orbit by whoever is free.

world: A pale gas giant of broad, soft bands and little weather, with one small amber storm. Nobody lives in its clouds. Its one moon is a small living world of shallow lakes and low hills, stripped bare by Lode and grown back under twenty years of rain into fields and young forest; the Growers' farms sit in its valleys.
from_space: Cream and pale gold bands under a faint warm haze, calm and nearly featureless. Beside the giant the small moon shows green and gold with blue lakes, and by night only a handful of lamp-lit farmsteads.
moons: One living moon of regrown fields, young forest and rain-fed lakes, where the Growers live; its scraped hilltops still show pale where the soil has not come back.
people: About 800 Growers, all on the moon, in farmsteads dug into the valley sides and roofed with turf.
resources: new soil, seed crops, timber, all from the moon
story: Lode stripped the topsoil from this giant's living moon and sold it off-world, and twenty years of rain brought the land back. Eight hundred Growers settled it quietly. Lode's survey still lists the moon as dead, and the Growers mean to keep it that way.

world: A dry temperate steppe world larger than most, with long rivers running through a few green valleys and no open sea. Low hills and grass plains cover most of it, with snow on the few ranges in winter. The herders' camps move with the seasons, so the settlements are loose, shifting and never planned.
from_space: Green-gold steppe with thin river lines and darker green valleys, under light cloud. By night the camps make a wide, faint scatter of fires and lamps, thickest along the rivers.
moons: One moon of cratered grey rock.
people: About 1.5 billion herders, moving camp with the seasons across the steppe.
story: Steppe and rivers, horse herds and a billion people who still move camp with the seasons. Lode has tried to fence the steppe twice; the fences are now fuel.

world: A warm world of ordinary size, a little under half land, folded into deep valleys and steep hills. Rainforest fills the valley floors, grassland covers the uplands, and the ice caps are small. The families farm terraces their ancestors cut into the valley sides, in villages grown along the rivers.
from_space: Green folds and grassy uplands on blue sea, with cloud lying in the valleys at dawn. By night threads of village light along the valley rivers.
moons: None.
people: 70 million valley farmers in river villages, growing coffee and fruit on the old terraces.
story: Deep valleys of rainforest and grassland, settled by families who still farm the terraces their ancestors cut. Lode wants the timber; the valleys want to be left alone and have so far been ignored.
history: Valle Hondo was settled in the Settlement, long before the Republic, by families who cut terraces into its valley sides and grew coffee and fruit on them; some terraces are older than any record on Charter. Under the Republic it sent one member to Parliament and asked for nothing. At the Receivership it signed nothing and was asked for nothing, because a world of deep valleys has no flat ground for a yard, a mine or a landing field. Since R.132 Praevisio has rated logging it a loss every year, and the valley families have lived on that forecast for eighty years. The margin shrinks every year as Lode cuts out the forests of easier worlds, and in R.208 the forecast came within a few points of profit. Lode surveyors have walked the valleys twice since, counting trees. The families fed them, showed them the paths and said nothing. The young have started listening to the Growers who come through to buy seed from the old terraces, which still carry crops Lode's breeders lost generations ago and which can be sown again from their own seed. In R.212 Valle Hondo is still ignored, and everyone in it is waiting for the year the number turns.

world: A cool airless world a little larger than most, grey rock and old craters with no water and no weather. The shield works stand under planned clusters of domes on the plains, each with a proving ground of scorched rock beside it, and the fitting halls run in buried galleries between them.
from_space: Steel grey and dark grey, cratered, with orange furnace dots across the plains where the domes are and scorched black proving grounds beside them. By night the domes glow orange and white.
moons: One moon, a white cratered rock half shot away, its broken side lumpy and pale; the firing batteries stand on what is left of it. No rings.
people: 2.5 billion hands, mostly Contract, under the domes and in the buried fitting halls; every hand works within sight of a proving ground.
story: Mordant's shield works: every Mandate's deflector generators are built here under domes and proof-tested by firing on them from the single white moon, which has been shot half away by the misses.

world: A glacier world a little smaller than most, mostly land under ice, cut by warm volcanic rift valleys where the ground steams. The growers melt the ice walls back a little further every year, and the rifts hold green terraces of vine-coffee and silk vines round lakes of open water. The rift towns are grown, built on the terraces as each new strip of ground comes free.
from_space: White ice cut by long green rifts and patches of open water, with steam over the rifts. By night thin lines of light along the rift floors.
moons: Three moons: a volcanic sulphur moon and two cratered grey rocks.
people: 5 million growers in the rift towns.
story: Hot volcanic rifts under the glaciers grow vine-coffee and silk, and every year the growers melt the ice walls back a little further. They sell to Alma's resorts and are paid in the happiness pill as often as in cash.

world: A small airless rock, dark and deeply cratered, with one pressurised quay along a crater rim. The sealed vault is cut into the rock behind the quay, its corridors lined with sealed niches, and the dockers' pressure halls stand beside it in a tidy row.
from_space: Dark grey rock pitted with craters, lit by a string of dock lamps along one rim. Nothing else shows.
moons: None.
people: 20,000 dockers and their families in the quay's pressure halls.
story: A Runner waystation on an airless rock where crews leave their dead in a sealed vault, so no body can be traced back to a ship. The dockers live in the pressure halls beside it. The vault is nearly full, and nobody has agreed whose dead move out.

world: A wet temperate world a little larger than most, three-fifths land, nearly all of it flat peat bog and reed plain with shallow brown lakes and slow rivers. Low cloud sits on it most of the year. The peat cutters' towns are old and grown along the dikes, the cut bogs round them scarred in long dark strips, and Lode's newer fuel depots stand in planned rows on the bog it now holds.
from_space: Dull brown and olive under low grey cloud, with darker cut strips across the bogs and shallow brown lakes. By night the dike towns show as long lines of light.
moons: Two moons: a grey cratered rock and, further out, a dark ice-rock. No rings.
people: 1 billion peat cutters and their families in dike towns across the marsh; a few million Lode staff run the depots and, in some years, the council.
story: A billion peat cutters live on the marsh, and their council signed a fuel contract with Lode forty years ago to see out a famine. Every renewal gave Lode a little more of the bog, and in some years Lode's managers run the council outright.

world: A temperate world of grain plains a little larger than most, flat and fertile, with blue inland seas and low hills at the edges. The cities stand at the river crossings, crowded and partly planned, and the plains between them are a patchwork of farms to the horizon.
from_space: Green and gold patchwork with blue inland seas and light cloud. By night the cities are bright knots joined by lit roads across the plains.
moons: One grey moon of cratered rock.
people: About 4 billion free citizens, in crowded river cities and farm towns across the plains.
story: A crowded free world of grain plains that has kept the Hand out for a century and a half by paying every toll early, in full, every year. Its treasury is the most nervous office in the galaxy, and a single bad harvest would end its independence.

world: A hot world of black lava plains, rust-red rocky scrub and long fissures where the vents open and close. The settlers cook, heat and power everything from the vents, and every town stands on skids, ready to be dragged to the next vent when the vent-reader says so. A town's old sites stay behind it as rings of scorched ground, so the plains round a busy fissure are dotted with them.
from_space: Black and rust plains with glowing orange seams along the fissures, under a thin smoky haze. At night the seams glow brightest, with a few small town lights clustered close beside them.
moons: None.
people: About 400,000 settlers in a few hundred towns on skids, each with its own vent-reader.
story: Settlers cook, heat and power their towns from volcanic vents, and build every town on skids. The vents move, so every town keeps a vent-reader who says when to pack up, and the vent-readers are right about two times in three.

world: A hot, wet world of jungle under almost constant rain, with warm shallow seas and wide river deltas that flood every season. The plantation houses sit on the rare dry ridges, tapping the jungle for resin and medical compounds, and the contract workers' camps are laid out in rows behind them along the tapping roads. Everything else is canopy, broken only by brown rivers and the paler scars of old clearings growing back.
from_space: Dense dark green under thick white rain cloud, with brown river deltas spilling into dark green-blue seas. At night only the plantation houses and their camps show, small hard clusters of light in a black canopy.
moons: None.
people: 90 million, a third of them contract workers on ten-year terms; the rest are the plantation families, their staff and the river towns that serve them.
story: The plantation houses import workers on ten-year contracts to tap the jungle for medical compounds. Most go home owing more than when they arrived. Alma buys the yield, and in some years it buys the government.

world: A hot, humid world of ordinary size, three-fifths land, all of it swamp forest and jungle cut by brown rivers and standing water. Cloud wraps it nearly every day. Continuity's camps are planned clearings on the river levees joined by mud roads; the exercise grounds are the jungle itself, and burned, churned strips show where the last exercises ran.
from_space: Dark green under steaming, almost unbroken cloud, with brown river lines in the gaps and pale scars of churned ground round the camps. By night the camps are a few square lit clearings.
moons: None.
people: 4 million hands, most of them Tranche recruits in their first months of fatigues; the rest are instructors and terrain staff, failed recruits kept on to play defaulters.
story: Continuity's jungle training ground, where new Tranches learn to fight in heat and rot. The recruits who fail are kept on as terrain staff, playing defaulters in the exercises until the exercises wear them out.

world: A tidally locked world a little smaller than most. Its day face is a vast plain of flare-fused glass, smooth in places and cracked in others, too bright to look at. Its night face is dark rock under frost, where the cut lenses are left to cool. The lensmakers live in the narrow twilight band, in small shuttered stone towns along a line of low brown hills, grown with no plan.
from_space: A dazzling white-gold day face that throws back mirror flashes as the glass catches the light, a thin brown band of twilight and a black night face. At night the twilight towns are a faint dotted line along the edge of the dark.
moons: Three small moons: two cratered grey rocks and one moon of cream frozen plains. None is worked.
people: 200,000 lensmakers and their families in the twilight towns.
story: The day face was fused to glass by a stellar flare a thousand years ago. Lensmakers live in the twilight band, cross into the glare in shuttered crawlers to cut lenses from the plains, and cool the stock on the night side; every lensmaker is half blind by forty.

world: A dusty tan and grey gas giant with ten muted bands, slow even weather and one small dark storm. Continuity's inspection ring circles it above the equator, and below the ring hang the barracks platforms, slung on cables so that they ride in the upper cloud deck. Nothing else is built here.
from_space: Tan, cream and dusty grey bands, circled by a dark steel ring lit end to end with inspection bays. Long cables drop from the ring to grey platforms in the cloud tops. Outside the ring a queue of ships a week long sits in a lit line.
moons: None.
people: 600 million hands, half of them Continuity staff: about 300 million live on the barracks platforms hung in the cloud tops, the rest on the ring itself, in the inspection halls and the Pacifier quarters.
story: Continuity's watch post on the Long Haul approach to Charter. Every ship bound for the capital is stopped and searched at the ring, and the queue in orbit can last a week. Pacifiers sell places in it.
history: Vigilia guards the Long Haul's approach to Charter, and every ship bound for the capital on that stretch of the lane has to pass it. The Republic kept a navy picket here, a few old hulls in orbit. At the Receivership Continuity took the post over and named it for the night watch. In the toll-lane years, the R.50s to R.70s, as Lode beaconed the Long Haul, Continuity built the inspection ring round the giant's equator so that every ship could be stopped, boarded and searched before it reached the Board. The ring was never big enough for the garrison, so the barracks platforms were hung below it on cables and lowered into the cloud tops. Ships wait outside the ring in one long queue, and Pacifiers have sold places in it for as long as anyone remembers; every hauler crew on the Long Haul knows the going rate. Since Praevisio named the defaulter collective in R.201, every search has taken longer. In R.212, with open war, the queue runs past a week, and the price of a place has gone up with it.

world: A cold world a little smaller than most, still mostly white ice sheet over low grey hills, with few mountains. Continuity's warming has opened a belt of grey open water and dark planted forest along the equator, a few hundred kilometres wide and wider every year. The camps are planned blocks in straight rows along the forest edge, each with its sawmill and roll-call yard, and the felled ground behind the cutting line shows as pale strips.
from_space: By day a white globe with a dark green belt at the waist and grey open water threaded through it, thin cloud forming over the thawed belt. At night the camps show as short, evenly spaced rows of light along the forest edge, and nothing shines on the ice.
moons: None.
people: 30 million hands, most of them prisoners serving forest sentences, with a Continuity garrison and camp staff in planned blocks along the forest belt.
story: A labour camp on a cold world Continuity is warming for its timber. Defaulters plant the forest belt and cut it until their sentence is served, and the sentence grows with every tree they miss. The belt widens each year; the sentences have kept pace.

world: A violet gas giant about 48,000 km in radius, banded in lilac and plum with one small wine-red storm. Nobody lives in its clouds. Its glow keeps its two close moons mild, and on both the vineyards climb terraced hillsides above the cellar towns.
from_space: A banded violet giant with a small dark red storm, and close beside it two small living moons of green land and blue sea under thin cloud. At night the cellar towns show as faint gold specks on the moons.
moons: Two living moons, both terraced with vineyards: the larger green and blue, with small seas; the smaller drier and browner, with more terraces than sea. No rings.
people: 28 million vintners and cellar families, all on the two moons.
resources: wine, luxury goods, a little fuel gas skimmed for the cellars' own ships
story: Wine country on two living moons of a violet giant: terraced vineyards and deep cellars that sell bottles to the core and hide Collective cargo in the same crates. Runners pay in good wine; Growers come to learn how old vines survive thin moon soil.

world: A frigid world, 6,000 km in radius, of high snow mountains and dark conifer forest in the valleys between, with cold grey seas covering under a third of it. The passes freeze shut for most of the year. The trapper clans live in log steadings in the forest, far apart.
from_space: White mountains and dark green forest beside grey seas. At night almost no lights.
moons: None.
people: 1 million free trappers and guides, in forest steadings.
story: Trapper clans guide anyone across the frozen passes for pay, no questions asked. That includes Repossessors, which is why runaways here hire two guides and trust neither.

world: A warm, wet, ordinary-sized world, about a third land, where rainforest covers the lowlands, green prairies lie in the rain shadow of high mountains, and snow holds on the highest ranges. Heavy cloud sits over the forest most of the year. Alma's collecting stations are planned compounds of labs and plant houses along the rivers, linked by airstrips rather than roads.
from_space: Lush deep green under thick white cloud, with lighter prairie green and white-capped mountains. By night small regular squares of light along the rivers, each one a collecting station.
moons: None.
people: 50 million hands, mostly plant collectors and lab staff, in Alma's collecting stations along the rivers.
story: Alma's pharmaceutical forest: half the plants in Alma's medicines were first found here, and every plant found since is patented before it is named.

world: A built ring round its star with a cold mountain floor: long snowy ranges, frozen lakes and dark pine valleys, kept wintry by the ring's own weather plant so the snow never fails. Casino towns climb both rim walls in terraces planned to the metre, and the service hands live in the decks behind them.
from_space: A white and grey band round its star, the floor all snowfield and dark mountain shadow. Both rim walls glitter with casino lights, brightest over the night stretches, and the outer hull is cream plate trimmed in pale blush.
moons: None (a built ring round its star).
people: About 6 billion hands, mostly service staff, in the terraced wall towns and the decks behind them; a few million executives are visiting at any time.
story: Alma's pleasure ring, built round its star for executives who want snow on demand. Casino towns climb both rim walls, and six billion service hands staff the tables where executives bet their own employees' Birth Debts. A hand can wake up owing a different supervisor because of a card game.

world: A large, hot swamp world under steady rain, with broad shallow seas and low deltas that never quite dry. There are almost no mountains, and the rivers wander over the flats in braided channels. The old port city on the great delta grew over centuries along the river quays, wharf on wharf; the newer runaway quarters spread out behind it on stilts and fill, with no plan at all.
