from_space: Olive and brown wetland wrapped in thick white rain cloud, the seas a muddy green. At night the delta city glows amber through the cloud, and the river quays show as bright threads.
moons: None. Its twin, Hoogstad, is a separate world one short jump away; convoys for both gather at Muster Rock.
people: 6 billion free citizens, runaways and founding clan families, most of them in the delta city and its stilt quarters.
story: The elder of the twin free ports, run by the Weighhouse, a guild of founding clans. Its law has one line the Hand hates: a Birth Debt dies at the dock. Any hand who lands here is free, so the Board pays the Weighhouse yearly to send runaways back, and it sends most of them.
history: Vrijhaven was settled during the Settlement by river clans who built their port on the great delta, long before the Republic. The founding clans formed the Weighhouse to weigh cargo and settle quarrels on the quays, and when the Republic came the port kept its own harbour law inside it. At the Receivership the Weighhouse paid the receivers' port fees instead of joining the Hand, and the freighters kept coming. In R.31 Alma began billing every birth to the newborn, and within a few years runaways were landing at the quays with their debts behind them. The Weighhouse answered with the one line the Hand hates: a Birth Debt dies at the dock, and any hand who lands here is free. The Board found it cheaper to pay than to fight. For generations it has paid the Weighhouse a yearly sum to send runaways back, and the Weighhouse sends most of them and lets a few stay. Those few and their children built the stilt quarters behind the delta city, and many crossed to the twin world of Hoogstad for work. In R.212 six billion people live here. The Runners need the port more than ever, and the Hand wants it outright.

world: A cold mountain world smaller than most, mostly land: sharp grey-white peaks over deep blue valleys with glacier lakes, and small frozen seas. The air is clear and dry. The post office is dug deep into one massif, and the townsfolk live in grown mountain towns in the valleys below it.
from_space: Grey-white peaks over blue valleys and lakes, with almost no cloud. By night a few small clusters of light in the valleys.
moons: One moon, a cratered grey rock.
people: 2 million mountain townsfolk; the clerks' guild and its families make up about a tenth.
story: A mountain post office, dug deep into the rock against the cold, keeps the galaxy's largest private letter archive. People pay to have letters held unread for decades, and the clerks have never once opened one, not even for the Hand.

world: A hot, dry desert world of bright dune seas, low black basalt ridges and dry wadis. The glassworks sit in the wadis, where the sand is finest, and are worked only at night because the day's heat kills. By day the families sleep in cool rooms dug under the works; by night the furnaces burn.
from_space: Bright yellow dunes with dark ridges and darker smudges of glassworks along the wadis, and hardly any cloud. At night the furnaces glow orange in small clusters along the dry valleys.
moons: None.
people: 3 million glassworkers in family works along the wadis, sleeping by day under the works and working by night.
story: Desert glassworks melt sand into viewport glass, worked at night because the day kills. Middlemen sell it to Mordant at a cut rate, and every Mandate's bridge window may have started here.

world: A hot desert world, 5,700 km in radius, with no open water: sand seas and gravel plains between long dark mountain spines. The oasis towns sit where springs come out at the mountain feet, old and grown, joined by caravan tracks, and at noon they sleep in cellars dug under the palms.
from_space: Sand gold with dark mountain spines and a few dark specks of oasis green. At night tiny scattered oasis lights.
moons: Two moons: a cratered grey rock and a small captured lump. No rings.
people: 850,000 free settlers in the oasis towns, among them a small Ilmar family that keeps the best well on the planet.
story: A desert world of oasis towns where caravans still carry water by beast and the towns sleep through the noon heat in cellars. They take in exiles if they work, and a small Ilmar family runs the best well on the planet.

world: A volcanic world a little smaller than most, with no open sea: charcoal-grey basalt plains, low cones and steaming fissures, dotted with thousands of hot pools coloured turquoise and orange by their minerals. The air is breathable but thick with steam. The towns are domes built over the thermal pools, grown outward from the oldest, and every home is heated free from the ground.
from_space: Charcoal grey dotted with turquoise and orange pools under drifting white steam. By night faint orange seams along the fissures and the warm glow of the domes over the pools.
moons: None.
people: 50 million settlers in domed pool towns run by the spring-keepers' families, a few thousand of whom keep the private pools where Hand executives bathe in secret.
story: A volcanic world of hot springs, where the settlers built domed towns over the thermal pools and heat every home for free. Hand executives come to bathe in secret, because there is nothing like it in Alma's resorts.

world: A pale gas giant banded olive and cream, with one broad calm trading band at mid latitude and quiet weather. The market town hangs under a crown of giant gas bags in that band, a grown jumble of halls, stalls and warehouses round the bell tower. High above, a lit dock ring circles the equator, where the big ships berth.
from_space: Olive and cream bands, with a busy orbit of traders round a lit dock ring at the equator. By night the market is a bright knot of light in the calm band and the dock ring a thin glowing line across the planet.
moons: Two small moons, both dark ice-rock, used by nobody. The dock ring is the only ring.
people: 25 million traders: about 18 million on the floating market and 7 million on the dock ring.
story: A market town hangs under a crown of giant gas bags in the calm band, on the Trunk Line. A bronze bell rung there at dawn sets every price; anyone may ring it once in their life, and the day's prices are theirs.

world: An airless rocky world some 5,200 km in radius, of long grey-brown valleys between worn ranges, with old craters on the high ground. The valleys are roofed end to end with pressure domes and covered ways, and under them run the repair docks, crew hostels and taverns of a lane town that grew into a planet. None of it was planned; each valley grew round its first dock.
from_space: Grey-brown rock with cratered highlands and dark valleys under long roofs. On the night side lit dock towns trace the main valleys in long lines, with ships rising and settling all along them.
moons: Two moons: a grey cratered rock, and a small captured lump where ships wait at anchor for a free dock.
people: 300 million dock hands, hostel keepers, tavern families and passing crews; several of the big dock families are Runners.
resources: ship repair, crew services, spare parts
story: A lane town grown into a planet: repair docks, crew hostels and taverns under pressure roofs along the main valleys. Runner crews refit here openly, because half the docks are owned by Runner families.

world: An airless rocky moonlet barely big enough to be round, heavily cratered, with no water. Everything lives in one pressurised dock sunk into the largest crater: fuel tanks, repair bays and the crews' quarters, laid out in a tight ring.
from_space: A dark grey, pitted speck. At night a single ring of dock lights shows round the big crater, with the running lights of ships waiting their turn.
moons: None.
people: 4,000 dock crews living in the pressurised dock.
story: A refuelling stop between the free ports and the Hand's lanes, its crews living in the pressurised dock. By old custom anyone who fires a weapon here is barred by every captain in the sector, for life, and the custom has held for ninety years.

world: A cool, small shallow-water world with no continents, only thousands of low reed islands scattered over grey-green shallows. Each family runs a fish weir from its own island, a fence of stakes and nets across a channel, and the islands are joined by causeways at low tide. Low cloud and drizzle are the usual weather.
from_space: Grey-green shallows dotted with small olive reed islands under low cloud, with darker water in the channels. At night only faint glints show: lanterns on the weirs.
moons: None.
people: 134,000 people, one family to a reed island, each with its weir and its vote; children join the council at ten.
story: Every family runs a fish weir from its own reed island and has a vote, and children join the council at ten. The fish go out on Collective ships, and the Hand fines the weirs when it can find them.

world: A flat, dry world of endless plains, with almost no hills and no seas. Irrigated grain covers the plains in squares and circles fed by deep wells, and the county towns sit at the crossroads of a grid of farm roads laid out centuries ago. The summers are long and hot, the dust thin, and frost lies only at the poles.
from_space: Gold and pale green squares and circles of grain to the horizon, with one black square burned among them each autumn. At night the county towns light the crossroads in an even grid.
moons: One small white moon of smooth ice, unused.
people: 40 million farmers in county towns across the plains.
story: A flat grain world that has never sold to Lode. Every autumn the farmers burn one full field unharvested, in sight of Lode's buyers, so the buyers know the price of a no.

world: A gas giant about 62,000 km in radius, banded brown and amber, with one slow orange storm. Below the visible cloud lies a dense, heavy layer of gas, and Lode's old refinery decks float on it like ships on a sea, drawing fuel gas up from beneath. The Walkouts hold the decks now, with Dust crews, and run the Collective fleet's fuel from them.
from_space: Brown and amber bands with one slow orange storm. At night the refinery decks show as clusters of warm light in the calm belts.
moons: Two moons: a dark ice-rock, and an industrial moon scarred by old open pits that Lode stopped working. No rings.
people: 2 billion people on the floating refinery decks, many of them former Lode refinery crews, now Walkouts and Dust.
story: Walkouts seized Lode's refineries here, great decks that float on a heavy layer of gas like ships on a sea, and now run the Collective fleet's fuel from them. The decks still carry Lode's stencils, painted over by hand with the names of the crew who took them.

world: A temperate world of ordinary size, a little under half land, spread over several continents with every climate from cold forest to warm dry plain. The farms are old family farms in a green and gold patchwork, and the towns are small and quiet, grown with no plan.
from_space: Blue seas and patchwork green-gold continents, ice at both poles and broken cloud. By night small, evenly scattered town lights.
moons: None.
people: 70 million farmers and townsfolk; the council sits in the largest town, which is not large.
story: A quiet farming world whose council has twice voted to join the Hand, for the clinics and the freighters, and twice been talked out of it by the grandmothers who remember what the clinics cost.

world: A small barren rock, airless and cratered, with no water and no weather. Its broad crater plains are wreck fields: hulls bought from both sides are dragged down and laid out in rows, stripped, sorted and stacked. The family lives in the best of the wrecks, a few old liners and a Bond freighter that still holds its pressure.
from_space: Dark grey rock with a glitter of metal across the crater plains where the wrecks lie, and pale drag scars where hulls have been hauled. At night a few portholes glow in the liners the family lives in.
moons: None.
people: 300 scrap dealers, one family and its hired hands, living in the best of the wrecks.
story: A bare rock with one business: a scrap family that buys wrecks from both sides, lives in the best of them and asks nothing. It also sells wrecks back to their former owners, at a premium, with the bodies removed.

world: A frigid world a little smaller than most, buried under glaciers almost to the equator, with a few frozen sea basins and black rock peaks where mountains break through the ice. Thin cloud, hard bright air. The family's heated galleries are cut into the wall of one great crevasse, beside the wreck.
from_space: Brilliant white, lined with blue crevasse fields and a few dark peaks. At the bottom of one long crevasse the steel-grey back of the crashed Mandate shows from orbit. By night a single short line of gallery lights.
moons: None.
people: About 20,000 ice-haulers, all of them one family by blood or marriage, in heated galleries cut into the glacier beside the wreck.
story: A crevasse on this glacier world holds a Mandate destroyer that crashed forty years ago, nearly intact. The ice-hauling family lives in heated galleries cut beside it, sells salvage rights to both sides and delivers to neither.

world: A cold, dry world of frozen desert, wind-scoured snow plains and worn grey mountains, with almost no open water and very little cloud. The archives lie far below, in vaults cut into the bedrock before the Receivership, and the archivists' towns sit over the vault entrances in sheltered valleys, low buildings half buried against the wind. The towns are old and orderly, laid out by the college round its stairheads.
from_space: White and pale grey, almost featureless, with faint grey mountain lines and a thin ice haze. At night only small, dim clusters of light show over the vault entrances.
moons: None.
people: 73 million, most of them archivists, copyists and their families, in towns over the vaults governed by the archivists' college.
story: Under its frozen desert lie archives older than the Receivership, including, it is said, the court's original ruling. The Board offers to buy the archives every decade. The archivists answer every decade, in writing, that they are not for sale.

world: A temperate world a little smaller than most, under half of it land, all low, flat country: reed swamps, wet meadows and dark forest, with shallow grey-green seas and small ice caps. It rains most days. The fishing villages are tiny and grown, a few houses on stilts at the edge of the reeds, and there are no roads at all.
from_space: Green land laced with silver wetlands and pools under soft grey cloud. By night it is dark; the villages are too small and too few to show.
moons: Two moons: a small cratered grey rock and a larger moon of smooth white ice.
people: 8,000 villagers in a few dozen fishing villages; nobody else lives here.
story: A few fishing villages in the reed swamps who have never met a Hand official. Their only outside visitor is a Collective midwife, twice a year.

world: An airless rocky world, smaller than most, whose largest continent is one tungsten mine: terraced pits kilometres deep, spoil heaps and haul roads, with grey dust over everything. The pit towns are pressurised domes and tunnels on the pit rims, built by Lode in identical planned blocks, and the dust gets into all of them. Old craters show only where the mine has not reached.
from_space: Dull brown rock with wide grey pit scars over most of one face. At night the pit towns ring each pit with lights, and haul-road lamps run between them.
moons: None. The ore haulers work a rock field farther out in the system, where the pit children learn to fly feeder skiffs.
people: 20 million hands, mostly Indentured miners and their families in pressurised pit towns.
story: A tungsten mine the size of a continent, worked from pressurised pit towns on a bare rock. Dust-lung is so common that Lode's clinic bills it as a pre-existing condition, back-dated to birth.
history: The Republic's surveyors charted Wolfram II as an airless rock with tungsten under it and left it alone, too far out to pay. After the Receivership Lode opened the first pits, and by the R.100s the mine covered a continent, worked by Indentured crews from pressurised pit towns on the rims. The dust is the place. It gets through seals and into lungs, and dust-lung is so common that Lode's clinic bills it as a pre-existing condition, back-dated to birth. Children start young on the ore haulers, sorting rock in low-gravity holds, and the pit rosters list them by the last two digits of their Hand numbers. In R.178 a girl was born here whose digits were 41. She went on the haulers at eight, and by twelve she was flying feeder skiffs through the rock field, because the adult pilots were dead or coughing. In R.197, at nineteen, she stole a skiff and ran. When she went dry at a Dust hold-out she kept the number as her name, so that Praevisio would have to print it on every loss report. Today Forty-One is the only Collective pilot with a threat file of her own, and the file is mostly blank. In R.212 Wolfram II still ships tungsten for the Hand's hulls, and the rosters still list children by two digits.

world: A calm gas giant about 58,000 km in radius, with broad soft bands of pale lemon and grey and only one small storm. Nobody lives in its clouds. The free farmers live on its big temperate moon, a world of rolling farmland, small seas and thin cloud, where Lode's grain silos stand at every rail junction.
from_space: Pale lemon and grey bands with one small amber storm. Close beside it the farming moon shows green and gold fields under thin white cloud, with a scatter of town lights at night.
moons: Two moons: the big farming moon, a living world of green and gold farmland and small blue seas under thin cloud; and a small cratered grey rock. No rings.
people: 210 million free farmers, all on the farming moon, in farm towns along its rail lines.
story: A quiet farm moon where Lode built every grain silo and owns them all. The farmers are free to sell to anyone else, as long as they don't mind watching the crop rot in the fields.

world: A snow world a little smaller than most, with cold grey seas over more than half of it and sea ice reaching well toward the equator. The land is low snow-covered tundra and long snow beaches, with a few ranges of worn hills. The hunters live in grown turf villages banked with snow along the beaches and cut holes for ice-fish in the sea ice offshore.
from_space: White land and white sea ice, with grey-blue open water in a band near the equator, under thin cloud. By night a few faint lights along the beaches.
moons: One moon, a grey cratered rock.
people: 3 million villagers in snow-banked turf villages along the beaches; their children are born at home.
story: Snow beaches where hunters cut ice-fish from holes in the sea ice and live in snow-banked turf villages. The village elders have refused Hand clinics three times, and their children are born at home.

world: A brassy gas giant banded bronze, copper and pale gold, with lively turbulence and one dark orange storm. The mint towns hang under their own balloons in the breathable layer, each an old grown town of smelters, vaults and counting houses, scattered through the calm zones of both hemispheres.
from_space: Bronze and copper bands with an orange storm, and two moons beside it. By night dozens of warm, smoky-gold clusters of light, one under each balloon.
moons: Two moons: first a mined moon of open pits and smelter towns, where the coin metal is dug; then a cratered grey rock.
people: 5 billion settlers: about 4.2 billion in the balloon towns and 800 million on the mine moon.
story: A gas giant that mints the last hard coins in the galaxy from metal dug on its moon, worth what the metal is worth and owed by nobody. Each mint town hangs under its own balloon. The Hand hates money that isn't debt, and the vaults are on every Board agenda.

world: A rugged frozen world larger than most, almost all land, its mountains high and sharp, with only a few ice-locked inland seas. The clans' fortress towns are cut into the walls of the snowbound valleys, terraced and walled, each valley a warlord's holding. Glaciers fill the high passes, and storms pile snow in the valleys through the long winter. Nothing here was planned; every town grew round its walls.
from_space: Grey-brown peaks over snowbound white valleys, with broad ice caps and patchy cloud. At night the fortress towns glow in the valley floors in separate clusters, with dark mountain between each one.
moons: One grey moon, a cratered rock with nothing on it.
people: 900 million mountain clansfolk in fortress towns cut into the valley walls, split between nine warlords; most adults have served in a war band.
story: Nine mountain warlords have been at war for forty years from fortress towns cut into the snowbound valleys. Continuity sells guns to all nine and counts on the war never ending.
